Jaydee Canvot was guilty of losing possession when Morgan Gibbs-White picked out the unmarked Ndoye and Benítez tipped over before Daniel Muñoz was inches away from scoring against his former club.

But the momentum shifted firmly towards the hosts thanks to a miraculous save from Benítez – deputising for the injured Dean Henderson – that denied Delap from three yards out after Gibbs-White’s shot rebound off the crossbar. “Walter made a save with a lot of bravery,” said Sage, who refused the opportunity to gloat about beating Glasner. “It’s not about revenge,” he insisted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Delap spurned another golden opportunity with his head and Forest were made to pay just before the break when Kamada scrambled home inside the six-yard area after Jørgen Strand Larsen’s pass deflected straight into his path. Suddenly Palace found their belief. Tyrick Mitchell’s volley was tipped over and from the resulting corner Lerma leapt highest and the ball squirmed through the legs of Matz Sels and just over the line. Replays suggested that Lerma’s effort grazed the arm of team-mate Khalaili on its way in, but VAR let the matter go.

One characteristic Sage has inherited is his team’s difficulty in defending set pieces and Palace were lucky to escape when a header from Gibbs-White at the start of the second half was deflected on to the post by Mitchell. Forest looked at sixes and sevens at the other end when Lerma again caused chaos from a corner but they scrambled the ball away.

There was no such reprieve a few minutes later when Quinten Timber’s pass was diverted into the path of Strand Larsen and Pino made no mistake with the rebound. The Spain forward then turned provider but Strand Larsen could not find a way past Sels. That didn’t stop the Palace fans from gleefully asking Glasner what the score was. Ndoye and Neco Williams had chances to make things interesting late on but Forest – and Glasner – had been humbled by then.

Sports.title: Mohamed Belloumi grabs point for Hull in seesaw draw with Everton
Sports.content:
Hull retained their unbeaten home record since returning to the Premier League with an entertaining draw against Everton at the MKM Stadium.

Brennan Johnson found the net in the 34th minute but was denied a first Premier League goal for Everton following a video assistant referee check, leaving the sides to go in goalless at the break. The hosts wasted little time after the interval, however, as Joe Gelhardt opened the scoring in the 48th minute following an error by Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised for Everton seven minutes later, and Thierno Barry, who had squandered plenty of earlier chances, then put the visitors ahead midway through the second period. Hull responded swiftly, though, with the substitute Mohamed Belloumi pulling the home team level in the 74th minute.

The Tigers have returned to the top flight with an unexpected bang, tasting defeat for the first time in their final fixture before the international break at Newcastle. They were slow off the mark in the early exchanges here, but eventually produced a forward burst of play that saw both Oli McBurnie and then Lewie Coyle threaten before being thwarted.

Gelhardt caused danger with a run down the right in the 22nd minute but his shot was comfortably collected by Jordan Pickford. Matt Crooks got his head to a corner 10 minutes later, but James Tarkowski cleared and play sped to the opposite end.

Barry unleashed a shot that was gathered by Konstantinos Tzolakis, but the ball rolled from his hands and was fired in by Johnson for what appeared to be the opener 11 minutes before half-time. But, after a lengthy VAR check, the winger was ruled offside. Gelhardt and Nobel Mendy then went close to easing the nerves of home fans with near-misses before half-time.

The hosts did not have to wait long for the opener after the break though. Sorba Thomas capitalised on a mistake from Maitland-Niles and fed Gelhardt, who coolly nudged the ball beyond Pickford in the 48th minute.

The Everton response was fairly rapid, however, and Maitland-Niles atoned for his slip-up by finding Dewsbury-Hall, who headed home in the 55th minute.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall heads home to make it 1-1. Photograph: Lee Parker/CameraSport/Getty Images

Barry, who had much to ponder after missing two earlier chances, then redeemed himself when he pounced to lash beyond Tzolakis to put the visitors ahead for the first time in the match.

But Hull, who had made a handful of changes, were not behind for long as the substitutes Elliot Stroud and Belloumi linked up and the latter sent a left-footed shot past Pickford in the 74th minute to secure a point for the Tigers.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

David Moyes felt his Everton squad completely underperformed. Change is afoot at the club after it was announced earlier in the week they would be put up for sale, but their manager was in no mood for excuses after the draw.

He said: “I’m really disappointed that we didn’t come away with three points, I couldn’t see them getting a goal when we went 2-1 up – I thought if anything we would go on and finish it. It looked really unlike us, the way we gave the goals away today, it was very, very poor.

“Hull have had some great results here, against Manchester United and Villa, they’re not easy to beat and they weren’t [today] but I thought we should have gone on and won the game comfortably.

“The overall performance from everyone was so far below our level, way below where we should be. I’m not giving the players any room for excuses because of what’s going on, whether that be the transfer window or that be ownership.”

Sports.title: European football: Freiburg move top of Bundesliga while Isco keeps Betis flying high
Sports.content:
Ten-man Freiburg scored an 85th-minute winner ⁠through Keisuke Goto to snatch a 2-1 home victory over ⁠Schalke 04 ⁠on ​Sunday and move top of the Bundesliga.

Freiburg, who had ⁠already made a club-record start with 10 points from their opening ⁠four matches, climbed to 13 points, ​ahead of Borussia ‌Dortmund on ‌goal difference. The champions, Bayern Munich, who drew 2-2 ‌against Augsburg on Saturday, are third on 11.

With Freiburg in control, Maximilian Eggestein put the hosts in front after 10 minutes, but Schalke hit ‌back through Adrian Gantenbein on the half-hour. Freiburg were reduced to ​10 men when Yuito Suzuki received a second yellow card in the 64th minute, seemingly handing Schalke the initiative.

But ⁠the visitors were far too passive and ​toothless ​in attack to ​make the extra man count ​and Freiburg ‌punished them ​five ​minutes before the end with the Japan international Goto snatching the winner with a glancing header.

Borussia Mönchengladbach remained rock bottom of the Bundesliga after a 2-1 defeat to local rivals Cologne on Sunday, in a match overshadowed by ugly scenes on the terraces.

The game was suspended for several minutes and riot police surrounded the away block after Gladbach fans appeared to fire fireworks into the home sections after Said El Mala’s superb second-half winner. That maintained pointless Gladbach’s miserable start to the season as the new coach, Alexander Blessin, failed to prevent the club falling to their fifth defeat in as many games.

The Real Betis playmaker Isco scored in each half ⁠as his side breezed to a 5-2 home win over Osasuna on ⁠Sunday that lifts ⁠them ​to third place in La Liga, five points behind the leaders, Barcelona, and one ahead ⁠of Real Madrid.

Isco fired home from the penalty spot in the 10th minute to ⁠open the scoring, and Abde Ezzalzouli added a second ​before the break after ‌Betis won the ‌ball high up the pitch and countered quickly.

Betis ‌looked to be set for a comfortable afternoon when Diego Llorente added a third three minutes after half-time, but two quick goals for the visitors from Ante Budimir and Raúl García reduced the ‌deficit to 3-2 in the 56th minute.

However, Isco eased their nerves again when he ​snapped up a loose ball in the box and rifled it home, and José Antonio Morante came off the bench in the 90th minute before scoring deep ⁠into stoppage time to leave Betis on 19 ​points after ​eight games.

Earlier on ​Sunday, Real Sociedad held off a spirited ​comeback from ‌Deportivo La Coruña ​to ​emerge with a 3-2 win at home, while struggling Elche grabbed a much-needed point by holding visitors Celta Vigo to a scoreless draw.

Lazio moved level on points with Inter at the top of Serie A with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday as 10-man Roma played out the first goalless draw of the Italian season at Como.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Nuno Tavares gives Lazio an early lead. Photograph: Riccardo Antimiani/EPA

Under Gennaro Gattuso, who has bounced back after his failure in charge of the Italian national side that missed out on the 2026 World Cup, Lazio continued their strong start to the season. Still unbeaten, the Roman side secured a fifth victory in six matches to pull level on 16 points with Inter, who beat Parma 3-0 at San Siro on Saturday.

Nuno Tavares gave Lazio a third-minute lead and Gustav Isaksen doubled it midway through the first half. Monza had Lorenzo Lucchesi sent off on 35 minutes for hauling down Tijjani Noslin as he broke through on goal, but the 16th-placed visitors rattled Lazio after the break, pulling a goal back and coming close to equalising before conceding a third goal in the closing stages.

Roma left Como frustrated. The dismissal of league top scorer Donyell Malen for a dangerous tackle early in the second half forced them to scale back their ambitions. Neither team could find the breakthrough in a clash between two sides widely regarded as dark horses for the title, leaving Inter and Lazio two points clear of Roma after their respective wins over Parma and Monza.

Bologna picked up their first win of the season by beating Lecce 2-1. Milan remain unbeaten in Serie A after drawing 1-1 with Sassuolo. Adrien Rabiot’s opener was cancelled out by Cas Odenthal as Milan settled for their third draw of the campaign and stay fifth in the table. Juventus are one point behind Milan after an 81st minute equaliser from Randal Kolo Muani salvaged a 1-1 draw with fourth-placed Cagliari.

Marseille put an end to their four-game losing run in Ligue 1 as Amine Harit and Himad Abdelli scored in a 2-0 win at Troyes. Struggling Marseille began the weekend in the relegation zone after suffering five losses in a row in all competitions, but a pair of second-half goals lifted them to 13th place.

Harit steered in a cross from Emerson Palmieri shortly after half-time before Abdelli converted a late penalty as Marseille avoided matching their worst losing streak over the past 40 years. Troyes had gone close to an equaliser just before Abdelli made the points safe for Marseille, but Renaud Ripart’s stoppage-time volley crashed against the post.

Rennes moved up to third earlier in the day with a 4-1 win against Auxerre, while Nice came from behind to beat Strasbourg 2-1.

Sports.title: Joy for Eckert as 10-man Southampton edge out Portsmouth in feisty derby
Sports.content:
At the full-time whistle in the south coast derby, Tonda Eckert thrust his arms out wide and roared into the sky with the rest of the Southampton supporters. It had been a tense 90 minutes after a tense few months, but finally the young German coach could let it all out. At the end of a week where he found out that he will face no immediate ban for his part in the Spygate scandal that rocked the Championship last season, he helped deliver Southampton’s first home win over Portsmouth for 22 years.

Southampton played more than half of a fiercely contested game with 10 men after Cameron Bragg was sent off for a second yellow card on 44 minutes and Eckert was keen to divert credit elsewhere at full time. “I think that one today belongs to the players,” he said. “If you go a man down there’s not so much you can do as a manager outside of trying to give a structure that helps. It’s the players that dig out games like this.”

There was widespread surprise at the leniency of the punishment that allowed Eckert to take his seat in the dugout for the derby. After Southampton admitted to spying on three opponents last season, the 33-year-old was handed a six-week ban, suspended until the end of the 2027-28 campaign, and a £28,000 fine for misconduct.

An FA independent disciplinary commission noted Eckert’s “genuine contrition” at what had happened. At Southampton, there is a sense that their expulsion from the playoffs in May and subsequent four-point deduction was punishment enough, and Eckert is keen to move on from a period of uncertainty that he admitted this week had changed his life.

This win was evidence of a club sticking together. James Bree was the author of the winning goal, turning the ball home after 20 minutes, but the pattern of the game shifted with Bragg’s dismissal. Southampton, united and resolute, held on to move into the top half – they would be third without the points deduction – with Eckert now able to contemplate another promotion push.

View image in fullscreen Southampton’s James Bree coolly opens the scoring, his goal turning out to be the winner. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Portsmouth were as usual given a pre-match police escort to St Mary’s and their full-back Jayden Meghoma, who made his professional debut for Southampton as a 17-year-old, was a magnet for Saints ire. He was a threat down the left, firing wide at the near post in a promising opening, but he lost Bree for the goal. Finn Azaz was given too much space in midfield and clipped a ball in behind a static Meghoma for Bree, forward from right-back, to guide a left-footed finish into the far corner.

Ebou Adams, who scored Portsmouth’s equaliser in a 1-1 draw in this fixture in January, was a central figure early on. He twice picked Bragg’s pocket in the Southampton half and drew yellow cards on both occasions. Bragg was consoled by his teammates after seeing red for an instinctive tug of Adams’s shirt after being caught on the ball.

The decision to start Bragg in a holding midfield role had backfired. “It will be a learning [curve] for him, but I asked him to be brave,” Eckert said. “I asked him to get on the ball and he does just that. I’ll take that on me, then.”

View image in fullscreen Cam Bragg is consoled as he walks off the pitch. Photograph: Robin Jones/Getty Images

Colby Bishop, whose header was well saved by Daniel Peretz, and Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, who drilled a shot just wide, went close to equalising before Eckert could try to plug the gaps at half-time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The game was just as frantic after the break. Azaz was perhaps lucky not to be sent off for a wild lunge on Adams. When Bree was treated for a battle scar around his eye, Eckert held council with his remaining midfielders James Ward-Prowse and Flynn Downes as Pompey continued to knock on the door. The substitute Adrian Segecic was drifting into spaces and had fizzed a couple of low efforts wide in the minutes before, while the right-back Zak Swanson saw his cut-back cleared by Jack Stephens from under the Southampton crossbar.

View image in fullscreen Tempers fray at St Mary’s but the hosts held on for victory. Photograph: Warren Little/Getty Images

“It was a different game after the red card,” said the Portsmouth head coach, John Mousinho. “But for the amount of pressure that we had in the second half, the amount of opportunities we had, to not put the ball in the back of the net – we’re devastated.”

While Eckert gradually cut back his side’s attacking presence, Mousinho emptied his bench in an attempt to find a way through a Southampton defence marshalled by Stephens and Keven Schlotterbeck, who laid their bodies on the line more than once in front of Peretz. Their clean sheet was a priceless end to a week where their manager was given something of a clean slate.

Sports.title: Jesse Lingard gets four-time Champions League winner as new manager at Brazilian club
Sports.content:
Jesse Lingard gets four-time Champions League winner as new manager at Brazilian club

Clarence Seedorf has landed his first managerial job in seven years by becoming the new head coach at Corinthians.

Seedorf, who won four Champions League titles at Ajax, Real Madrid and AC Milan, is eyed as one of football's greatest-ever midfielders.



2 Seedorf has returned to management by taking the head coach role at Corinthians, seven years after his last job Credit: Getty

He also won 87 caps for the Netherlands national team and played at the 1998 World Cup.

After his retirement in 2014, Seedorf managed Milan, Shenzhen FC and Deportivo La Coruna.

A spell at Cameroon followed but ended in 2019, with Brazilian outfit Corinthians the 50-year-old's next challenge.



Seedorf has signed a deal with the club until the end of next year.

Corinthians have slipped to 17th in the 2026 Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A table and are now in the relegation zone following a heavy defeat to league leaders Palmeiras on Sunday evening.

However, they won the Supercopa do Brasil earlier in the year with a 2-0 win over Flamengo.



Lingard set for new Corinthians manager

Many fans of English football will recognise one of the players in Jesse Lingard, who signed for the club in March.

The former Manchester United and West Ham United star moved to Brazil after terminating his contract with FC Seoul in South Korea.



Lingard was an FA Cup, League Cup and Europa League winner with United, and made 182 appearances in the Premier League.

Now at Corinthians, the 33-year-old attacking midfielder has scored two goals and assisted one other in 29 outings.

2 Lingard is a regular for Corinthians, who are the ninth club of his playing career Credit: Getty

His first goal for the club, their winner against Barra in the Copa do Brasil, meant he became the only English scorer in the competition.



Lingard then found the target in a 2-0 Copa Libertadores victory over Penarol.

Corinthians last played on Wednesday night but were beaten 2-1 by Internacional in the league, with Lingard an unused substitute.

Now with Seedorf in charge, the seven-time Brazilian champions will hope to salvage their season before it ends in December.

"Taking on this challenge is an honour, but also a huge responsibility," their new head coach said upon his arrival.



"I am here to give my all and build a team that fights for every ball, every minute, every victory."

Sports.title: Police forced to intervene as fans clash minutes after Liverpool vs Man City in chaotic scenes
Sports.content:
Police forced to intervene as fans clash minutes after Liverpool vs Man City in chaotic scenes

Police needed to quell tensions between Liverpool and Manchester City supporters after their Premier League clash.

Goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki handed a 3-0 win to City at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

2 There was a heavy police presence at Anfield, and officers needed to separate fans after the full-time whistle Credit: Getty

The match was highly charged before kick-off after an independent commission ruled that City are guilty on all counts of financial rule breaches in the Premier League from the 2009/10 season to 2017/18.

An appeal has been lodged by the club, who claim they are innocent and have a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' to hand.

'Cheats' and 'Guilty 114' could be seen on banners outside the stadium as City faced a hostile reception at the home of their rivals, Liverpool.

There was fortunately little, if any, disorder between the two sets of fans before and during the match.

Liverpool and City fans clash

However, as reported by the Manchester Evening News, police had to intervene after the full-time whistle.

In a video posted by Chris Slater on X, fans could be seen scuffling as they walked out of the stadium.

A small group of City supporters were swiftly surrounded by officers as tensions grew.

One Liverpool fan could be seen being pepper-sprayed, but the police managed to prevent any physical altercations between supporters.

Some of the Reds faithful were heard shouting 'F****** cheats' and 'Cheating b*******' to their rivals.

It appears as though there was no further trouble as fans continued to head home.

2 City brushed off the outside noise of their guilty verdict to win at Liverpool Credit: Getty

On the pitch, City's goals were all scored after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for Liverpool by picking up a second yellow card.

City stay top of the Premier League with six wins from six, and three points clear of holders Arsenal.

talkSPORT reported afterwards that the club did not allow manager Enzo Maresca to speak to radio stations.

This is a breach of broadcasting rules, and City did not explain why they made their decision.

Now that City have appealed, there will be a further wait to hear about the sanctions they face for their charges.

An appeal hearing is set to be held in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: Man City breach another Premier League rule immediately after victory against Liverpool
Sports.content:
Manchester City fell foul of Premier League broadcasting rules after their victory against Liverpool on Sunday.

City were 3-0 winners in their first match since being found guilty on all charges of financial rule breaks by an independent commission.

3 City broke Premier League rules by not allowing Maresca to speak to talkSPORT or other radio broadcasters Credit: Getty

The club, who have appealed, were adjudged to have artificially inflated their revenue by £900million via 'sham' contracts from the 2009/10 season to 2017/18.

Victory at Anfield is their sixth from as many games this season and keeps them top of the Premier League table.

City breach Premier League rule with Maresca decision

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook was at Anfield for the match and spoke to Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola afterwards.

However, when looking to interview City manager Enzo Maresca, the club refused to allow him to speak to radio stations.

This is a breach of rule K.207 in the Premier League handbook for the 2026/27 season.

"Each Club participating in a League Match must ensure that each Radio Broadcaster that has the right to the Radio Transmission of that League Match is permitted to interview (a) at least one Player who featured prominently in the League Match and (b) the Manager, following the League Match," it states.

City did not offer an explanation as to why Maresca was not allowed to speak to talkSPORT.

Maresca, however, did speak to television broadcaster Sky Sports, as well as the rest of the media during his post-match press conference.

Blocking out the noise for three points

Banners that read 'Cheats' and 'Guilty 114' were seen outside and inside Anfield for the heated league clash following the verdict.

Liverpool fans booed the City players as they walked out on the pitch as they and the rest of English football await the appeal's outcome.

3 City were at their very best despite the hostile reception and remain top of the table Credit: Getty

However, City had the last laugh as they left Merseyside with all three points thanks to a top performance.

Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for Liverpool in the 62nd minute as he picked up a second yellow card.

Moments later, Erling Haaland fired City ahead with a well-taken half-volley to spark jubilation from their travelling supporters.

Jeremy Doku then scored the best of the lot when he curled into the top corner before Rayan Cherki wrapped up the scoring late on.

City have scored 16 goals, conceded five and kept three clean sheets so far this season.

They are three points ahead of reigning champions Arsenal and could well be favourites for the title.

3 City could face serious sanctions for their rule breaches but, for now, they are loving life in the Premier League Credit: Getty

However, talkSPORT pundit Scott Minto has warned the Premier League of what could happen if City were to lift the trophy in May.

"I think it could be one of the biggest shambles in Premier League history, if they're then found to be guilty," he said. "But if you are Manchester City, that's the aim, isn't it?

"To kick the can down the road, to keep on asking the Premier League, to then go back to the clubs, to keep on spending the legal battles with it.

"Do they take it to the High Court? Do the High Court accept it? How long will that take, even if they don't? And therefore it could go beyond this season, for sure."

talkSPORT understands Premier League clubs have planned to write to chief executive Richard Masters stressing the importance of City's case, inclusive of appeals.

They want it resolved this season, with any sanctions that are subject to appeal being in play this campaign and as soon as reasonably possible.

Sports.title: National League side make unprecedented decision after losing boss to EFL club
Sports.content:
Forest Green Rovers owner Dale Vince has sensationally revealed that his club are going to operate without a manager or head coach.

The National League side were dealt a huge blow earlier this month when boss Robbie Savage departed to take over at Peterborough.

3 Robbie Savage enjoyed a perfect start to his Peterborough tenure Credit: Getty

The 51-year-old enjoyed a picture-perfect start to his first managerial role in the EFL with a 3-1 away win at Leicester City on Saturday.

talkSPORT understands the latest Foxes defeat has left much-maligned manager Russell Martin’s future in serious danger.

However, should Leicester pull the trigger, they won't be facing any competition for a new boss from Savage's former side, Forest Green.

That is because the world's first fully vegan club are not actively looking for the Welshman's replacement.

After Savage's exit, coaching trio Jonathan Gould, Josh Bowen and Yan Klukowski have been taking charge of the team.

Forest Green not looking for new manager

Vince told BBC Radio Gloucestershire: “We’re in a situation where we’re not in a hurry. We’re not actually having any conversations.

“We haven’t spoken to anybody about the role. We like where we are; we’re going to see how it goes — maybe for a few games, maybe for a month.

“The coaching team have been doing the heavy lifting anyway; they know the team inside out.

“I think the three of them make very balanced, rational decisions.

3 Dale Vince claimed there is no manager vacancy at the club Credit: Getty

“We aren’t talking to anybody," Forest Green chairman and owner Vince continued. "I promise you we haven’t had a single conversation.

“All of the speculation within the media is just speculation. Nobody is in the frame; nobody is connected to the job.

“At the moment, there is no vacancy.”

Forest Green, who dropped out of the Football League two years ago following successive relegations, are currently 16th in the fifth tier.

The club, who finished seventh last term in Savage’s sole season in charge, suffered a 4-2 defeat at home to Hartlepool on Saturday.

Forest Green are now without a win in five matches - having failed to win in each of the matches since Savage stepped away from his post.

3 Forest Green have won just four of 12 games this season and are without a win in their last five Credit: Getty

“I don’t feel an urgency,” Vince added.

“If you look at how we played last Tuesday (the 1-1 draw with Wealdstone), we played really well; we could have nicked it.

“There’s no drama. Without Robbie, I think we’re fine without a manager.

“The thing I see in football is teams are led by big-ego managers, and I’m not sure that they always make the best decisions. We’re going to try something different to see if we can get a more balanced outcome, decision-making-wise. We’re going to run without the big-ego manager for a little while and see what happens.

“We’ve got a team of coaches that, between them, have an awful lot of experience — Premier League, Championship. We think between them they’ve probably got it. But also they know the players and the club inside out.

“I think we won’t miss the manager, but let’s see. We’re just focused on being the best we can be. With this change imposed upon us, we’re trying to see if we can make something quite good out of it.”

Sports.title: ‘Sham’ club Man City awaiting sanction but Ryan Gravenberch’s swift punishment settles Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
How ironic that after the events of the last three weeks, it was ‘sham’ club Manchester City who benefitted from their opponents being given a swift punishment.

City players were taunted by taunts of ‘cheats’ before, during and after the game as they took to the field for the first time since being found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules.



4 Man City stars gleefully celebrated victory at full-time Credit: Getty

However, it was Ryan Gravenberch’s contentious 62nd-minute red card that tilted the balance of arguably the most hyped match in Premier League history in their favour.

City’s team coach took a back route into the stadium to avoid the baying crowd waiting to greet them on the Anfield Road.

Merchandise stalls were having a field day selling flags emblazoned with the word ‘GUILTY’ and Oasis-themed tee-shirts reading ‘(What’s the story) tainted glory.'



City fans arrived armed with inflatable bananas, a throwback to a 1980s Maine Road terrace tradition when they were relegated to the second tier.

They also chanted owner Sheikh Mansour’s name and ‘cheating bastards. We know what we are.’



As the home supporters belted out their traditional pre-match ‘You’ll never walk alone’ anthem, many in the away end turned their backs and broke into a spontaneous Poznan.

The cauldron-like atmosphere certainly seemed to inspire Liverpool’s players in the early stages, while Marc Guehi in particular looked rattled.



The England defender gave away a needless free-kick after being caught in possession by Victor Munoz before later taking the ball out of the gloves of his own goalkeeper from a Milos Kerkez cross.

A heated 11th-minute clash between City’s £116m man Elliot Anderson and Alexis Mac Allister prompted a pantomime melee involving players from both teams and more cries of ‘cheat, cheat, cheat’ from the stands.

That was really where the first half drama ended, and neither goalkeeper was seriously tested as the action on the pitch failed to live up to the build-up off it.

4 City were braced for a hostile reception against Liverpool due to their guilty verdict Credit: Getty



4 The Anfield crowd made its feelings clear at kick-off Credit: Getty

Anderson’s reaction to a heavy challenge from Gravenberch two minutes into the second, leading to a booking for the Dutchman, half cranked up the noise levels once more.

Nico O’Reilly having his name taken by referee Chris Kavanagh for a late tackle on Munoz to pick up City’s first yellow card prompted a roar from the Reds faithful as loud as if a goal had been scored.

The academy product was another player who showed signs of being knocked off his stride by the furore surrounding City’s guilty verdict.



Haaland had not had a sniff of goal until Antoine Semenyo picked the pocket of Milos Kerkez and played in the striking Viking, but he rolled his shot wide with only Alisson to beat.

The Norwegian goal machine made amends moments later by smashing a left-foot half-volley into the far corner after Jeremy Doku’s cross had been deflected into his path.

4 Gravenberch's red card was the turning point in the match Credit: Getty

Feeling of injustice among Man City critics

Haaland’s opener came just three minutes after Gravenberch had been given his marching orders for an innocuous challenge on super sub Doku.



Doku crowned an outstanding cameo off the bench three minutes later by cutting in from the left and curling an unstoppable right-foot shot into the top corner.

Rayan Cherki left Anfield in stunned silence with a sublime piece of footwork to leave Alisson on his backside before slotting into the far corner to seal a resounding 3-0 win.

The fact that City’s three goalscorers cost a combined £137m will only add to the feeling of injustice among their critics. Not that there were many Liverpool fans left to boo them come full-time.

Maybe cheats do prosper...

Sports.title: Man City substitute star earns 9/10 in player ratings as Citizens smash ten-man Liverpool
Sports.content:
Manchester City ignored the outside noise and shone to stay top of the Premier League with a convincing win at Liverpool.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki all scored in a second-half rout as City won 3-0 in their first match since being found guilty on all charges of financial rule breaches in the Premier League.



3 Financial charges loom over City, but their quality on the pitch guided them to a massive win at Liverpool Credit: Getty

In their bid to provide a hostile atmosphere, some Liverpool fans at Anfield displayed banners that called their opponents 'Cheats' amid the guilty verdict.

However, they watched their side go down to ten men on 62 minutes as Ryan Gravenberch was sent off, after which they simply collapsed.

Haaland smashed in on the half-volley before Doku excellently curled into the top corner as the visitors found their groove on Merseyside.



Cherki then wrapped up the points with a composed finish to ensure City maintain their 100 per cent record in the league after six matches.

They are three points clear of reigning champions Arsenal and the second-highest scorers in the league on 16, as Brighton lead with 18.



City star earns 9/10 off the bench

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook assessed each of the City's players' performances and rated them at full-time.

Doku, who was brought on for Iliman Ndiaye early in the second half, earned the best score of all as he was handed a 9/10.



His fellow goalscorers Haaland and Cherki were given 7/10 and 8/10 respectively, whilst Ruben Dias was also graded with the latter.

Alex Crook's Man City player ratings vs Liverpool Gianluigi Donnarumma - 7

Matheus Nunes - 7

Ruben Dias - 8

Marc Guehi - 5

Nico O’Reilly - 5

Elliot Anderson - 6

Enzo Fernandez - 7

Antoine Semenyo - 7

Rayan Cherki - 8

Iliman Ndiaye - 5

Erling Haaland - 7 Subs: Josko Gvardiol - 6

Jeremy Doku - 9

Allan - 6

Ayyoub Bouaddi - 6

Speaking to Sky Sports after, Haaland said: "Every single person part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time.

"It was tough, it was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone.

3 Doku was the standout player according to Crook, as the eyes of the football world watched City excel on the road Credit: Getty



"It's always tough to come here, if you look at the record it's tough. With the Pep (Guardiola) and (Jurgen) Klopp era it was tough for both teams, always has been.

"Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together.

"That's the only thing we can do."

Liverpool arrived at Anfield knowing they would have even stronger backing from their supporters as the findings on City stick around.

However, they were dealt a big blow before kick-off as Dominik Szoboszlai was not named in the squad due to a hamstring injury.



His absence followed the news that Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo would also miss the game with injuries.

3 Gravenberch's red card was the turning point in the match and Liverpool fell apart on their home turf Credit: Getty

Lewis Koumas made his first Premier League start and impressed on occasions up front.

But overall, the frailties in the defence and one-man disadvantage meant Liverpool have suffered their first league defeat.

Sports.title: ‘Devastated’ – Micah Richards demands Man City to show evidence in emotional request
Sports.content:
Micah Richards has emotionally called for Manchester City to disclose their evidence of innocence against the financial charges they face.

The Premier League announced that City have been found guilty by an independent commission on all charges of serious financial rule breaches from 2009 to 2018.



2 City say they have irrefutable evidence to support their innocence against charges of financial rule breaches Credit: Getty

Points deductions, stripped titles and relegation are sanctions that the club could face, although they have appealed against the verdict.

City stress they are innocent and claim they have a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' to support them.

This has remained unseen amid the appeal process, but Richards has demanded that they let fans see the evidence to ease uncertainty.



Richards, the ex-City defender who won the Premier League and FA Cup at the club, made his plea on Sky Sports before the clash away to Liverpool on Sunday.

Emotional Richards makes City demand

"I feel devastated, I would say," he replied when asked about how he felt watching his trophy celebrations, both of which came during the period of charges.



"More because of what the fans have had to go through and endure over this period. Me coming through the Man City academy, going there when I was 14.

"All the noise around Man City - what should happen and what shouldn't happen - and I put my neck on the line for this club.



"They've given me this amazing opportunity to go all the way through the academy and then break into the first team. My dream was to win the FA Youth Cup; I missed out on that.

"Then I won the FA Cup, move onto the Premier League. So, for that to be in question now is very confusing.

"You've got one side saying there's charges, you've got Man City's side saying they've got irrefutable evidence, and it just leaves a situation for me, for the fans, for everyone at the club. So devastating."

2 Richards, who made 245 appearances for City, wants them to release the evidence for their fans Credit: Rex



Richards then added: "I feel let down by the fact that it's dragged on so long.

"The fact that Man City talked about this evidence... I want to see it, make it easier for the fans because they're the last to know about everything.

"But us as players, what can we possibly do? We go out on the pitch, we give 100 per cent.

"I've literally got one knee giving 100 per cent for Manchester City Football Club; that's how much I love this club, and I would do anything for this club because of the opportunity they have given me.



"I'm in a difficult situation now where I'm being questioned, whether it be integrity, medals, or whatever it may be.

"But I know I gave everything, 100 per cent, for that club, and that's all I could have done as a player."

Sports.title: Liverpool dealt another huge blow as star man is ruled out of Manchester City clash
Sports.content:
Liverpool dealt another huge blow as star man is ruled out of Manchester City clash

Dominik Szoboszlai has dealt Liverpool a further blow after missing out on selection to face Manchester City.

The Hungarian midfielder is reportedly nursing a hamstring injury having not been seen at the team hotel on Sunday morning.

2 Szoboszlai is not fit to play for Liverpool in what is a big blow ahead of the City clash Credit: Getty

Liverpool are already without star attackers Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo for the encounter due to injuries.

Instead, it's Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister who will start in midfield for the Reds, with Florian Wirtz playing ahead of them.

Lewis Koumas has also been selected by Andoni Iraola in what will be his first Premier League start.

"Another one coming from the international games," Iraola told Sky Sports on Szoboszlai. "He came with an overload, he felt a tight hamstring.

"He's tried somehow, kind of pushing through training, but he was not feeling 100 per cent and we will have to wait for Dom, yes."

City, who are set to face a hostile reception at Anfield following their guilty verdict on financial charges, are at full strength.

Erling Haaland, Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson all start for Enzo Maresca's side.

Nico O'Reilly is also in over Josko Gvardiol, despite picking up an injury on international duty with England and withdrawing from the squad.

You can follow updates of what promises to be a tasty fixture on our live blog here.

Not so friendly welcome

It is almost two weeks since the Premier League announced City have been found guilty on all charges by an independent commission.

2 City are braced for a hostile reception against Liverpool due to their guilty verdict Credit: Getty

They were adjudged to have artificially inflated their revenue by over £900million from 2009 to 2018 via 'sham' contracts.

City have appealed and maintain their innocence amid the threat of sanctions such as points deductions, stripped titles and relegation.

Their team buses, flanked by police vehicles, arrived at Anfield via an alternative entrance to avoid the large crowd of Liverpool fans.

However, Reds supporters still expressed their grievances with flags that read 'Cheats' and 'Guilty 114'.

City fans were also escorted into the away end, although there was little to no disorder.

Inside the stands, one large banner had the message 'A generation of supporters cheated'.

Sports.title: Liverpool 0-3 Man City PLAYER RATINGS: Who always made the wrong decision in the big moments? Who will Andoni Iraola be demanding more from? And who could be City's main man but for pending punishments?
Sports.content:
It was a game that had so much more to it than a football match. Liverpool fans brought cheating banners, City fans brought bananas to mock their charges – but, ultimately, the Premier League leaders brought their A-game.

Underneath all the off-field chaos, there was indeed a football match taking place. And it was a good one, until Ryan Gravenberch was sent off.

Liverpool went blow-for-blow with Enzo Maresca's City, whose future remains uncertain. 'Going down,' the Liverpool fans chanted – they may well be, but, for now, they are the league's best.

Gravenberch was given his marching orders in the 62nd minute, and Liverpool couldn't cope after. City upped the tempo, and scored three goals, celebrating as if nothing was going on off the field.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all on the scoresheet as City carried on their 100 per cent record. Liverpool, meanwhile, have two wins from their six games so far, and are ninth in the standings.

Daily Mail Sport's LEWIS STEELE was at Anfield to rate the players.

Erling Haaland (centre) was on the scoresheet as Manchester City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1)

Alisson – 6

Could do nothing about any of City’s goals. Had little to do beforehand but his presence put off Haaland at 0-0.

Ronald Araujo – 5

Played fine overall but Doku and Co gave him the run-around when they started to fly forward after the red card. Booked.

Jeremy Jacquet – 6

Made some fine interventions in the first-half and has been a strong addition to Liverpool’s team.

Virgil van Dijk – 5

Slow to react at times and none of Liverpool’s defenders could cope with City when they had the man advantage. Booked.

Milos Kerkez – 5

Made some powerful runs forward but struggled defensively, which happens all too often for the Hungary international.

Milos Kerkez (right) was good going forwards but once again struggled defensively

Ryan Gravenberch was having his best game this season until an unnecessary red card

Ryan Gravenberch – 6

Was enjoying his best afternoon of the season until he was sent off. The first yellow was harsh but the second was correct and he should have known better than to make the foul.

Alexis Mac Allister – 6

Like midfield partner Gravenberch, the Argentine had a couple of chances to score but had two shots that went inches wide.

Victor Munoz – 7

Liverpool’s best player and a constant nuisance. A rather unknown figure before he signed for the club, Munoz is outshining his big-money team-mates.

Florian Wirtz – 4

Another big game that has gone by without a meaningful moment from £116million Wirtz. Made the wrong decision in the big moments time and again.

Bradley Barcola – 5

Had one or two nice moments but Iraola will be demanding much more from the £123million signing. Has not got going in a red shirt yet.

Lewis Koumas – 7

Like a rash with relentless running, which Iraola will love. This was his first Premier League start and it will not be his last if he carries on impressing like this.

Lewis Koumas didn't stop running and will be enjoying plenty more Premier League minutes if he keeps that up

Manager

Andoni Iraola – 6

His team were well in the game until the red card which ended the contest. Might have done better if not for injuries, too.

Substitutes

Trey Nyoni (for Wirtz, 66) – 6

Jeremie Frimpong (for Araujo, 75) – 4

Rio Ngumoha (for Koumas, 75) – 5

Joe Gomez (for Jacquet, 88)

Federico Chiesa (for Barcola, 88)

MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1)

Gianluigi Donnarumma – 7

Made two strong saves in the space of seconds during Liverpool’s best spell of the game. Commanding at claiming set-pieces.

Matheus Nunes – 7

Pocketed £123million man Barcola for the most part and seems an integral member of Maresca’s side.

Ruben Dias – 7

A captain’s performance from Dias, who could be seen giving mini team talks to his troops during the game.

Marc Guehi – 6

A few shaky moments early doors but settled and produced a confident display as ever.

Nico O’Reilly – 6

Munoz gave him a tough time but O’Reilly made some fine defensive interventions. Good running going the other way but his final ball was lacking. Booked.

Victor Munoz (right) have Nico O'Reilly a tough afternoon but the City man coped well overall

Enzo Fernandez – 7

A tenacious player who has breathed new life into City’s midfield that looked leggy at times last season.

Elliot Anderson – 9

An outstanding footballer who could be the main man for City for the next decade if it was not for pending punishments. Ran the game and seemed to be first to every loose ball.

Iliman Ndiaye – 6

Double trouble for the Senegal international, who was not just a rival player but also an ex-Evertonian. Struggled to affect the game.

Rayan Cherki – 8

Sensational goal and is one of the most exciting players in the Premier League, the sort that kids will want to emulate on the playground.

Antoine Semenyo – 7

Another bright light for City, Semenyo gave his old boss Iraola a few headaches down both wings.

Erling Haaland – 7

Barely noticeable but came up with the all-important moment that opened the scoring. How often does he do that?

Manager

Enzo Maresca – 8

Got his tactics spot on as City weathered the early storm and then started to thrive after the red card.

Enzo Maresca got his tactics spot on with his team excelling after Gravenberch's red card

Substitutes

Jeremy Doku (for Ndiaye, 56) – 8

Josko Gvardiol (for O’Reilly, 66) – 7

Allan (for Haaland, 80)

Ayyoub Bouaddi (for Fernandez, 80)

Rulli, Khusanov, Kovacic, Lewis, Reis.

Referee

Chris Kavanagh – 4

The red card ruined the game. The second yellow was right but the first was harsh.

Sports.title: Gary Neville claims the wait for sanctions against Man City is 'really bad for the Premier League' as Piers Morgan labels it a 'total farce' after Enzo Maresca's side extend lead at top
Sports.content:
Gary Neville claims the wait for sanctions against Man City is 'really bad for the Premier League' as Piers Morgan labels it a 'total farce' after Enzo Maresca's side extend lead at top

Gary Neville has claimed the uncertainty surrounding Manchester City's status is 'really bad for the Premier League' after their 3-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield.

Enzo Maresca's side played for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

The club maintained their innocence and appealed against the verdict.

If City lose their appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Despite receiving a hostile welcome to Anfield on Sunday, Man City earned a 3-0 victory over Liverpool to continue their perfect start to the Premier League season with Maresca's side now three points clear after six straight wins.

Neville, who served as a co-commentator on the match for Sky Sports, claimed post-match that the fixture had underlined to him that the continuing uncertainty is 'really bad for the Premier League'.

Manchester City beat Liverpool 3-0 in their first match since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules

Gary Neville claimed the wait for sanctions against Man City is 'really bad for the Premier League' after watching the club move three points clear at the top of the table

Neville cited the use of 'sham' in the independent commission verdict, which was repeatedly used to describe contracts used to help disguise secret funding of more than £830million, claiming people could begin to use the word when discussing the league with City's status unclear.

'A win at Anfield is really difficult, and we should be eulogising them, but there is that thing in the back of your mind,' Neville said.

'At the end of the game it's quite hard because you're imagining that if these guilty verdicts are confirmed that Manchester City are not going to be in the position that they're in, and there's going to be a huge cloud hanging over the whole league.

'This is not good for the Premier League right now, that's what I've just recognised today.

'This is really bad for the Premier League and it's going to continue for a few months.

'The word "sham" was used quite a lot and people will think for the next few months it's a sham league.

'We've heard the word 'cheats' ring round the ground for the last ten minutes of the match. We've heard Liverpool fans singing 'going down' at a team at the very top of the league. You can't get that negativity out of your head.

'What we can do is admire the football, admire Erling Haaland and [Jeremy] Doku and the finishes we've seen, and the [Rayan] Cherki goal.

Enzo Maresca and Man City players celebrated wildly in front of their fans at full time

Piers Morgan claimed Man City winning the title 'could ruin the Premier League' as he called for a punishment to be announced

'The Man City fans can celebrate behind the goal, but the rest of us are wondering what's going to happen and it's damaging right now.'

Man City eased to victory in the second half at Anfield after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for two bookable offences.

Haaland and Doku struck in a three-minute spell to put Man City 2-0 up, before Cherki sealed victory with the visitors' third of the match.

Man City players and Maresca celebrated in front of their supporters following the triumph, with the head coach later praising his side for how they handled the 'noise' around the match.

Neville's fellow pundit Jamie Carragher claimed there is 'no way' Man City could be allowed to win the league this season if the verdict remains, and stressed the need for a final outcome before the end of the campaign.

'Man City right now are the best team in the league, they are top of the league, but there is no way Man City can be allowed to win the league this year if they are found guilty,' Carragher said.

'That cannot happen.

'We keep using the word sham, the Premier League used the word sham about the last eight years, but we didn’t know it at the time.

'We know it now, we are watching it. That today, what does it mean going forwards. This has to be done before the end of the season, there is no way this can carry on until the end of the season.'

Broadcaster Piers Morgan, responding to Man City's celebrations, claimed the club leading the Premier League was a 'total farce' and called for their punishment to be announced.

'Sorry, but this is a total farce. Manchester City players, and fans, celebrating wildly like nothing has happened - despite the club being exposed as the worst cheats in football history,' Morgan wrote.

'What happens if they win the title again this season? That could ruin the Premier League.'

'The Premier League has to act asap and announce City’s punishment. This cannot go on.'

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca insists he doesn't care how long Man City's appeal against guilty verdict takes as he shrugs off the 'noise' after thumping win at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca brushed off his club's conviction on 114 Premier League charges on Sunday night and insisted: 'We have to make our own noise.'

Maresca was laughing and in high spirits after the 3-0 win kept City three points clear at the top of the Premier League, repeatedly describing the controversy around the guilty charges as 'noise' and insisting he 'didn't care' how long the club's appeal took.

He said: 'The noise will always be there so we need to learn how to deal with that but at the same time we need to try and bring our noise, which is win games which is what we have done today. At the end of the game, our fans were singing so the noise was from us and not the environment.

'All the away games are going to be with noise so we need to learn how to deal with the noise. And at the same time, we need to make our noise. Our noise is we're singing at the end, our fans, and this has to be our target at the moment.'

City maintaining Premier League ascendancy while Liverpool's fans branded them 'cheats' and taunted them with chants of 'going down' discredits the competition. But on the question of an appeal dragging on, the Italian said: 'You cannot imagine how happy I am. I don't care.'

He also insisted that off-field issues may galvanise his team, who have won their first six games of the campaign. 'Probably yes, probably no. I don't know,' he said. 'It can create togetherness with the fans. Hopefully we can celebrate a win. This is the only thing we can focus on.'

Enzo Maresca was delighted with his players' positive reaction to the guilty verdict asking for more 'noise' from the jubilant travelling support at full time

A dejected Andoni Iraola maintained he was pleased with his team's performance despite the final score

Erling Haaland bagged his sixth of the season in emphatic style to open the scoring early in the second half

City were given a taste of the hostility they will face from now on when forced to take an alternative route to Anfield, as thousands of Liverpool fans lined the approach road to hurl abuse at them. Abu Dhabi chairman Khaldoon al Mubarak did not put in an appearance at Anfield.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said of the situation created by City's appeal: 'Uncertainty is not good for anyone. But it is what it is, we cannot change it. We have to wait.'

He also said his players had performed well before the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch for a second yellow card after a foul on substitute Jeremy Doku. The Dutchman should never have been booked for a first challenge on Elliot Anderson, Iraola insisted.

Liverpool, whose defeat leaves them ninth, have won only four Premier League games at Anfield in ten months. But Iraola said: 'You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It's a loss and we didn't get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.' He said it was unlikely Dominik Szoboszlai will be back from a hamstring to face Austrian side LASK on Wednesday.

Erling Haaland, whose father Alf-Inge was among City's fans celebrating when he scored City's first, said: 'It's important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do. It was tough. It was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front.'

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher calls for Liverpool to DROP Florian Wirtz after he offered 'absolutely nothing' in Man City defeat following 'last hope' move from Jurgen Klopp
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has led the criticism for Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz after another drab performance against Manchester City from the £116million man.

Wirtz was one of the biggest movers in the Premier League last season but had a below-par season, with many giving him the benefit of the doubt considering it was his first season in the division.

But he has continued to struggle this term too, and under a new manager, with the German yet to score and picking up just one assist in the six top-flight matches so far this season.

His performances have led to some questioning his place in the Liverpool team, and former Reds defender Carragher is now front and centre of that after Wirtz's showing against Manchester City on Sunday.

'I'm going to go back to Florian Wirtz, because I was critical of him after the last game Liverpool played at Bournemouth,' he began on Sky Sports. 'I was then criticised a little bit by Liverpool supporters for putting a negative slant on it. But what I did say was it could be the last hope if Jurgen Klopp could get his arm around him when he was with Germany.

'He played really well for Germany under Jurgen Klopp. But he has come here today, I'm looking at the game with no Isak and no Gakpo, our two best attackers this season. We need Barcola and we need Wirtz to step up and help Munoz and Koumas at the top of the pitch. Koumas and Munoz were better than the two £100m players.

Florian Wirtz (left) should be dropped from the Liverpool team, according to Jamie Carragher

Carragher (right) criticised the midfielder's lack of impact throughout his Reds career

'That can't be right. It's not right. It wasn't a decision for anyone in the stadium when Liverpool went down to 10 men. And the big bright spark was Gravenberch. He started badly and was taken out the team. There is no way Wirtz should be playing ahead of Gravenberch.

'What Florian Wirtz is doing for Liverpool is not enough right now. He's played 55, 60 games for Liverpool. If we were looking at Barcola, he has played four or five. You would want more but hold your horses. If you were critical of him, it would be over the top, but not the guy that has played 60 games.'

Wirtz has in fact played 56 times for the Reds, picking up seven goals and 11 assists in that time.

He joined a team last summer that had just won the Premier League with Dominik Szoboszlai as their No10, but have now moved the Hungarian into a deeper role.

That, according to Carragher, should not happen going forward.

'He shouldn't be in the Liverpool team right now,' Carragher added on Wirtz. 'I don't want to hammer Liverpool players. But we're not saying this after five-ten games, we're saying this after 50-60 games.

'Wirtz never looks like scoring a goal. You don't come away thinking he missed chances or he worked the goalkeeper. There was absolutely nothing today where you thought he put someone through, or nearly scored. There's absolutely no goal threat whatsoever.'

Sports.title: Man City embraced their shame and laughed in the face of English football, no one knows whether their emphatic 3-0 win at Anfield matters. For now cheats do prosper, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Manchester City delighted in a delirious dance with their own notoriety at Anfield on Sunday evening. The team belonging to the club branded the biggest cheats in English sporting history embraced their shame and laughed in the face of the scorn of the rest of football.

On the occasion of their first public outing since they were found guilty by an independent commission of 114 charges of financial chicanery, City defied the revulsion that has been visited upon them and waltzed past Liverpool, the team which suffered most from their cheating, with a comprehensive 3-0 victory. It was another bad day for a game reeling from what City have done to it.

The win restored their three-point lead over Arsenal at the top of the table and extended their record at the start of this season to six successive triumphs but as the football world waits to see whether their appeal succeeds or what their punishment will be, no one knows whether that matters or whether it is utterly meaningless.

The City fans in the away end turned their backs to the pitch in the dying minutes and did the Poznan, the dance of celebration they have made their own. Their celebrations may be muted if, as many expect, they are relegated to League Two at the end of this season.

It is a sign of quite how dysfunctional the Premier League has become that a team with a perfect record, a team that played some wonderful football in the second half, was serenaded with chants of ‘going down, going down, going down’ by the Liverpool fans. They may indeed be going down but they are going to enjoy life while they do.

For them, all the noise was just sound and fury, signifying nothing. For the rest of football, it was a thoroughly dispiriting day. For now, it seems, cheats do prosper.

Erling Haaland celebrates breaking the deadlock at Anfield after Liverpool went a man down

The Reds were beaten 3-0 by City in the visitors' first game since being found guilty

Jeremy Doku netted the second of the game with a brilliant curling effort in front of fans waving inflatable bananas

It will have struck a discordant note for the rest of the game to see them celebrating so wildly at the end when they have been found guilty of serial cheating but the modern City is not a club known for its humility and they are not about to change now. This is a league in limbo but for now, no one can touch them.

The match merely marked the end of an extraordinary day on Merseyside. A couple of hours before kick-off, crowds were already standing five and ten deep on the Anfield Road, as they had done back in the closing weeks of the 2013-14 season when they tried to will Brendan Rodgers and his Liverpool team to the Premier League title with a wall of sound. City won the title that year, of course. It was one of the triumphs that may soon have an asterisk attached to it.

This was a different kind of welcoming party. It was intended to greet the City coach. Some Liverpool fans held up flags bearing the legend: ‘Guilty – 114 Charges’. Beneath the words, there were likenesses of Erling Haaland, Bernardo Silva, Pep Guardiola, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki dressed as a gang of convicts, looking glum, heads in hands, surrounded by champagne bottles and piles of cash.

Other Liverpool supporters held up flags that simply said: ‘Cheats’, against a sky blue background and the figure ‘114’. Further along the road, red smoke from a flare wafted through the air. The police officers waiting near the Players’ Entrance looked edgy. The temperature began to rise. ‘You cheating bastards,’ the Liverpool supporters yelled in anticipation of the bus arrival, ‘you know what you are.’

It felt like football’s equivalent of waiting to pelt aristocrats with rotten eggs as they rode in tumbrils through the streets. But the City coach did not come this way. It took a back route instead and approached the ground all but unnoticed.

Two buses painted blue and bearing City’s name passed slowly beneath the Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand and, followed by a jogging security contingent, trundled unmolested into an underground car park.

And so on this day, amid subterfuge and shame, City’s new life as the pariahs of the English game began. This is their reality now, after an independent commission decided they were guilty of 114 of the charges of financial chicanery that the Premier League had levelled against them. The rest of English football will treat them as condemned men.

They entered Anfield like fugitives and, as they try to escape the guilt for the financial chicanery that helped them win so many titles between 2009 and 2018 and beyond, fugitives is what they are. It will probably feel that way to the rest of the league until their appeal has been decided and they have faced their punishment. City gave notice on Sunday that, until then, they will laugh in their faces.

City are laughing in the face of football and were delirious in their celebrations

Ryan Gravenberch (right) was sent off by referee Chris Kavanagh in the second half

Anfield displayed banners mocking City after the guilty verdict, including one with 114 pound signs within the word 'cheat'

'A generation of supporters cheated', summed up the sentiment from Liverpool fans

The Anfield crowd left them in no doubt about the extent of the anger that other clubs feel about the unfair advantage they gained for so long. ‘A generation of supporters cheated,’ one banner hanging in the Kop said, articulating the feeling that City stole away the joy of days of triumph from fans of other clubs, days they will never get back.

‘And after all, you robbed us all,’ another banner in the Kop said. At the end of their warm-up, it was that banner in front of which the Liverpool players chose to congregate and salute their supporters. Perhaps it was coincidence. Perhaps it was not. The supporters roared their approval.

'All of your stars are fading away,’ one more sign referencing the work of Manchester band Oasis, said. In the front row of the Kop, home fans unfurled a long, thin, banner that ran for half the length of the stand. It was a row of 114 £ signs, decorated with the word ‘Cheats’.

In many ways, it was sad to see City reduced to this. This is a fine old club brought low by the actions of its owners. Once the standard bearers of the Premier League, once a team that won an unprecedented four top flight titles in succession, City are now a team to be mocked and scorned by supporters of other clubs.

The television cameras picked out City’s embattled chief executive Ferran Soriano sitting in the stands. There was no sign of the chairman, Khaldoon Al Mubarak. That was a surprise on a day when most expected him to make a point of showing solidarity with the club’s players and staff.

It was left – as it is always left – to the most loyal of City’s fans to stand up for the club. What has happened to City is no fault of theirs, of course, and the hard-core travelling contingent – including Noel Gallagher - showed their own defiance in the best way, travelling here to hostile territory and waving an army of inflatable bananas in the air.

Better inflated bananas than inflated commercial income. The yellow fruit was a nod to the times before the Abu Dhabi takeover when City spent time in the lower leagues and their fans did not waver in their support. The bananas were a symbol of that time. For some legacy fans, the prospect of being relegated to League Two holds no fears.

Rayan Cherki scored the third after a great team move as City ran out comfortable winners

Enzo Maresca gestures to the fans after steering his side to victory away at Anfield

City supporters are seen doing the Poznan in a game that ultimately could be meaningless

City fans in the away end celebrated while the rest of football turned away in despair

City’s players, too, were unfazed by their infamy. It was three minutes after half-time when Liverpool conjured the first real chance of the game. The ball fell to Lewis Koumas on the edge of the area and his stinging left-foot shot was beaten away by Gianluigi Donnarumma. Suddenly Liverpool poured forward. Donnarumma saved again from the excellent Ryan Gravenberch. Alexis Mac Allister whistled a shot wide.

But then City took control. Haaland, whose father Alf Inge, was also standing with the City away fans, was played through by Antoine Semenyo but clipped his right-foot shot just wide of the far post.

Many had speculated that at least one of the teams would not finish the game with all ten outfielders on the pitch and they were proved correct three minutes later when Gravenberch was sent off for a second bookable offence, an innocuous push on Jeremy Doku. Fernandez brandished an imaginary card in the referee’s direction as soon as the foul occurred and Chris Kavanagh agreed with him.

Seconds after Gravenberch had trudged off the pitch, City were ahead. Doku cut inside and unleashed a fierce shot that cannoned off Mac Allister. Haaland reacted fastest and lashed an instant drive past Alisson. The goal was scored in front of the away end. The fans there celebrated wildly. The goal must have tasted particularly sweet.

Three minutes later, City were two ahead. Doku teased Victor Munoz on the edge of the Liverpool box, jinked to his right and curled a delicious shot over Alisson. Twelve minutes from time, Cherki completed the victory with the best goal of the lot, running on to an extravagant flick by Josko Gvardiol and slipping the ball beneath Alisson for the third.

The pariahs celebrated in front of their own supporters and punched the air. The rest of football turned away in despair at what the game has become and the uncertainty that stalks it.

Sports.title: No triumphalism from Liverpool fans, just a bleak sense that the football had given way to utter irrelevance. A dark day at Anfield but Man City will probably not be here again, writes IAN HERBERT
Sports.content:
No triumphalism from Liverpool fans, just a bleak sense that the football had given way to utter irrelevance. A dark day at Anfield but Man City will probably not be here again, writes IAN HERBERT

The planning had been meticulous, of course. Flags bearing the word ‘cheats’ and images of Pep Guardiola and Manchester City’s players as convicts were going for a fiver from stalls next to The Park pub. People responded to the message, circulating all week, about meeting at the King Harry pub ahead of a ‘greeting’ for the City team bus. ‘Bring flags, pyros, flares,’ it said, and they did.

But inside those pubs, there was neither triumphalism, nor a particular desire to raise holy hell on the visiting team, just a bleak and resigned sense that the football combat which is supposed to belong to 4.30pm on an Anfield autumn Sunday had given way to utter irrelevance.

Virtually everyone willing to be engaged on this subject in The Park mourned a proper honest football rivalry and so much time lost on the one they had always thought was real.

‘You can’t turn things back and go to the ifs, buts and titles that might have been,’ said Dave. ‘It’s the wasted time, isn’t it? I’ve been bringing my boy here for eight years and I ask myself how much of that counts now.’

Supporters like this want to feel they have belonged to a contest which resonates down the ages and some of them actually talked, with sentiment, about Liverpool’s Manchester United clashes of the Sir Alex Ferguson era.

God knows that rivalry crossed the line of decency at times, with minorities of each side’s fanbase using the other’s tragedy to mock them.

Liverpool fans gathered outside Anfield for a hostile welcome but inside the ground there was little triumphalism

Liverpool were exposed for squad limitations - which happens when not playing 'fantasy football', as their opposition had done

United know all about running a gauntlet of hate as their bus approached this stadium. Bob Paisley was put on their team bus one year in the 1980s, in hope that the sight of him talking to Bryan Robson might quell the hate as it headed up to Anfield.

But that was a rivalry built on bricks and mortar, not shifting sands, paid for in pounds sterling, not Abu Dhabi funny money.

It was honesty which saw Ferguson knock Liverpool off their perch. ‘Give me that every day,’ was the response when that thought was put to those in the King Harry, a drinking place for generations of Liverpool fans.

‘It seems strange to say anything positive about Ferguson and United, but it was about football then,’ said Sam, a student back in his home city to see Liverpool play. ‘We hated them, but they didn’t cheat us.’

The young group he was with were not inclined to head out and join the thousands who, by 2.30pm, were gathering around the place on Anfield Road where the front window of City’s coach was shattered by a missile before the Champions League quarter-final first leg in 2018. ‘Doesn’t interest me. No pleasure in that,’ said Sam.

To take that walk was to witness the extraordinary spectacle of hundreds standing on sandstone walls, shinning up signposts and hanging out of upstairs bedroom windows to see the City bus and somehow play a part in something. They were photographed, videoed and the gathering became something of a celebrity event, so hundreds of others joined them for fear of missing out. A parallel event took hold and as it did so, you wondered where the game we love had gone.

Part of the backdrop to this scene was an image of Bill Shankly, along with his words, which one of the hotels has mounted in red and white. ‘The socialism I believe in is everyone working for each other, everyone having a share of the rewards,’ are those words. ‘It’s the way I see football. It’s the way I see life.’ Shankly would certainly not have cherished this day.

City fans celebrated their win with abandon but they will probably not be back for a while

Liverpool fans felt a sense of resignation about the credibility of what they were watching

Around the back-to-back terraces stretching between The Park and the King Harry were reminders of how much harder growth is when you don’t have a Gulf state’s sovereign wealth fund behind you. Pockets of waste ground are yet to be shaped into something better by Liverpool City Council and the place lacks the opulence of east Manchester, which has been transformed by Abu Dhabi.

But when the houses come, they will be homes for local people who badly need them, not swanky flats which price them out, as so much of east Manchester became after the Gulf state was given first voice of lucrative development sites by Manchester City Council.

In the Sky Sports studio, Daniel Sturridge spoke about wanting to know where he stood when it came to his 2013-14 season for Liverpool, one about which this club can feel genuinely robbed. But Roy Keane, integral to that purer, honest Liverpool/United rivalry, cut to the underlying pathos of what City’s deceit has left us with. ‘We all want to move on from this,’ he said. ‘This could go on for years and it will ruin the game.’

Even on this day, Liverpool were exposed for the squad limitations which come of not having ‘fantasy football’ money, as Jurgen Klopp once described City’s outlay.

Briefly, Lewis Koumas almost conspired to script something excellent from the meaninglessness. The 21-year-old, socks around his ankles, was standing pretty much on the spot where Steven Gerrard’s slip against Chelsea handed City the title, 12 years ago, when he raced to receive Bradley Barcola’s pass and hit a fine rising drive. Some story it would have been, for a young Liverpudlian, as Gerrard looked on.

But it was Erling Haaland, a player handed a £525,000-a-week, nine-year contract, 21 months ago, who scored instead. Jeremy Doku, a City substitute earning £180,000-a-week under the terms of his new deal, turned the screw.

In those days of fair and honest combat, the scoreline would have sent the Anfield crowd away nursing anger and loathing. But those who drifted out on Sunday night seemed at a loss about an irrelevant footnote to a phantom rivalry and a City side who will probably not be here again for some time. There were no winners on this day.

Sports.title: Liverpool's lack of depth exposed as Andoni Iraola's men crumbled far too easily against rampant Man City... the big-money signings failed to step up when needed, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
As Manchester City’s jubilant players danced in front of Noel Gallagher, Alfie Haaland and Co in an away end full of inflatable bananas, the Anfield DJ had some fun by playing Little Lies by Fleetwood Mac.

Most of what we saw in this blockbuster-billed but slight letdown of a spectacle is a lie, of course – but for Liverpool and Andoni Iraola, there were several cold, hard truths staring them in the face.

For the second year in a row, the sensational talents of Jeremy Doku, Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland were simply too much for the Reds to handle, in a short period that – regardless of being a man down – showed why Iraola’s men are a little short of what they want to be.

It was the first defeat for the Basque boss since he moved from Bournemouth but also confirmed a few more worries that may have nagged him in his first months on Merseyside, such as the faltering fortunes of the big-money men.

Florian Wirtz was the biggest letdown of the 22 that started the match, while Bradley Barcola has left a lot to be desired since his move from Paris Saint-Germain. A few nice moments aside, neither of the two marquee men did enough.

Barcola will be given time, of course, as he settles into his new surroundings — but Wirtz is not the new boy any more and needs to start delivering.

Victor Munoz's display was one of the few positives to take from a bleak day for Liverpool

At a combined £239m, Wirtz and Barcola were shown up by the two unknown quantities that joined them in the Reds attack: Lewis Koumas, on his first Premier League start, and new boy Victor Munoz, who signed from Osasuna for £34.5m, peanuts in this day and age.

Koumas was like a rash with his relentless pressing, Munoz was a constant nuisance to City’s defenders, but Barcola was predictable and Wirtz constantly made the wrong decisions when he got the ball in attacking areas.

This game was there to be won for Liverpool. There were openings either side of half time and yet the home team did not seem to believe enough, second-guessing themselves when they had chances to exploit holes in behind City.

It would be wrong to criticise Iraola’s side without mentioning two huge mitigating factors, though: the red card, which was the wrong decision, and three defining players sitting in the stands in Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai.

The Reds have scored seven league goals this season and six had come from that trio. Without them, there was a lack of bite as the attack looked rather toothless.

This afternoon, then, also showed up Iraola’s lack of depth, an issue that was well flagged during the summer transfer window.

Sunday saw another disappointing display from Liverpool's big-money signings

Without Isak, they were left to rely on Koumas who is an admirable player with a big future but was playing in the Championship with Hull City last season.

There were things to like about this performance. Until the red card, Liverpool were solid at the back and Alisson barely had a save to make despite City finding a lot of joy with off-the-ball runs from the likes of O’Reilly and Anderson exposing spaces.
