Sports.title: Ryan Garcia’s Catchweight Defense Overlooks Who Benefits
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia’s defense of catchweights leaves out who benefits when the more popular fighter dictates the conditions. He argues that flexible limits create bouts that otherwise could not occur, entirely skipping over how that dynamic forces concessions onto opponents.

“Impossible @Showbizz. That stops matchups that couldn’t happen without it. It will actually limit boxing and boxing is a sport without any [limits],” Ryan said on X.

Meeting between divisions can bridge weight classes, sure. Yet the marquee attraction can easily use contract terms to tilt the contest before either man touches a glove.

The B-side contender gets squeezed into a corner. Walk away, and he surrenders his career-high purse, elite visibility, plus a rare spotlight. Agree, and he secures the event while compromising his physical prime on fight night.

Ryan overlooks that reality. A signed contract proves agreement occurred, not that both sides wielded equal clout during negotiations.

His 2023 clash with Gervonta Davis proved the exact dynamic. The deal called for a 136-pound limit, paired with a morning check capping rehydration at 146 pounds. Davis wanted that second barrier.

Even when contract terms apply equally on paper, they rarely extract the same toll. One athlete cruises in comfortably while the other drains himself dry just to qualify.

Garcia also sidesteps rehydration stipulations altogether. These terms extend far past the opening weigh-in, policing how much bulk a fighter recovers before entering the ring. Paired with strict weight caps, they hand the A-side major leverage over an adversary’s preparation.

Nobody can claim Davis definitely loses without those rules in place. Still, simply getting two big names into the ring cannot stand as proof that the contract was balanced. Ryan loves talking about flexibility. His case still needs to account for contenders who must surrender their physical strength just to earn their shot against the bigger star.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Sticks With Original Riyadh Fight Plan
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez plans to proceed with his October 31 bout against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh, Turki Alalshikh confirmed, standing by the Saudi boxing chief amid ongoing uncertainty around the event.

“Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens. He fears nothing,” Alalshikh wrote on X.

That commitment signals a fighter acting in full partnership with organizers. Instead of requesting a change of venue, Canelo gave private assurances that he will make the trip as scheduled. For someone working to hold the fight card together, receiving that backing from the main attraction carries serious weight.

Alalshikh made his appreciation unmistakable in his closing message.

“Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends.”

Canelo is displaying loyalty by keeping the original arrangement intact. Alalshikh has put substantial muscle behind major events featuring the Mexican superstar, and Canelo appears determined to return that backing when complications arise.

Turki Alalshikh is holding the deepest checkbook the sport has ever seen. For an aging superstar whose standard pay-per-view numbers in Las Vegas had begun to settle, maintaining direct favor with Riyadh Season is essential.

How prospective spectators respond to the situation remains less certain.

A promise from the headliner aids the promotion, yet it will not settle the concerns of traveling supporters. Individuals looking at plane tickets, hotel reservations, or seat prices will reach their own conclusions. Canelo’s willingness to compete does not guarantee their presence.

Sparse seating on fight night would still mean Alalshikh values the champion’s pledge. Still, empty sections would drain energy from the arena once Canelo and Mbilli step under the lights. Official ticketing numbers remain unconfirmed, making lower attendance an open risk rather than a settled fact.

The boundary is simple: the fighter controls his arrival, while paying fans decide if they make the trip.

At this point, Alalshikh holds the guarantee he needed most. Based on his statement, Canelo is staying the course in Riyadh.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel’s Tyson Fury Pick Leans on Old Memories
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel picks Tyson Fury to handle Anthony Joshua, but that pick relies on memories from a decade ago. Kabayel shared rounds with Fury back in 2016, sharing the ring with a fleet-footed heavyweight vastly different from the man competing today.

Kabayel credits Fury with superior ring IQ, even while respecting Joshua’s single-shot knockout power. His prediction leans on Fury having multiple paths to victory, yet those ancient gym sessions tell us very little about present-day form.

“The better boxer, the better boxing IQ [is with] Fury,” Kabayel told The Ring. “But only one guy in the heavyweight division can beat the guys with one hand. This is Anthony Joshua.” “I think Fury will win the fight. Points, KO, but we will see. My prediction is with Fury.”

The glaring flaw in Kabayel’s logic involves Fury’s faded mobility. The 2016 incarnation feinted opponents out of position, changed angles effortlessly, and slipped outside hitting range with ease. Combine that fluidity with his massive frame, and he became a nightmare to track down.

Recent outings show a far more stationary operator. Fury still knows how to manipulate range with his reach, yet recognizing open space is quite different from possessing the foot speed to claim it. Against someone carrying Joshua’s power, lingering in the pocket too long invites disaster.

Kabayel admits his sparring comparison carries an asterisk.

“For me, the hardest sparring was with Fury,” Kabayel explained, pointing out that he had logged three extra years of professional seasoning before testing Joshua in 2019.

That timeline skews the perspective. Kabayel met Fury as a raw prospect, then shared rounds with Joshua as a fully developed contender capable of holding his own.

Fury’s ring craft gives him a legitimate shot. Still, wondering whether his aging reflexes can execute his intentions remains the central issue. Kabayel’s glowing scouting report honors a long-gone fighter Joshua never has to face.

Looking at Fury across his recent outings, the double defeat to Oleksandr Usyk followed by soft recovery touches against plodding veterans like Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach, you are watching a fighter surviving on reputation and size rather than elite capability.

Beating Wladimir Klitschko in Düsseldorf was a psychological masterclass against an aging champion afraid to pull the trigger, and the 2020 demolition of Deontay Wilder was the absolute ceiling of Fury’s offensive bullying. Everything since has been a steady march into decline.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Expects Early Finish In Daniel Dubois Rematch
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley expects his rematch with Daniel Dubois to finish early, with either heavyweight capable of ending the fight before it reaches the later rounds. Their first meeting lasted 11 rounds, so Wardley’s prediction points to a quicker, more explosive second fight.

“It’s only going one way. It’s finishing early one way or another. It’s going to be a crazy night. Everyone, tune in,” said Wardley to Queensberry.

That “one way or another” qualification leaves room for both outcomes. Wardley knows the danger Dubois brings, even after beating him the first time. He is promising action without pretending that trading heavy punches comes without a cost.

Wardley’s overhand right gives him a clear weapon to take into the rematch. He has already described how he used it to counter Dubois’ jab in their first fight, making Dubois think about what could come back whenever he extended his left hand.

Dubois needs an answer to that punch. His jab can help him control the fight, but throwing it repeatedly without adjusting his defense could give Wardley the opening he is looking for. Wardley doesn’t need to change much if the same counter remains available.

Still, their first fight showed that hurting Dubois early and finishing him early are two different things. Wardley had success well before the stoppage, yet needed 11 rounds to complete the job. Chasing a quicker ending could also make him easier to hit if he becomes too eager after landing.

Wardley expects his supporters to add to the atmosphere on Saturday.

“It’s huge for me. Hometown boy, home grown. Had the club, the supporters, everyone behind me from the beginning,” he said. “So it does mean the absolute most and they’re going to make themselves heard on Saturday night.”

The crowd will be ready for the fireworks Wardley promises. Whether the finish comes early depends on how well Dubois adjusts, and whether Wardley can turn his next opening into something decisive.

Sports.title: Ricardo Sandoval Must Settle The Score With Mendoza
Sports.content:
Ricardo Sandoval must decide on his next fight after losing his WBA and WBC flyweight titles to Sergio “Yoreme” Mendoza last Saturday night in Chicago. The immediate rematch route is his only real play if Golden Boy has a return clause baked into the contract.

Mendoza was brought in as a late replacement, so Sandoval’s team likely secured rematch language. If they did, Sandoval has to trigger it immediately. He gave up all the leverage he built by beating Kenshiro Teraji in Tokyo, and nobody at 112 or 115 is going to offer him big money without those belts.

If there is no rematch clause, Sandoval is in no-man’s-land. The flyweight division moves fast. Unification bouts, big cards in Japan, and potential moves up to junior bantamweight are off the table for him. Those paydays belong to Mendoza now.

To rebuild, Sandoval has to face reality about his defense. Getting dropped three times inside five rounds by a guy coming off a second-round knockout loss shows Sandoval’s habits caught up to him. He relies on taking shots to give shots, but without elite sharpness, his punch resistance completely disappeared last night under Mendoza’s firepower.

Apart from a rematch, he needs a tune-up to see if his chin and punch resistance can hold up before trying to climb back into the top five of the sanctioning bodies. Sandoval should aim for spring 2027, ideally March or April.

That gives him roughly five to six months. He cannot afford another extended layoff, yet he took serious physical damage on Saturday night. Absorbing three knockdowns before getting stopped in the fifth round means mandatory medical suspensions and mandatory rest. He must keep his gloves off for at least sixty to ninety days to let his body recover. Rushing into hard sparring in November or December would be reckless.

Sitting out another year would kill what is left of his career, though. Inactivity was a major reason his timing, reflexes, and punch resistance betrayed him against Mendoza. At 112 pounds, fighters burn out quickly, and the division forgets former champions fast.

Flyweight is the wrong division to play the brooding, inactive contender. It is arguably the most unforgiving weight class in the sport because success relies almost entirely on twitch reflexes, hand speed, and conditioning. Those are the exact attributes that disappear when a fighter sits on the shelf.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Hesitates Over Schofield vs. Zepeda Unification
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya agreed to a Floyd Schofield–William Zepeda unification after being pressed during DAZN’s post-fight interview, but his initial response suggested little enthusiasm for matching his two lightweight champions.

Schofield had just captured the vacant WBA title by defeating Lucas Bahdi when De La Hoya announced his interest in unifying. That invitation became less straightforward once Chris Mannix brought up Zepeda, Golden Boy’s WBC champion.

“We want to unify the titles against anybody,” said De La Hoya to DAZN.

Mannix asked whether Zepeda would be next. De La Hoya’s answer sent the conversation toward Abdullah Mason instead.

“Well, maybe it’s not the fight to do next, but let’s go with Mason or any world champion in the WBC. Whoever it is, ‘Kid Austin’ is ready,” said De La Hoya.

Mannix returned to the obvious option: “Zepeda has got that WBC world title. Let’s take that fight next.”

“We’ll make that fight happen then,” De La Hoya replied.

That was an agreement, although it came after De La Hoya had already suggested taking another route. There was no date announced or indication that either fighter had accepted the matchup.

The hesitation is understandable from a business perspective. Golden Boy now has two lightweight champions it can promote separately. Each can headline title fights, build his audience, and pursue opponents from other promotional companies. Putting them together guarantees that one leaves without his belt.

Mason is with Top Rank, making him a different proposition. Schofield could lose that fight too, but a victory would bring another title into Golden Boy while preserving Zepeda’s separate championship run. An in-house unification offers no such possibility.

That does not establish De La Hoya’s motive, but it explains why “anybody” might become less appealing when the opponent is another revenue stream within his own company.

For Schofield, Zepeda would also be a tough first defense. His sustained pressure and punch volume would test the new champion’s ability to keep control while being pushed backward.

Zepeda also has an obstacle to facing Schofield next. According to EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai, the WBC has ordered him to defend against interim champion Jadier Herrera, with purse bids scheduled for October 20. Mason’s WBO mandatory is also due, with Joe Cordina ranked No. 1.

De La Hoya’s unification plans could therefore require approval from the sanctioning bodies or agreements involving the mandatory challengers before either fight can proceed.

Sports.title: Schofield Wins WBA Title As Sergio Mendoza Upsets Sandoval
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield claimed the vacant WBA lightweight title, while Sergio Mendoza delivered the night’s biggest upset by stopping unified flyweight champion Ricardo Sandoval on Saturday at Wintrust Arena in Chicago.

The Golden Boy Promotions and Most Valuable Promotions card aired on DAZN. Schofield’s title victory came with disputed knockdown calls, while Mendoza overturned expectations in the co-feature.

Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs), of Austin, Texas, defeated Lucas “Prince” Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs), of Niagara Falls, Ontario, by unanimous decision over 12 rounds. The judges scored the fight 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111.

Schofield’s speed and movement helped him win rounds, but Bahdi’s power made the contest more competitive than the widest score suggested. In the third, Schofield knocked Bahdi into the ropes, prompting referee Ben Rodriguez to rule a knockdown.

Bahdi hurt Schofield during a fierce sixth round and landed a right hand in the ninth that sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Rodriguez credited Bahdi with a knockdown in the eleventh, although Bahdi appeared to step on Schofield’s foot as he went down. Schofield stayed mobile in the final round to secure the belt.

In the co-feature, southpaw Sergio “Yoreme” Mendoza (28-1, 24 KOs), of Hermosillo, Mexico, stopped Ricardo “El Niño” Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs), of Rialto, California, at 0:24 of the fifth round to capture the WBA and WBC flyweight titles.

Mendoza dropped Sandoval twice during the final half-minute of the second round, with referee Mark Nelson administering a count each time. Sandoval rallied in the fourth, outscoring the challenger, but Mendoza dropped him again early in the fifth. After Sandoval rose, Mendoza drove him into the ropes with another attack, prompting Nelson to stop the fight.

The defeat ended Sandoval’s reign in his first defense and disrupted his plans for bigger fights following a lengthy layoff.

Super featherweight Jan Paul Rivera (17-0, 7 KOs), of Salinas, Puerto Rico, defeated Abraham Perfecto (14-3, 9 KOs), of Tecate, Mexico, by unanimous decision over ten rounds.

Rivera dropped Perfecto with a left hook in the second, prompting a count from referee Tommy Gonzalez. Rivera lost a point for a low blow in the ninth but remained comfortably ahead, winning 99-89 on all three cards.

Cruiserweight Tristan “Sweet T” Kalkreuth (18-1, 13 KOs), of North Las Vegas, Nevada, stopped Ivan Rosado (12-1, 9 KOs), of San Juan, Puerto Rico, at 0:44 of the third round of their scheduled ten-round bout.

Kalkreuth dropped Rosado with a right hand to the chin in the first. A third-round flurry brought the intervention of referee Ben Rodriguez, with Rosado still on his feet.

Light middleweight Grant Flores (14-0, 10 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped Mikey Dahlman (19-3, 17 KOs) at 1:48 of the second round.

Flores dropped Dahlman with a left to the body in round two. Dahlman beat referee Dave Smith’s count, but Flores followed with unanswered punches until Smith halted the contest.

Lightweight Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Oxon Hill, Maryland, stopped Pedro Castaneda (9-2-1, 5 KOs), of Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, at 0:28 of the third round of their scheduled eight-round fight.

Boxing from a southpaw stance, Harvey landed a left hand to the chin that dropped Castaneda. Castaneda got up but was in no condition to continue, prompting referee Dave Smith to wave it off.

Super featherweight Cris Williams (15-0, 8 KOs), of Chicago, defeated southpaw Asa “Ace” Stevens (7-1-1, 2 KOs), of Waianae, Hawaii, by unanimous decision over eight rounds.

Williams controlled the opening four rounds and hurt Stevens in the seventh. The judges scored it 78-74 twice and 77-75, with Mark Nelson refereeing.

Minimumweight Naomy “Wonder Woman” Valle (16-1, 9 KOs), of San Jose, Costa Rica, defeated Sheyla Moreno by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds.

Valle’s cleaner punching helped her build a lead, and a point deduction for holding in the eighth did not prevent her from winning her professional U.S. debut. Dave Smith refereed the bout.

Heavyweight Joshua “The Rocket” Edwards (8-0, 7 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Houston, stopped Craig Lewis (15-10-1, 8 KOs), of Detroit, one second into the third round of their scheduled eight-round contest.

Edwards controlled the first two rounds and hurt Lewis near the end of the second. Lewis could not continue because of an injury, and referee Tommy Gonzalez halted the fight at the start of the third.

Michael Vale served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Beats Lucas Bahdi To Claim WBA Title
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield won the vacant WBA lightweight title Saturday night, using his speed and movement to beat Lucas Bahdi by unanimous decision in a fight that tested his ability to recover under pressure.

The judges scored it 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111 at Wintrust Arena in Chicago. Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) earned the belt, but Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs) made him work considerably harder than the widest card suggested.

Schofield established his jab early, darting into range with combinations before moving away. Bahdi answered with heavier punches and body work, showing that he could trouble the quicker fighter when he found openings.

A left hook sent Bahdi into the ropes in round three, earning Schofield a knockdown and an early advantage. Bahdi absorbed the setback and continued looking for opportunities to land his power shots.

The sixth became a fierce round in which both fighters were hurt. Bahdi badly rocked Schofield with heavy punches, but Schofield fired back rather than allowing the Canadian to take complete control. His willingness to trade made the fight entertaining, although it also gave Bahdi the kind of contest he needed.

Schofield returned to movement and counters in the following rounds. That approach forced Bahdi to chase, and his difficulty cutting off the ring allowed Schofield to collect points without remaining in punching range.

The refereeing became a talking point in the ninth when a Bahdi right hand sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Bahdi received credit for a knockdown in round eleven, though their feet tangled during that incident.

Schofield stayed mobile in the twelfth and reached the final bell. He showed enough boxing ability to win, along with the toughness to recover when Bahdi hurt him. The next step is tightening his defense: his speed won rounds, but trading unnecessarily repeatedly exposed him to Bahdi’s biggest weapon.

Ghana News.title: “US Embassy introduced TRIBE Culture Fest to NSA, GTA” – Kofi Adams
Ghana News.content:
Kofi Adams

Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams says the United States Embassy introduced TRIBE Culture Fest to the National Sports Authority (NSA) and the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) ahead of activities planned around the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Mr Adams made the disclosure on TV3 on Sunday, October 11, as he addressed questions surrounding the involvement of the private events organisation in the visa controversy.

According to the minister, the introduction took place during a meeting at the US Embassy, rather than through an arrangement initiated by his ministry.

“Tribe Fest Culture, I’m told, was introduced to the National Sports Authority and the Ghana Tourism Authority by the American Embassy. That is what my investigations told me,” he said.

The minister’s comments come amid scrutiny of arrangements involving TRIBE Culture Fest, the NSA and the GTA for activities linked to the World Cup in the United States.

The controversy has prompted questions about the submission of names to foreign embassies and the role of public institutions in supporting people seeking to travel for World Cup-related activities.

Mr Adams has maintained that the NSA did not inform his ministry of any agreement it had reached with the US Embassy concerning visa acquisition.

He also said the NSA’s engagements with the embassy were not necessarily related to the issuance of visas, distinguishing those discussions from the ministry’s own efforts to establish procedures for coordinating travel arrangements.

The Sports Ministry has previously maintained that its role included forwarding a request from the NSA seeking visa support for 90 people described as volunteers and event coordinators. The ministry has said forwarding the request did not amount to selecting the applicants or guaranteeing visa approvals.

The Minority in Parliament has called for a wider investigation into the roles of the Sports Ministry, NSA, GTA and TRIBE Culture Fest, arguing that the controversy raises questions that go beyond one official.

The allegations remain subject to investigation, with the relevant authorities expected to establish how the arrangements were made and whether any laws or procedures were breached.

Ghana News.title: “NSA did not tell us of any embassy arrangement” – Kofi Adams
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams says the National Sports Authority (NSA) did not inform him about any visa arrangements it had reached with the United States Embassy ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

His comments come amid growing controversy over visa arrangements involving the NSA, the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) and private entity TRIBE Culture Fest, which has triggered calls for investigations into the roles of the institutions and their officials.

Speaking on TV3 on Sunday, October 11, Mr Adams said the ministry was unaware of any agreement between the NSA and the embassy relating to visa acquisition.

“The embassy did not communicate to us, where they have reached, the NSA did not communicate to us where they have reached, the NSA did not communicate to us if they had any arrangement with the embassy, so all up till this point we knew that we are still having the engagement and setting the rules and boundaries of operations,” he said.

The minister explained that the NSA and GTA were government agencies whose employees travelling on official government business would require a different visa category from those travelling with the Ghana Football Association (GFA).

“NSA and GTA are governmental agencies, this is important because travellers who work for the GFA will need to apply for visitor B1,B2 visa’s, where emplyee’s of the NSA and GTA who are travelling on official government business will need to apply for diplomatic visas,” he said.

Mr Adams acknowledged that the NSA had engaged the US Embassy but insisted those discussions were not related to the issuance of visas.

“Yes the NSA were having their own engagement with the embassy but not in relation to the issuant of visas, those engement were outside of the visa acquisition,” he added.

The controversy has raised questions about the submission of names to foreign diplomatic missions and the roles played by state agencies and private organisations in facilitating travel for activities linked to the 2026 World Cup.

The Minority in Parliament has called for a broader investigation into the matter, arguing that accountability should extend beyond the former NSA Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah, who was suspended and later dismissed amid the controversy.

The minister’s comments come as the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service investigates the allegations. The outcome of the probe is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the visa arrangements and determine whether any wrongdoing occurred.

Ghana News.title: Glasner suffers loss on Selhurst return as Palace beat Forest
Ghana News.content:
Oliver Glasner endured a frustrating return to Crystal Palace as his Nottingham Forest side let slip an early lead to lose to the Eagles.

After guiding Palace to FA Cup and Conference League success, Glasner left the club at the end of last season and took on the Forest job in the summer.

Initially it looked like it would be a triumphant return to Selhurst Park as Forest took a third-minute lead through Dan Ndoye's neat low finish. They then dominated much of the first half, with Liam Delap somehow denied a second from point-blank range by Walter Benitez.

Palace were not in the game at all but incredibly turned the tables with two goals just before half time.

Daichi Kamada finished off a nice team move to level four minutes before the break for his first Premier League goal, and Jefferson Lerma headed in a second deep in stoppage time.

It got even better for Palace in the second half when Yeremy Pino slotted into the bottom corner, prompting Eagles fans to tease Glasner with chants aimed at their former manager.

Benitez made another fine save late on to prevent substitute Chris Wood from reducing the deficit and giving Forest some hope of snatching a point.

Palace's second win of the season moves them up to 12th in the Premier League, while Forest are 14th.

Ghana News.title: WAFU B U17: ‘We won but I expected more from my boys’ – Kassim Ocansey
Ghana News.content:
Black Starlets head coach Kassim Ocansey has expressed mixed feelings following Ghana’s 1-0 victory over Togo in their opening match of the 2026 WAFU Zone B U17 Championship in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.

Ghana secured all three points in the Group A encounter, with David Kwarteng scoring the decisive goal on the 7th minute in the game. However, despite the victory, Ocansey believes his players could have been more clinical in front of goal after creating several scoring opportunities.

“We won, but I expected more from my boys,” Ocansey said after the match, admitting that Ghana could have done better with the chances they created.

“We created good chances, but we couldn't convert. I am happy we have the three points, but we could have done better with the chances we created,” he added.

The Ghana coach expressed confidence in his team's attacking potential, insisting that improved finishing could help the Black Starlets score more goals in their subsequent matches.

“If we are able to convert the chances we create, we can get three or four goals in every game. We'll work on that ahead of our next game,” Ocansey stated.

The victory gives the Starlets a positive start to their campaign, but Coach Kassim Ocansey will be keen to address the team's shortcomings in front of goal as they prepare for their next assignment in the competition.

The Black Starlets will look to build on their opening-day triumph and maintain their winning momentum as they pursue qualification for the 2027 U17 Africa Cup of Nations through the WAFU Zone B Championship.

Kassim Ocansey’s side will come up against Benin in their next game on Tuesday

Ghana News.title: Man City cruise to statement win over 10-man Liverpool
Ghana News.content:
Manchester City's first game since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations ended in victory as they outclassed Liverpool at Anfield.

Enzo Maresca's side restored their three-point lead at the top of the table in emphatic fashion - but there remains the sense that this is a season in limbo as City await their punishment, with the potential for Premier League expulsion, relegation or record points deductions.

Liverpool fans made their feelings known before and during the game with constant "cheat" jibes, but City, who have appealed against the verdict of an independent commission, responded with a measured display before picking Liverpool apart, who had been reduced to 10 men when Ryan Gravenberch was sent off.

Erling Haaland broke the deadlock with a thunderous finish after 65 minutes, substitute Jeremy Doku adding the second with a stunning strike into the top corner three minutes later.

And City confirmed their vast superiority when Rayan Cherki produced brilliant individual skill to make it 3-0 12 minutes from time.

The game opened in a predictably fevered atmosphere as the Kop delivered taunts about the guilty verdict, unfurling banners emblazoned with messages such as 'A Generation Of Supporters Cheated', while City fans responded backing their owners by brandishing a flag reading 'In Khaldoon We Trust'.

Once the initial sound and fury died down, the first half was an anti-climax as City slowed the game to combat the hostile environment while Liverpool struggled to make a breakthrough.

The second half showed more signs of life, with City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma saving from Victor Munoz and Gravenberch in swift succession, while Haaland held his head in anguish after rolling a chance wide when clean through.

Gravenberch's dismissal, given a second yellow card for a foul on Doku, left Liverpool with an uphill task as City moved through the gears to win with ease.

Ghana News.title: Be careful with cross-border lending, foreign currency exposures – BoG to financial institutions
Ghana News.content:
Dr Johnson Asiama, BoG Governor

The Bank of Ghana has advised Regulated Financial Institutions (RFIs) that engage in cross-border lending, investments, trade finance, or foreign currency exposures to have adequate policies and procedures for identifying, assessing, measuring, evaluating, monitoring, reporting and controlling or mitigating country risk and transfer risk on a timely basis.

This is to avert the potential default or deterioration in credit quality of foreign counterparties arising from country-specific macroeconomic, fiscal, political or financial sector conditions.

The advice is captured in the Credit Risk Management Directive for all Banks, Savings and Loans, Finance Houses and Financial Holding Firms.

The BoG also urged RFIs not to introduce or implement such products, market entries, or delivery channels unless the required regulatory approvals have been obtained, where applicable.

Credit Risk Management Process

On Credit Risk Management Process, it said an RFI shall establish and enforce strict policies to avoid association with individuals involved in fraudulent activities or other serious financial crimes or misconduct.

Similarly, an RFI shall employ robust due diligence measures, including obtaining references from known parties, accessing credit reference bureaus, and becoming familiar with individuals responsible for managing a company, including checks on their integrity, experience, and financial condition.

Credit Appraisal and Approval

The Central Bank pointed out that an RFI shall establish sound, well-defined credit-granting criteria for approving credit in a safe and sound manner. “The criteria shall specify eligible borrowers, the types, amounts, and tenors of credit the RFI is willing to provide, and the terms and conditions under which credits may be granted”.

Again, an RFI shall undertake a comprehensive credit risk assessment that is proportionate to the nature, type and size of the exposure.

Similarly, it shall apply experienced credit judgement using a scalable and flexible approach to its credit risk assessment of a borrower, particularly where borrower information is limited, adding, FRIs shall diversify their loan portfolios across sectors, geographical locations, borrower types and credit risk mitigants within the constraints of local market structures.

Exposures to individuals

For exposures to individuals, the BoG said an RFI’s credit assessment shall, at a minimum and where relevant, consider the purpose and structure of the exposure and sources of repayment, including reasonable verification of income or cash flows using formal or alternative documentation; the borrower’s or counterparty’s current risk profile (including the nature and aggregate indebtedness) and its sensitivity to economic and market developments; among others.

From 1st July 2027, the Bank of Ghana will begin the implementation of the Credit Risk Management Directive for all Banks, Savings and Loans, Finance Houses and Financial Holding Firms.

The broad objective of the directive is to enhance the resilience of Regulated Financial Institutions (RFIs) by ensuring that they establish and fully implement adequate and effective credit risk management systems that commensurate with their risk-taking activities and capital strength.

Ghana News.title: GPL 2026/27: Medeama go three clear as Hearts of Oak recover and Bechem stage stunning comeback
Ghana News.content:
Medeama strengthened their position at the top of the Premier League with a commanding 3-1 victory over Heart of Lions, while Hearts of Oak returned to winning ways and Bechem United produced an impressive comeback on an eventful Matchday Six.

Karela United completed the weekend’s round-up of winners with a 1-0 victory over Dreams FC. Malik Abubakar scored the decisive goal, giving Karela their third consecutive home win.

Ghana News.title: Ntiamoah Foundation launches “BEYOND 20” anniversary campaign
Ghana News.content:
Ntiamoah Foundation has launched BEYOND 20: From Impact to Legacy, a year-long campaign marking two decades of improving lives through education, health, and community development, while setting out its vision for the future.

Established in 2006 by the Entrepreneur, Robert Kwaku Appiah Asante (R.K.A. Asante), Ntiamoah Foundation has worked primarily with communities in the Birim North and Birim South Districts of the Eastern Region. Its interventions span early childhood literacy, Reading Clubs and libraries, ICT education, scholarships, menstrual and maternal health, support for health facilities, and community outreach.

Over the past two decades, the Ntiamoah Foundation has invested over GH¢23 million in today’s value in improving access to education, healthcare and community support. This investment has supported 34 schools and nearly 6,500 young readers, strengthened 14 Community-based health planning and services (CHPS) facilities, supported 436 life-changing surgeries and reached over 8,000 girls through menstrual health programmes, to name a few. Together, these achievements reflect a 20-year commitment to creating opportunities and improving lives in underserved communities.

Launching the anniversary campaign, Executive Director Mercy Quansah-Ansah said the milestone provides an opportunity to reflect on the Foundation’s impact and set the direction for its next chapter.

“Twenty years gives us much to celebrate, but BEYOND 20 is also about asking what we can put in place today that will still be changing lives twenty years from now. For us, that is the shift from impact to legacy: creating opportunities today that can continue to transform lives for generations to come.”

As part of the campaign launch, the Foundation has unveiled a 20th-anniversary identity and redesigned website, which will serve as a platform for impact stories, programme updates, anniversary activities and opportunities for individuals and organisations to support its work.

Building the Next Chapter

Throughout the anniversary year, Ntiamoah Foundation will continue its established education and health programmes while introducing three flagship initiatives designed to turn twenty years of impact into a legacy.

Programme B.E.A.M. will become the Foundation's flagship education model, bringing together literacy, life skills, creativity, digital learning, leadership and community support to develop confident, ethical and future-ready young people. It builds on two decades of investment in Reading Clubs, libraries, ICT and other educational interventions.

The Foundation will also launch the R.K.A. Asante Scholarship Scheme, a permanent programme established in honour of its founder. Beyond financial support, the scheme will combine scholarships with mentorship, leadership and professional development and community service. To commemorate the 20th anniversary, 20 for 20 Awards will select the first twenty scholars, creating the inaugural cohort of what the Foundation hopes will become a lifelong community of future leaders committed to giving back.

The third flagship initiative is the Legacy Project, a long-term investment in community spaces and infrastructure that will continue serving people beyond the anniversary year. The project will create spaces to preserve local history and heritage, advance learning and leadership, and build skills and opportunities for young people. It will also include recreational infrastructure, beginning with 3 multipurpose community centres to promote youth development, healthy lifestyles and community connection.

Board Chair Dr. Kojo Pumpuni Asante said the next chapter will require an even broader community of partners: “Ntiamoah's journey has always been built on partnership. As we look beyond twenty, we invite individuals, institutions and organisations who share our belief in the power of education and health to join us. The next chapter is about multiplying opportunity and building something that future generations can inherit and build upon.”

Derek Boateng, Senior Manager for Sustainability and External Relations for Zijin Golden Ridge Limited, one of the Foundation's longstanding partners, congratulated Ntiamoah Foundation on the milestone:

“Over the years, we have witnessed Ntiamoah Foundation's commitment to improving educational outcomes, strengthening healthcare delivery and creating opportunities for vulnerable communities. Its impact can be seen not only in the projects delivered, but in the lives transformed. We congratulate the Foundation on twenty years of service and look forward to continuing our partnership.”

A Year of Celebration and Legacy

BEYOND 20 will spotlight the people, partnerships and communities that have shaped Ntiamoah Foundation's journey, while mobilising support for its next chapter.

The anniversary year will culminate in a Fundraising Gala Dinner and Thanksgiving Service in December, bringing together partners, donors, community leaders, beneficiaries and other stakeholders to celebrate twenty years of service and support the Foundation's future programmes.

BEYOND 20 is both a celebration of what has been achieved and an invitation to help build what comes next.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: UK PM Andy Burnham says it is ‘clear’ Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
World.content:
The claim marks the first time a UK prime minister has publicly acknowledged Russia’s interference in the vote to leave the EU.

Share UK PM Andy Burnham says it is ‘clear’ Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote on social media

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said it is “clear” that Russia interfered in the country’s 2016 Brexit vote, warning French and German voters of the same threat.

“I asked the question coming to Downing Street: Was there interference in the 2016 referendum from Russia? And I’ve had the clear answer that yes, there was,” Burnham said in an interview with The Rest Is Politics podcast released on Sunday.

Burnham’s comments mark the first time a UK prime minister has publicly acknowledged that Russia interfered in the UK’s vote to leave the European Union. Burnham did not provide evidence for or details on the claim.

He said that “these things are important now to put clearly on the record, and, I believe, help voters in Germany and France understand that some of this politics is instigated via our enemies, namely Russia.”

Burnham said he spoke with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz about possible links between Russia and the far-right Alternative for Germany party when the two leaders met last week in Berlin.

In his address to the United Nations General Assembly in September, Burnham also condemned Russia’s attempt to interfere in the UK’s 2019 general election.

According to a 2020 report by Parliament’s Intelligence and Security Committee, the UK government had failed to ask for a deep assessment of Russia’s interference in the 2016 referendum. The report did confirm that Russia had meddled in the 2014 Scottish independence referendum, however.

Russia has repeatedly denied meddling in Western democracies or interfering in another country’s elections or referendums, casting the UK as being gripped by “anti-Russian hysteria”.



UK reconsiders Brexit

Last month, Burnham argued that the UK should reconsider options for a future relationship with the EU, including rejoining the bloc, reigniting the decisive debate more than a decade after the historic vote.

He said that the UK’s departure from the bloc had failed to fulfil Brexit supporters’ pledge of “taking back control”, and instead has made the UK weaker economically and on immigration.

World.title: Iran’s FM urges diplomacy in call with Saudi counterpart
World.content:
Tehran offers to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis following deadly strikes on the kingdom.

Saudi Arabian Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud has received a phone call from his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, the Saudi state news agency reported.

The two ministers discussed the recent escalations in the region after the Houthis, backed by Iran, attacked Saudi airports.

In a post on Telegram on Sunday, Araghchi emphasised that insisting on a military approach while disregarding political solutions would further complicate the situation. The Iranian minister said the region’s crises have no military solutions. Last week, Araghchi said “there is no military solution” to the US war, adding, “only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict.

Araghchi said Iran is ready to provide any assistance necessary to facilitate the start of dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen and to help achieve a political solution.

Following the deadly attack on the Riyadh airport that killed 12 people and wounded 300, US President Donald Trump said he would reconsider the US role in Yemen, adding that he is weighing resuming strikes on Iran.

These remarks represent a departure from the president’s comments on Thursday that Washington will not resume strikes on Iran until after the US midterm elections.

Iranian and Saudi diplomatic ties have endured despite longstanding friction, with embassies restored under a 2023 Chinese-brokered agreement remaining operational. Before that breakthrough, a seven-year diplomatic rupture had fuelled regional proxy conflicts.



Riyadh’s relationship with Tehran has deteriorated since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran in late February. Following the attacks, Tehran and its aligned forces have struck US military assets and energy infrastructure across the Gulf region, including oil fields in Saudi Arabia.

In March 2026, Prince Faisal warned Iran that tolerance of its attacks on Saudi Arabia and those of neighbouring Gulf states is limited, calling on Tehran to “recalculate” its strategy.

World.title: Hurricane Isaias leaves trail of destruction across the US Gulf Coast
World.content:
Residents across the southeastern United States have begun cleanup efforts after Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic tropical cyclone of the 2026 season, slammed ashore near Destin, Florida, on Friday.

As of midafternoon Sunday, roughly 356,000 customers remain without power in southern Alabama and the northwestern region of Florida, according to data from PowerOutage.com, an independent tracking website.

At its peak, the storm knocked out power to nearly 800,000 homes and businesses across the Gulf Coast.

Sarah Gatewood, a spokesperson for the utility company Florida Power and Light (FPL), announced that workers from across Florida and more than two dozen other states had mobilised to restore power.

At least four deaths have been linked to Isais after it made landfall as a Category 2 storm on the five-tier Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.

The tempest churned northward into Alabama on Saturday with fierce tropical-storm-force winds before weakening into a post-tropical cyclone and tracking further north towards the Appalachians.

Though its power is waning, the storm continues to endanger the mid-Atlantic region with the potential for flash flooding.

According to the National Weather Service (NWS), surface observations indicate that Isaias now has maximum sustained winds of 160 km/h (100 mph) and an estimated minimum central pressure of 28.88 inches, or 978 millibars.

Across Florida and Alabama, residents have reported damage from the storm’s high-velocity winds.

A Rest and Relax Inn in the resort city of Pensacola, Florida, saw its roof sheared off during the hurricane, and a boathouse was flattened in Destin.



The immediate struggle for basic necessities was most stark in Pensacola, the westernmost part of the Florida Panhandle, where the storm downed power grids and caused widespread structural damage.

Hundreds of cars lined the block around a United Cajun Navy distribution site, a volunteer disaster relief organisation, on Saturday morning.

Pensacola’s Mayor DC Reeves warned of critical drinking water shortages following the storm, which affected drinking wells and water infrastructure. Residents, he said, remain under an advisory to boil tap water before use.

“We are winding down day three of storm response and recovery operations, and we remain focused on public safety, clearing debris, and restoring critical infrastructure and services,” Reeves said on social media.

Isaias also forced the indefinite closure of Pensacola International airport, Florida’s 10th-largest airfield, due to severe damage.

Fallen trees and power lines continue to make travel hazardous in Houston County, Alabama, which remains under an emergency flash flood warning, according to state emergency officials.

“Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice,” the agency posted on X.

World.title: Ceuta or Sebta? Why one city has two names and a disputed status
World.content:
Felipe VI’s first visit to Ceuta and Melilla as king brings Spain’s territorial dispute with Morocco back into focus.

Share Ceuta or Sebta? Why one city has two names and a disputed status on social media

Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia are due to visit Ceuta on October 13 and Melilla the following day, in Felipe’s first visit to either city as king since he ascended the throne in 2014.

The trip comes after a major migration crisis at the Ceuta border in July and as the long-running dispute between Spain and Morocco over the two cities on the North African coast remains unresolved.

Spain considers Ceuta and Melilla part of its territory, while Morocco regards both cities and several smaller Spanish-held territories in North Africa as part of its own territory.

The city that sits on the southern side of the Strait of Gibraltar also has different names in Spanish and Arabic.

In Spain, it is Ceuta. In Arabic, it is Sabta, commonly written as Sebta in Latin script.

So why does the same city have two names? And how did a city on the North African coast come under Spanish sovereignty?

Where does the name Ceuta come from?

The name is much older than either modern Spain or Morocco.

The city was known as Sabta in Arabic. Spain’s Ministry of Culture identifies Sabta with present-day Ceuta and traces its history through successive periods of Idrisid, Umayyad, Taifa, Almoravid, Almohad and Marinid rule.

The Spanish form, Ceuta, developed from earlier forms of the name. Sabta and Ceuta are different linguistic forms of the same city.

Who controlled Ceuta before Spain?

Ceuta passed through several political and dynastic systems in the Maghreb and al-Andalus.

Under the Idrisid dynasty, the city was in the hands of the Banu Isam before being taken by the Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Rahman III in 931, bringing it into the political sphere of al-Andalus.



In the 11th century, Ceuta became linked to the Taifa of Malaga. It later came under the Almoravids and Almohads. From the beginning of the 14th century, it became part of the Marinid sphere with periods when other local dynasties held power.

By the early 15th century, Ceuta was under Muslim rule.

That changed in 1415.

How did Ceuta become Portuguese?

On August 21, 1415, Portuguese forces led by King John I captured Ceuta.

The Portuguese conquest brought an end to more than seven centuries of Muslim rule in Ceuta. Ceuta’s own cultural heritage authority dates Muslim rule from 709 to the Portuguese conquest in 1415.

Ceuta remained Portuguese for more than two centuries.

Portugal and Spain were then ruled by the same monarchy from 1580 to 1640. When Portugal restored its independence in 1640, Ceuta remained under the Spanish monarchy rather than returning to Portuguese rule.

The 1668 Treaty of Lisbon, which formally recognised Portuguese independence, left Ceuta in Spanish hands.

That is how Ceuta came under Spanish sovereignty.

Why does Morocco claim Ceuta?

Morocco’s argument is rooted in the city’s history and geography.

Ceuta lies on the North African coast, surrounded by Morocco on its landward side. Morocco has claimed Ceuta and Melilla since gaining independence in 1956 and regards the two cities as occupied Moroccan territories.

Spain takes the opposite position.

Under Spanish law, Ceuta is an autonomous city. Its Statute of Autonomy describes Ceuta as an integral part of the Spanish nation and gives the city its own system of self-government.

The dispute, therefore, is not about who administers Ceuta. Spain does. It is about sovereignty.

Morocco says Ceuta should form part of Moroccan territory. Spain says its sovereignty over the city is established and Ceuta is part of Spain.

Neither side has accepted the other’s position.

Why doesn’t history settle the dispute?

Because the two sides interpret that history differently.

Morocco points to Ceuta’s long history within Muslim political systems in the Maghreb and its location on the North African coast. Spain points to centuries of Portuguese and Spanish control and to Ceuta’s present constitutional status as part of Spain.

The historical record does not provide a simple answer to a modern sovereignty dispute. The political systems that ruled Ceuta before 1415 were not nation-states with today’s borders, and the city’s current status is based on centuries of subsequent Portuguese and Spanish rule.

Morocco’s territorial claim dates from the period after independence in 1956, but Spain has continued to exercise sovereignty over Ceuta.



Why does Morocco call it Sebta?

Sebta, or Sabta, is the Arabic name for Ceuta and predates the modern sovereignty dispute.

In Morocco, Sebta is the Arabic name used for the city while Ceuta is the established Spanish form.

The choice of name can have political resonance because Morocco disputes Spanish sovereignty over the city. But using Sebta is not automatically a political statement. It is also simply the Arabic name.

What about Melilla?

Melilla’s history is different from Ceuta’s.

Spanish forces took control of Melilla in 1497 when it was incorporated into the Crown of Castile.

Ceuta, by contrast, was first Portuguese before remaining under the Spanish monarchy after Portugal regained its independence.

Today, both cities are Spanish autonomous cities, and Morocco claims sovereignty over both.

Why does Ceuta still matter?

Ceuta’s importance today goes beyond its size.

Ceuta is considered part of Spain, but it is not included in the European Union customs territory. Its border with Morocco is also an external border of the Schengen area.

That has made Ceuta a focal point for migration and border policy as well as a recurring issue in relations between Madrid and Rabat.

The issue returned sharply to the headlines on July 30 when more than 72,000 migrants entered Ceuta from Morocco, according to the Reuters news agency.

Now Felipe’s planned visits to Ceuta and Melilla are putting the two disputed cities back in the spotlight.
