World.title: US Homeland Security secretary sees no ‘risk’ from livestreamed execution
World.content:
The decision to livestream Nidal Hasan’s execution has triggered harsh criticism and warnings that it could encourage radicalisation.

Share US Homeland Security secretary sees no ‘risk’ from livestreamed execution on social media

United States Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has defended the planned livestreaming of Nidal Hasan’s execution, playing down warnings that images of his death by firing squad might be used as a propaganda tool for violent groups.

In an interview on Sunday with the CBS News show Face the Nation, Mullin framed the decision as part of President Donald Trump’s hardline approach to crime.

“I follow President Trump. He’s a commander-in chief of the country,” Mullin said, crediting the Republican leader with “restoring America values”.

Mullin also brushed aside concerns that the images of Hasan’s execution could be leveraged against the US.

“I don’t see an elevated risk at this point at all because of this,” Mullin said. “I think people need to understand, if you attack America, we will come after you, and we will make sure that the punishment fits the crime.”

Hasan, a former US Army major, was sentenced to death in August 2013 after being convicted of shooting and killing 12 unarmed active-duty soldiers and a retired serviceman at the Fort Hood military base in Texas.

The attack took place on November 5, 2009, when Hasan opened fire in a medical facility on the base where service members receive routine check-ups before deployment. The incident is considered one of the deadliest mass shootings to take place on a US military base.

Another 32 people were injured in the shooting. In the process of responding to the attack, police on the military base shot Hasan, leaving him paralysed from the waist down.



Critics have questioned the optics of broadcasting a firing squad killing of a man in a wheelchair. The livestreamed execution is scheduled for December 3.

But Mullin dismissed those concerns, arguing that viewership is optional. “Once again, no one has to watch it if they don’t choose to,” Mullin said.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth had announced plans last week to livestream the upcoming execution, triggering a wave of criticism. But Trump on Saturday suggested he may reconsider the decision.

“There are two thoughts: Don’t show it and show it. Because, you know, by showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did,” Trump told reporters outside the White House.

“So I’ll make a decision, ultimately. I know what the military would like to do, but we’ll make a decision.”

Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle, however, have denounced the idea of a public execution.

In a Sunday morning appearance on NBC’s Meet the Press, Republican Senator Thom Tillis warned that broadcasting Hasan’s death would “put at risk” US lives.

“Terrorist organisations will use this as a recruiting tool. It will radicalise other people, and this is not who we are,” Tillis said.

“Look, the Fort Hood shooter should be put to death, but there’s a way to deal with this that’s proper, and there’s a way to deal with this that’s more improper than I have ever observed in my life.”

Tillis, whose term as senator ends in January, also directed criticism at Hegseth for what he suggested was reckless leadership.

“It’s another example of why Pete Hegseth and all of his bravado needs to get the hell out of the Department of Defense, because he is a failed leader,” Tillis said.

The senator was considered one of the deciding votes in Hegseth’s January 2025 confirmation vote, and he has since called his support for Hegseth’s cabinet nomination “the biggest regret” of his tenure.

Other Republicans echoed Tillis’s concerns about the livestream. Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, for instance, compared the public execution with something she would expect “from terrorists and dictators”.

She also argued that Hasan has sought public attention, something he would receive in a broadcast execution.

“It would give this individual, who deserves no further notoriety, the martyrdom he seeks,” Murkowski added.

Republican Representative Tom Barrett of Michigan, a former military member, issued a statement on Friday explaining that he had trained at Fort Hood a year before the attack.



He also said he opposed the public execution, despite considering Hasan “evil”.

“Secretary Hegseth should seriously reconsider this decision,” Barrett wrote on X.

“Making a public spectacle out of an already tragic situation is unnecessary and does not serve a public interest.”

Military executions are extremely rare in the US and can only be approved by the president under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.

If the order against Hasan is carried out, he will be the first member of the US military to be executed since 1961.

World.title: Palestinian Authority Says Elections Are to Be Postponed
World.content:
The Palestinian Authority in the Israeli-occupied West Bank informed France this week that legislative elections in the territory scheduled for Nov. 28 would be postponed by several months, according to two Palestinian officials briefed on the communications.

The message was conveyed in a letter to the French foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, from Hussein al-Sheikh, deputy to the Palestinian Authority president, Mahmoud Abbas, the officials said. Reuters first reported on the letter.

A postponement of the elections would come as Fatah, the governing party in of the PA, suffers from division, especially over Mr. Abbas’s increasingly authoritarian rule. Israel, which controls whether ballot boxes or election observers can enter Gaza, has also shown little readiness to facilitate the voting. That lack of engagement complicates the work of the Palestinian Authority’s election commission, according to three Western diplomats.

The Palestinian officials and Western diplomats spoke to The New York Times on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly on the sensitive matters.

World.title: Trump's 'energy ceasefire' claim welcomed by Zelensky but Russia silent
World.content:
Donald Trump has claimed that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an "energy ceasefire", with Kyiv saying it would support such a move but Moscow yet to comment.

The US president insisted that it was "effective immediately" but provided no details.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky initially expressed surprise at the announcement, before saying Kyiv would support it if Moscow did. He also accused Russia of striking Ukrainian energy facilities after Trump's post.

Trump has been urging Ukraine to stop strikes on Russian oil infrastructure - which Kyiv says are vital to curtailing revenue for Moscow's war machine - so Russia can fulfil a recently-struck deal to release diesel to the US and the global market.

The diesel deal, temporarily undoing sanctions on Russian imports, is attracting growing criticism. Zelensky called it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. European officials and some US politicians, including from Trump's Republican party, have said they do not support it.

The deal is Trump's latest effort to lower domestic fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections, having spent months grappling with the political consequences of the war with Iran which has pushed up global fuel prices, particularly those for diesel.

That has soured Trump's standing with the American public, who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation.

World.title: One killed, 11 injured in second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport in two days
World.content:
One person has been killed and 11 injured in a second strike on the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, officials have said.

A Saudi military spokesman said a projectile had hit King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, causing a fire in one of its passenger halls. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said in a statement on X that one person, a Pakistani resident, had been killed in the attack.

It comes a day after a strike on the same airport killed 13 people and injured 308 others, following similar strikes earlier this week.

The Houthis in Yemen said they were behind the attacks and warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi Arabian airports and airspace.

The group said they had targeted the airport with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones in the past 24 hours.

They also attacked oil facilities and Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, their military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree said.

He vowed to continue the "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia", warning that all Saudi airports were potential targets apart from those in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

The Houthis have said they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war, as well as an air strike on the airport in Sanaa.

On Sunday Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition, said air defences had intercepted a missile near the airport in Riyadh, while authorities were dealing with the fire caused by an "unknown projectile" that hit Passenger Hall No 4.

US President Donald Trump has said the US would "make a decision" and "move very quickly" on whether to strike the Houthis, while UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting suggested the UK could "potentially" provide more support for Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Tusk
World.content:
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a man accused of plotting an assassination attack against him and his defence minister has been detained.

The interior ministry earlier reported that police had received credible information about possible attacks against Tusk and Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.

Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about the planned attacks, with a spokesman saying officials were treating the threat as "deadly serious".

Tusk thanked the police for "swift and decisive action" in arresting the suspect.

The suspect was arrested in the Lower Silesia region and was a Polish national, Jacek Dobrzynski, a spokesman for the Special Services Co-ordinator told local media.

"In this case we are talking about a strong likelihood that these threats could actually be carried out," he said.

The plan was uncovered when an email with information about the potential attack was forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security, Interior Ministry spokeswoman Karolina Galecka said.

Tusk has been Polish prime minister since 2023, having previously held the office from 2007 to 2014.

He served as president of the European Council from 2014 to 2019.

World.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
World.content:
At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says.

Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining sites in Sudan's River Nile state on Saturday.

Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented.

Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border.

Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region.

"The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday. "These acts may constitute war crimes."

It noted that its death toll was provisional and could rise.

The Paris-based Sudan Tribune reported that the death toll could far exceed the number reported by Emergency Lawyers, citing a survivor of Saturday's attack who said many more people had been injured.

Eyewitnesses said the attack began around 06:00 local time (04:00 GMT), with the aircraft firing more than five missiles directly at the miners' camps, destroying them and excavation pits with people still inside, the newspaper wrote.

The Sudan Tribune reported claims in June that Egyptian forces had used drones and artillery to target artisanal mining sites in the same region, killing several, after sporadic incidents of Egyptian border guards of burning equipment, torching temporary shelters, and firing live ammunition to disperse mine workers.

Days later, Egypt's border agency announced that it and the military had begun a sweeping security campaign along the border to foil illegal migration, drug smuggling and illegal mining.

At the same time, Sudan's de facto leader announced an investigation into the alleged strikes, which were said to have killed dozens.

Gold lies at the core of the border tensions.

Sudan's ongoing civil war has led to a surge in artisanal mining - an often risky practice conducted by civilians with rudimentary tools and without official permission - particularly in remote areas near its borders.

Gold-rich areas such as those in River Nile state lie along porous borders in terrain historically associated with cross-border smuggling routes, with artisanally mined gold potentially feeding into those channels.

Egypt's border force said in June that it had seized 86 tonnes of gold ore along with amateur prospecting equipment.

Artisanal mining has also reportedly continued in Sudan's conflict zones and smuggled gold may be a source of income for armed insurgent groups.

This has raised concerns of illicit Sudanese gold undermining the legitimate Egyptian gold market.

World.title: Homes and bridges swept away as fresh floods hit Nepal
World.content:
A major river in Nepal has flooded, sweeping away houses, bridges and damaging a part of hydropower station, authorities have said.

Around 50 people have been rescued from along the bank of the Budhi Gandaki River in the central Gorkha district, the army confirmed. No casualties have been reported yet, however five people are missing.

A video of the flood shows the moment raging waters sweep down a valley and wash away an entire building complex.

Nepal is on high alert and still trying to recover from catastrophic floods that hit its border towns with Tibet two months ago, leaving more than 1,400 people dead and thousands missing.

Sunday's flood tore through the Gorkha district as children and communities prepared to mark the first day of the Dashain festival, a major moment in the Nepali calendar.

Families have been forced to flee their homes, with many facing uncertainty over where they will find safe shelter and access to essential supplies.

The flood swept away about a dozen houses and several suspension bridges, while a hydroelectric project was damaged, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.

Within a couple of hours, the river's water levels at one location had risen from two metres (6ft 5in) to nearly 8.5m (27ft 9in), officials said.

Binod Parajuli, a meteorologist who works with the Nepalese government, said: "Our hydrological station was swept away and we are not getting any data from that location."

However, experts say the debris-flow is much smaller and travelled more slowly than the devastating flash floods in August.

What caused the latest flood is still unclear. Some say a landslide may have blocked the river or its tributary for some time, causing the dammed water to burst out, while others say locals upstream saw an ice-avalanche.

Save the Children is mobilising an emergency team to respond to Sunday's flood.

"Children's lives have been ripped apart in an instant yet again", the charity's director in Nepal, Tara Chettry, said.

"We are yet to see the full scale of the damage, but they may have lost their homes, schools and communities. Many children in Gorkha will still be in shock and distress after the mega floods in August, barely having a chance to get back on their feet."

The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli river, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused the previous disaster.

World.title: Ukraine strikes Yandex data centre in third attack on Russian tech giant
World.content:
Yandex has been forced to pause its operations at a data centre near Moscow after the facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone strike - the third attack on the Russian tech giant's sites this week.

The company - dubbed "Russia's Google" - said no one was injured at the centre in Vladimir, east of the capital, but some of its services were unavailable to users.

Earlier this week, Yandex said it was struggling to maintain its services after two of its five data centres were hit in Ukrainian strikes.

Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks on infrastructure in recent months as the war between them continues in its fifth year following Russia's full-scale invasion.

Kyiv said it was targeting places that provide revenue streams for Moscow's war machine, and that the attacks could force Russia to divert its resources to repair the damage at Yandex.

Sunday's attack came hours after US President Donald Trump warned that Ukraine should "damn well stop" attacking Russia's oil refineries so Moscow could release more diesel to the global market - a deal that has drawn criticism from Europe and sparked a diplomatic row with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky.

World.title: Orangutans released back into Borneo forest after devastating fires
World.content:
Eight orangutans have been released back into the wild in Borneo after they were taken into captivity when their habitat was threatened by wildfires over the summer.

Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday, International Animal Rescue Indonesia (Yiari) and the forestry ministry said.

Indonesian authorities rescued 46 orangutans from fires in August and September. Wildfires in the region are usual for the country's dry season but intensified this year.

The apes are critically endangered. Around 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago, according to conservation group WWF.

While Indonesia is among many countries to grapple with wildfires each summer, this year's were more intense due to the El NiÃ±o ocean warming phenomenon, which makes weather patterns more volatile and intense.

Yiari CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said relocating the eight orangutans to the reserve was a "necessary step" when their habitats became unsafe.

Among them was Mama Nopi and her offspring Nopi, Naufal and Nopan, who had been surviving in a coconut and rubber plantation before their rescue in early September, Yiari said.

Fires had incinerated the surrounding forestry, restricting their access to food and bringing them closer to humans.

World.title: Poland stabbings driven by online glorification of violence, Tusk says
World.content:
Three violent attacks at Polish schools this week were driven by the "glorification of violence" online, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

The attacks have left one woman dead and others injured, including children.

"These are very often spontaneous actions inspired by online activity," Tusk said on Sunday, during a crisis meeting with security services.

Police have arrested 117 people across the country for possession knives or other weapons, or for threatening to attack schools or fellow students, after searching tens of thousands of schools.

A woman was arrested on Saturday after injuring three people while attacking a 17-year-old girl at an educational institution in the capital, Warsaw.

It came a day after thousands of police visited schools across Poland, following two stabbing attacks earlier in the week, one of which led to the killing of a female caretaker.

"We are not dealing with any group organized on a big scale," Tusk said on Sunday.

"In the past years and months, we have noted - globally and in Poland - a rise in the fascination with violence," he added.

The prime minister said the attacks were acts of "nihilistic violence" associated with the extreme right.

"Some of the people detained are active in the ultraright environment," he said, adding that police had noticed a rise in online searches of Nazi content as well as of "mass killers who have become idols online".

On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student attacked and injured nine people at a vocational school in the central Polish province of Mazovian.

A day later, the 37-year-old caretaker was killed after a 15-year-old entered a primary school in LeszczydÃ³Å-Nowiny, north of Warsaw.

Interior Minister Marcin KierwiÅski also said a 17-year-old was detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, after allegedly stating "on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone".

Thousands of Polish âpolice officers visited schools nationwide to try to reassure pupils after the stabbings sparked rumours of a "Bloody Friday" of more attacks stemming from a supposed online challenge.

Meanwhile, Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said.

A special services spokesman said officials were treating the threat as "deadly serious".

World.title: 2027: Nigerian governor urges residents to reject election-season promises by politicians
World.content:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State has urged voters to resist financial and material inducements from politicians, warning that such offers could undermine the state’s future in the 2027 general elections.

Mr Otti gave the advice on Sunday at the 2nd Session of the 7th Synod of the Anglican Communion, Diocese of Aba Ngwa North, held at All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Abayi-Umuocham, Aba.

The governor, represented by his Chief of Staff, Caleb Ajagba, charged citizens to prioritise long-term development over immediate material benefits offered by politicians.

He alleged that politicians responsible for the state’s challenges over 24 years were returning to seek voters’ support.

Mr Otti warned against allowing such politicians to derail the progress his administration was pursuing.

“The people that created a problem that God now had to answer your prayer by sending someone after His own heart, are all over again.

“But the Bible says surely they shall proceed no further. Please, let us be careful. When God opens a door, may we not close it.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Don’t use the ₦5,000, the ₦10,000, the wrapper or the rice they will give you and close the destiny of Abians for the next four years, because even prayer and fasting will not open it.

“May we not lose what God has given to us on the platter,” he said.

Call for vigilance

Governor Otti also urged Christians to remain vigilant, warning that some politicians who previously neglected the Church were seeking its attention.

“Like we have been told the season is here again and politicians are everywhere and as the Bible says we are not ignorant of the devices of the enemy.

“These are devices because many of them who have not been coming to church have started coming to church.

“Many of them who have not been accepting or taking your calls have suddenly started calling you. If you call them and you miss their call, they call you back. Those are devices,” he said.

Mr Otti said the first three years of his administration had focused largely on laying a foundation for development, adding that the next four years, beginning in 2027, would prioritise consolidation.

“Those who build houses will understand that foundation-laying is the most crucial, and the foundation has been laid after 24 years of ruins.

“What will now be happening is consolidation and beauty will emerge.

“This present house (Abia State) you are seeing today, in the next four years, you will know that God has really come to tabernacle in the midst of man.

“Today Abia State has become a point of reference,” he said.

On the church’s development projects, Mr Otti assured the congregation of his administration’s support towards their completion.

He, however, reiterated that public funds should be deployed to develop the state rather than finance religious projects.

The governor commended the guest speaker for delivering what he described as an appropriate and unadulterated message, urging Christians to verify information and examine issues critically before reaching conclusions.

He said the synod’s theme, “Don’t Just Absorb It; Think It Through,” drawn from Acts Chapter 17 verse 11 to 12, was relevant as the country approached another political season.

“As Christians, we have the capacity to change the negative narrative of this nation; especially our state,” he said.

The sermon

Earlier, the Bishop of Aba Ngwa North Diocese, Anglican Communion, Nathan Kanu, said the theme challenged Christians to move beyond hearing messages to examining issues prayerfully and responding wisely.

Mr Kanu commended Governor Otti for identifying with the church and supporting its activities, presented gifts to the governor’s representative and prayed for God’s blessings on his administration.

In his sermon, the Guest Speaker and Bishop of Ohaji/Egbema Diocese, Chidi Oparajiaku, urged Christians to think critically before taking action.

Speaking on: “The Bereans Wisdom,” with his text from Acts, chapter 17, verse 12 and 15, Mr Oparajiaku said the synod’s theme was timely and encouraged believers to examine messages rather than accept or reject them without reflection.

“The theme of the synod is very important and apt in this our time, it didn’t say throw it away, it says think through it,” he said.

Mr Oparajiaku regretted that Christians, who were expected to demonstrate sound judgement, sometimes fell victim to deception.

“When members of the church know the Bible, they would not be deceived.

“This is because the church refused to behave like the Bereans. The Bereans Christian never took everything for granted they always thought through whatever they heard,” he said.

The bishop thanked God for giving Abia the opportunity to be governed by Mr Otti, whom he credited with changing the fortunes of the state.

The synod attracted dignitaries, including the Labour Party’s National Vice-Chairman, South-East, Ishmael Onuoha; state chairman, Peter Azubuike; and Osisioma Local Government Area Chairman, Chidi Agu.

Others were the Special Assistant to Governor Otti on Special Duties, George Chiedozie; Special Adviser on Labour Matters, Godson Anucha; and Aba industrialist, Bob Udeagha.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: 241 candidates jostle for 36 elective positions in Cross River
World.content:
No fewer than 241 candidates of various political parties have been cleared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to contest 36 elective positions in Cross River State in the 2027 general elections.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the positions comprise the governorship, Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly seats.

According to INEC’s final list of candidates, eight candidates are vying for the governorship seat, 25 for the three senatorial seats, 63 for the eight House of Representatives seats, and 145 for the 24 State House of Assembly seats.

NAN reports that out of the 241 candidates, 198 are males representing 82.2 per cent, while 43 are females, representing 17.8 per cent.

The Calabar South State Constituency has the highest number of female candidates—seven of them.

NAN also reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) each fielded five female candidates for the upcoming general election.

NAN further reports that although 14 political parties are participating in the elections in the state, only the APC, ADC and NDC fielded candidates for all the elective positions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The youngest candidate NAN investigation shows is 26-year-old Aboh Glady, who is contesting for the State House of Assembly seat on the platform of the Action Alliance (AA).

The oldest candidates are 69-year-old Asuquo Asuquo and Francis Ukpanyang, both of the Action Democratic Party (ADP), contesting for Calabar Municipal/Odukpani Federal Constituency and Calabar South State Constituency, respectively.

It will be recalled that five members of the National Assembly (NASS) representing Cross River failed to secure their parties’ tickets to seek re-election in 2027.

Cross River has 11 representatives at the National Assembly, comprising three senators and eight House of Representatives members, all of them members of the ruling APC.

Two of the three senators secured the APC tickets for the 2027 elections, while only three of the eight House of Representatives members seeking re-election succeeded in clinching their party’s tickets.

The successful House of Representatives members are Joseph Bassey, Calabar South/Akpabuyo/Bakassi Federal Constituency; Peter Akpanke, Obudu/Bekwarra/Obanliku Federal Constituency and Victor Abang, Ikom/Boki Federal Constituency.

Those who lost their bids for re-election are Emil Inyang, Biase/Akamkpa Federal Constituency; Bassey Akiba, Calabar Municipal/Odukpani Federal Constituency; Godwin Offiono, Yala/Ogoja Federal Constituency; and Mike Etaba, Obubra/Etung Federal Constituency.

However, Alex Egbona, representing Yakurr/Abi Federal Constituency, defected to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) shortly before the APC primaries.

World.title: NPFL Roundup: Plateau United thrash Kano Pillars as Rangers cling to top spot
World.content:
Plateau United delivered the standout result of Matchday 8 of the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) season with a 4-0 thrashing of Kano Pillars, while Rangers International retained top spot after rescuing a late 2-2 draw against Barau FC.

Rangers moved to 17 points from eight matches, just one point ahead of Rivers United, who maintained their unbeaten start with a goalless draw against Abia Warriors.

Plateau United climbed to third place with 14 points following their emphatic victory, while Sporting Lagos, Warri Wolves and Nasarawa United also recorded important wins in an eventful round of fixtures.

Plateau United punish Kano Pillars

Plateau United produced one of their most convincing performances of the campaign, scoring four goals without reply against Kano Pillars.

Paul Samson opened the scoring after just three minutes, giving the hosts an early advantage. Kano Pillars struggled to contain Plateau United, who doubled their lead through Ekundayo Ojo in first-half stoppage time.

Samuel Ayanrinde added a third in the 82nd minute before Nenrot Silas converted a penalty in the 90th minute to complete the rout.

The result lifted Plateau United to 14 points and third place in the standings, strengthening their early-season challenge.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

For Kano Pillars, the defeat was a significant setback. The former champions remained on 11 points on 10th position

Rangers survive Barau scare

Rangers needed a late equaliser to preserve their position at the top after playing out a 2-2 draw against Barau FC in Kano.

Ifeanyi Okechukwu put the visitors ahead in the 38th minute, but Joseph Atule equalised for Barau from the penalty spot in the 56th minute.

Aliyu Sugau converted another penalty 12 minutes later to give the hosts the lead.

Rangers, however, refused to leave empty-handed, with Chidiebere Nwobodo scoring in the 90th minute to secure a point.

The draw took Rangers to 17 points from eight matches, keeping them narrowly ahead of Rivers United.

Rivers maintained their unbeaten record after a 0-0 draw with Abia Warriors, moving to 16 points and remaining firmly in contention for the top position.

Sporting Lagos fight back

Sporting Lagos came from behind to defeat Bendel Insurance 2-1 after conceding within the opening minute.

Bendel Insurance striker Kayode Oke scored after just 18 seconds, putting the visitors ahead almost immediately.

Sporting responded through Victor Samuel in the 14th minute before Gafar Olaniyan completed the comeback eight minutes later.

The victory lifted Sporting Lagos to 12 points level with Insurance.

Ikorodu City, Nasarawa United claim wins

Ikorodu City strengthened their position in the top half of the table with a 2-0 victory over Kwara United.

Kwara United finished with 10 players after Saheed Olaniyi was sent off in the 86th minute for a second bookable offence.

Nasarawa United also secured a 2-0 win, defeating Doma United through goals from Sunday Dapman in the 10th minute and Jofrank Istifanus, who converted a penalty in the 55th minute.

Kun Khalifat FC recorded another 2-0 victory, overcoming Shooting Stars to collect three points in their campaign.

Warri Wolves boost survival bid

Warri Wolves earned a valuable 3-1 victory over Inter Lagos as both sides sought to improve their positions in the standings.

The result provided a boost for Wolves, while Inter Lagos were left with work to do after the defeat.

Elsewhere, Ranchers Bees and Niger Tornadoes played out a goalless draw despite the hosts being reduced to 10 players.

Habibu Yakubu received a straight red card for impeding a goal-bound move, but Niger Tornadoes were unable to capitalise on their numerical advantage, even with eight minutes of added time.

Enyimba suffer another setback

Enyimba’s difficult start continued with a 4-2 defeat to Katsina United.

The loss left the former African champions with seven points from eight matches and deep in the relegation zone.

With Rangers and Rivers United separated by just one point and Plateau United moving into third place, the early-season race remains closely contested.

World.title: Houthi strike on Riyadh Airport kills 12, injures 309 as Saudi Arabia vows retaliation
World.content:
A missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killed 12 people and injured 309 others, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to threaten a decisive response against Yemen’s Ansar Allah rebels (popularly called the Houthis) amid escalating regional tensions.

Al Jazeera reports that the Sunday attack was the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade. Some of the injured were reported to be in critical condition.

The Saudi-led coalition blamed the Iran-backed Houthis for the attack, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime” because of the deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport personnel.

The strike comes amid renewed fighting between the Houthis and forces loyal to Yemen’s internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia. The escalation has heightened concerns about a wider regional conflict, particularly after US President Donald Trump indicated that Washington could consider joining military action against the group.

Passengers flee as airport is hit

Witnesses described scenes of panic at the airport following the strike, with passengers running for safety as people were injured.

One passenger told AFP that they were at Gate 403 when the adjacent Gate 401 area was hit.

“I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running,” the witness said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said the fatalities included four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one citizen each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.

Airport operations were suspended following the incident, while authorities began assessing the damage.

The scale of the casualties also prompted health officials to mobilise additional medical personnel to respond to what a medical source described as a serious emergency.

Two doctors told AFP that some of the injured were pilgrims travelling to Mecca.

Houthis warn airlines against using Saudi airports

Following the attack, the Houthis renewed their warning to airlines, airport workers and travellers against using Saudi airports.

The group urged those concerned to take its warning seriously and said Saudi Arabia bore responsibility for what it described as failed interception efforts.

The warning signals the possibility of further attacks on Saudi aviation infrastructure as hostilities intensify between the group and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces.

The renewed violence follows the breakdown of a United Nations-brokered truce that had helped keep large-scale fighting largely contained since 2022.

The latest developments threaten to undermine diplomatic efforts to end Yemen’s prolonged conflict, which has caused widespread displacement and a severe humanitarian crisis.

Saudi Arabia faces pressure to retaliate

The Saudi-led coalition has vowed a decisive response to the airport attack, raising the prospect of further military operations against Houthi positions in Yemen.

Dania Thafer, executive director of the Gulf International Forum, said Saudi Arabia would likely respond forcefully but suggested that Riyadh would prefer to avoid a prolonged escalation.

She said the Houthis’ actions posed challenges not only to Saudi national security but also to international maritime security.

The conflict, she argued, had expanded beyond a series of retaliatory attacks, with implications for regional stability and international shipping.

Saudi Arabia has previously led a military coalition against the Houthis, intervening in Yemen’s civil war in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

Trump considers possible US military involvement

The attack has also raised questions about the extent of possible US involvement in the conflict.

US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Washington was considering whether to join military action against the Houthis.

“We may. We’re going to look at it,” he told reporters.

The US president also said he intended to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, describing the airport attack as “not acceptable”.

According to media reports cited in the coverage, the United States has provided intelligence-sharing, target-identification and planning assistance for the latest Saudi-backed offensive.

Washington previously supported the Saudi-led campaign in Yemen with intelligence, logistical assistance and weapons, although it did not directly participate in the coalition’s air strikes during the initial intervention.

In 2021, however, the administration of former US President Joe Biden ended support for the Saudi-led offensive, citing the devastating humanitarian consequences of the war.

Yemen conflict threatens wider regional stability

The airport strike underscores the risk that renewed fighting in Yemen could develop into a broader confrontation involving regional and international powers.

The Houthis have maintained their opposition to the Saudi-backed Yemeni government and have repeatedly threatened targets they consider linked to their adversaries.

Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, faces pressure to protect its territory and critical infrastructure while avoiding a return to a prolonged military campaign.

With Washington considering its next steps and the Saudi-led coalition threatening retaliation, the latest attack could further complicate efforts to restore a lasting ceasefire and secure a political settlement to Yemen’s conflict.

The escalation also raises concerns about the security of civilian aviation and international maritime routes, both of which could be affected if the hostilities spread beyond Yemen’s borders.

World.title: CDS orders extension of aerial intelligence to troubled North-west, North-central theatres
World.content:
The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), Olufemi Oluyede, has directed the Defence Space Administration (DSA) to extend its “space-based” intelligence and surveillance support to ongoing military operations in the North-west and North-central theatres.

The spokesperson for the DSA, Funmilayo Bamisaye, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, noting that the directive, given on Friday during the DSA’s 12th anniversary in Abuja, was aimed at enhancing operational effectiveness and troops’ situational awareness.

Mr Oluyede said the aerial support is already aiding troops of Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in the North-east. Its extension is expected to bolster joint forces of Operation Fansan Yamma in the North-west and Operation Savannah Shield in the North-central.

“As we speak now, they are supporting Operation Hadin Kai, and I have given instructions that they should extend that to Operation Fansan Yamma in the North-West and Operation Savannah Shield in the North-Central,” Mr Oluyede, a Nigerian Army general, was quoted as saying.

The defence chief commended the military agency for its “contributions to military operations through space-based intelligence, surveillance and communications capabilities.”

Mr Oluyede also urged the DSA to prioritise indigenous research, technological innovation and human capital development. He also called for stronger collaboration with academic institutions, industries and relevant national agencies to develop resilient space capabilities.

According to the defence chief, systems must be developed, field-tested and refined to meet operational requirements while remaining compatible with existing military structures and equipment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Oluyede lauded the DSA’s strides, including the launch of DELSAT-1, Nigeria’s military satellite launched in 2022, the Special Intelligence Infrastructure, an enabling framework for DELSAT-1, and the Modular Earth Observation Outpost station at the headquarters of Operation Hadin Kai.

He said these initiatives had strengthened Nigeria’s defence space architecture and brought specialised intelligence support closer to operational commanders.

Mr Oluyede also welcomed the commencement of academic activities at the Defence Space School in Delta State, describing indigenous expertise and technological development as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to harness space for national security and development.

The DSA boss, Philip Ilodibia, corroborated the defence chief, saying modern warfare increasingly depends on timely intelligence, situational awareness, secure communications and effective coordination across multiple operational domains.

Mr Ilodibia, a major general, noted that DSA has progressively developed capabilities to support the operational requirements of the Armed Forces and other security agencies since its establishment in 2014.

He said the DSA’s success should be measured by the operational challenges it resolved, the decisions it enabled and the strategic advantages it delivered.

The DSA boss called for stronger synergy among the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force, stressing that space-enabled intelligence, surveillance, communications and geospatial capabilities could improve joint situational awareness, interoperability and operational effectiveness.

He also advocated sustained collaboration between the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA) and the Nigerian Communications Satellite Limited (NigComSat) to strengthen indigenous space capabilities.

Gabriel Olonisakin, a former CDS under late President Muhammadu Buhari, welcomed Nigeria’s plan to strengthen space-based intelligence. However, he noted that it requires sustained investment.

Mr Olonisakin, a retired general, referenced the Russia-Ukraine war, highlighting the growing role of space technology in modern conflicts, particularly cyberattacks on satellite communications infrastructure and the use of satellite imagery to monitor troop movements.

He urged the DSA to leverage strategic partnerships to develop sovereign space capabilities and strengthen national security.

World.title: Enugu govt condemns attack on NDC members
World.content:
The Enugu State Government has condemned Saturday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Party (NDC) at two locations in Enugu, stating that no one died during the attacks.

The government also dismissed reports that a party member, Ifeanyi Nworie, died during the incident at the party’s state secretariat, describing the claim as false.

Chidiebere Onyia, the secretary to the Enugu State Government (SSG), disclosed this while briefing reporters at the Government House, Enugu, on Sunday.

Mr Onyia said the incidents occurred at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport and the NDC State Secretariat in the Government Reserved Area, Enugu, on Saturday.

He explained that the airport incident was a matter between the party and federal authorities, adding that the state government had taken steps to establish what transpired.

According to him, the NDC had published a notice inviting its supporters and members of the public to its proposed “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the airport.

He said the police had advised the party to obtain approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) before security personnel could be deployed for the event.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our findings revealed that the NDC did not secure FAAN’s approval to host a grand statewide rally at the airport.

“Security agencies, therefore, advised the organisers to reconsider the event, but the party went ahead to mobilise its members to the facility.

“The attempt to forcibly gain entry into the airport resulted in a face-off between party members and airport authorities, prompting security agencies to intervene and restore order,” he said.

On the incident at the party’s state secretariat, Mr Onyia said security reports confirmed a violent clash, which the police are investigating.

He disclosed that a 43-year-old man, identified as Ifeanyi Nworie, sustained a gunshot wound during the incident.

“Our findings showed that Nworie was rushed to the Enugu State University Teaching Hospital, Park Lane, where he was stabilised before being transferred to the National Orthopaedic Hospital, Enugu, for further examination.

“We can, therefore, authoritatively report that there were no deaths as falsely claimed by some reports and NDC leaders,” he said.

Enugu govt reacts to allegations

The SSG reiterated the state government’s commitment to protecting lives and property, irrespective of political affiliation.

He said Governor Peter Mbah’s administration had invested heavily in security to sustain peace and create an enabling environment for investment and economic development.

“The Enugu State Government strongly condemns any form of violence, including politically motivated violence.

“We welcome healthy debate, freedom of association and peaceful assembly, but these rights must be exercised responsibly.

“Political parties should be models of good conduct, while politicians should embrace decorum and issue-based campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections,” Mr Onyia said.

He also dismissed allegations that the Chief Security Officer (CSO) to the governor supervised the shooting at the NDC secretariat.

According to him, the governor’s CSO was with Mr Mbah at the Teachers’ Grassroots Movement mega rally held at Okpara Square, Enugu, at the time of the incident.

Mr Onyia accused some opposition figures of attempting to portray Enugu as unsafe and the government as intolerant of political opposition.

He alleged that internal leadership disputes among opposition parties sometimes led to violent clashes, which the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) was later blamed for.

The SSG cited the 12 September incident at Obuofia in Nkanu West Local Government Area, saying investigations had identified suspects who were being prosecuted by the police.

He further alleged that the government had uncovered plans by some opposition elements to recruit armed thugs and bandits to create insecurity in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Mr Onyia maintained that the Mbah administration had no reason to undermine opposition activities, expressing confidence that the governor’s performance would earn him re-election in 2027.

(NAN)

World.title: International Day of the Girl Child, By Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili
World.content:
A girl who learns is a girl who is not a bride. Today the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom.

The numbers are clear. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent.

In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry.

The cost of inaction is high. Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Center for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress.

Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly.

Progress is possible. An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong:

Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more.

In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage.

If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated.

Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet. A girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has.

At the Columbia launch I said that community programmes and advocacy are not enough on their own. Governments must lead. On this Day of the Girl, Human Capital Africa calls on African governments to:

Make foundational learning a girl-protection policy. Every girl should be reading with comprehension by age ten, using proven methods such as structured pedagogy and Teaching at the Right Level.

Every girl should be reading with comprehension by age ten, using proven methods such as structured pedagogy and Teaching at the Right Level. Guarantee the move into secondary school. Remove fees, uniform and transport costs for girls, especially in rural communities with high rates of child marriage.

Remove fees, uniform and transport costs for girls, especially in rural communities with high rates of child marriage. Enforce 18 as the minimum age of marriage in law and in practice , in every state and every community, with traditional and religious leaders as partners.

, in every state and every community, with traditional and religious leaders as partners. Fund this domestically. As foreign aid shrinks, African budgets and African philanthropy must take over.

As foreign aid shrinks, African budgets and African philanthropy must take over. Measure and publish. Track girls’ learning, their transition to secondary school, and child marriage rates in national accountability systems. The AU Decade of Education gives Africa ten years and a continental mandate. As a member of its Steering Committee, I will press for girls’ learning and retention to be at the centre of how the Decade’s success is measured. A Decade that does not end child marriage will not have transformed African education.

The Columbia report sets a realistic target: cutting child marriage prevalence from one in five to one in seven within five years. Africa can lead the way to that target, but only if we treat every girl’s classroom as the place where her childhood is protected.

Any girl-child should be a student, not a bride. She should learn, then lead.

Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili

Founder, Human Capital Africa

Former Nigeria’s Minister of Education and Vice President for Africa Region, World Bank.

World.title: Messi’s retirement: FCTA ex-spokesman proposes FIFA Over-40 World Cup
World.content:
A former spokesman for the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), Nosike Ogbuenyi, has asked the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) to introduce an Over-40 World Cup so that retired international footballers can keep showcasing their skills.

Mr Ogbuenyi said he submitted a proposal to FIFA through the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) secretariat in Abuja on Thursday.

He said the competition, proposed for players aged 40 to 65, would give fans more opportunities to watch some of football’s most celebrated players long after they retire from conventional professional football.

“The introduction of the FIFA Over-40 World Cup will enable the football-loving world to continue to watch the best of all times on the field of play for a longer period,” he said.

Mr Ogbuenyi, who served twice as special assistant on media to the FCT minister, said the proposal was inspired partly by the retirement of some of the game’s biggest names and the difficulty fans face in keeping up with former stars after their playing careers.

“Here in Nigeria, we have seen our most talented and best of all times retire and become less visible publicly. We, the football fans, find it difficult to keep track of our legends and stars like Jay Jay Okocha, Kanu Nwankwo, Victor Ikpeba, Emmanuel Amunike, Obafemi Martins, Vincent Enyeama and John Obi Mikel,” he said.

Beyond Nigeria, he listed several former and current players whom he believes fans would like to see return to the pitch in a veterans’ competition. They include Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Angel Di Maria, Gabriel Batistuta, Michael Owen, David Beckham, Andres Iniesta, Sergio Ramos, Xavi, Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Ronaldinho, Ronaldo de Lima, Roberto Carlos, Didier Drogba, Samuel Eto’o, Zinedine Zidane and Thierry Henry.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Others on his list include Oliver Kahn, Miroslav Klose, Manuel Neuer, Lothar Matthäus and Keisuke Honda.

Proposed rules, benefits

Mr Ogbuenyi said the proposed tournament could promote fitness among former players, provide an additional income source, and keep them in the public eye after retirement.

He also argued it could help former internationals stay connected to their countries and contribute to developing younger players and the wider game.

According to him, the competition would give professional footballers a clearer pathway after leaving the physically demanding environment of youth and senior football, while allowing supporters to follow their idols for longer.

He further suggested that the tournament could discourage age cheating in youth and senior football categories by giving players another age-based competition to aspire to.

On eligibility, Mr Ogbuenyi proposed that players be between 40 and 65 years old and have represented their countries at the senior international level. He also said players should retire from senior international football before representing their countries in the veterans’ competition.

He argued the tournament could be commercially viable for FIFA, citing potential revenue from television rights and corporate partnerships, given the prospect of bringing together some of the game’s most recognisable names.

Why now?

Mr Ogbuenyi said Messi’s retirement, the Argentine forward and eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, created an opportunity to draw attention to his proposal.

“I have found this period of the retirement of the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, Lionel Messi, the most auspicious time to submit this proposal. As the iconic Argentine footballer bowed out after a 21-year international soccer career on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, I kept wondering what the football world would look like if FIFA created a new tournament that would allow talismanic players such as Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Jay Jay Okocha, Kanu Nwankwo and others to continue to exhibit their skills on the global stage.

“In fact, I first started nursing this idea when Jay Jay Okocha, Nigeria’s most adored football prodigy, retired about 15 years ago. But I had to wait for this moment of Messi’s retirement to submit the proposal because of the anticipated global momentum.”

He said he had no personal interest in the proposal and was motivated by his passion for the game.

“I am not making any claims for bringing up this idea and putting it across through this proposal to FIFA. I am just writing as a football fan who wants the world to be happier through more football games entertainment.”

Mr Ogbuenyi expressed confidence that FIFA would evaluate and approve the proposal, which he believes could offer another way to celebrate former players and promote the game.

He currently works as an assistant editor at PREMIUM TIMES. He has previously worked with Daily Champion, The Comet, The Sun, and ThisDay newspapers.

World.title: Why Abia South must vote NDC’s candidate, Michael to support Obi
World.content:
By Innocent Anaba

Spokesman of the Dr Kasarachi Enyinna Michael Campaign Organisation, the National Democratic Congress, NDC, senatorial candidate for Abia South, Chief Emperor Ogbonna, has said there was need to have members of the party in the Senate and House of Representatives, to support Mr. Peter Obi if he wins the presidential election.

He also said that Michael represents a new era, as he has done so much for Abia South, where he lives and has companies operating in the area and that voting for him would ensure Obi has party members to support and pass his policies at the National Assembly.

Speaking weekend, he said: “Now, we all talk about Peter Obi. Everybody is talking about Peter Obi, that Peter Obi is the Ronaldo of Nigerian politics today. In fact, he is the most popular Nigerian today, as you know. Now, if Peter Obi becomes the President and we don’t have senators in the National Assembly or members of the House of Representatives, how will he perform? It is a normal thing. Assuming I am the President today and I am bringing reforms that would reduce the cost of governance, reforms that would stop corruption, first of all, I have to call my party men, and I will tell them, ‘Please, this is what I want.’ If NDC does not have a majority in the House and you voted for Peter Obi, you are wasting your time.

“Assuming the APC or other parties have the majority, they will just gang up and impeach him. It happened in Anambra State. They impeached Peter Obi in Anambra State as governor. Later, he went to court and got his mandate back.

“Now, in Nigeria, they may impeach him because his party may not have the majority.

“That is why we are telling Nigerians, be the grassroots. If you want a change, be the change yourself.”

On the senatorial candidate, Michael, he said: “For those of us who are young, we align with NDC and we brought out Dr. Michael, who is the right candidate for Abia South. Abia South is made up of Aba South, Aba North, Obingwa, Ugwunagbo, Ukwa West and Ukwa East.

“Now, we have looked at the political situation in Abia State. The person that has been there is Enyinnaya Abaribe. He has been there for a very long time. From being deputy governor, and he started talking about Otu Onu (one term), Later, he was elected to the Senate on the ground of Otu Onu. And he has been there for 20-something years. I am a voter in Abia South. I am a taxpayer too. I pay taxes, and I know that we need a change.

“So, that is why, for those of us who are young, we align with NDC and we brought out Michael, who is the senatorial candidate. For those who don’t know him, he is from Ogwe in Ukwa West.

“He is not only a giver; he is somebody who, when he looks at you, knows what your problem is. He is a true democrat. He is not a pompous person. If you see him, you will like him. Everybody likes him.

“He is an achiever. He is a technocrat. He has a company, Fintech, that operates in Abia State. His family has a house on Azikiwe Road. He grew up on Azikiwe Road, so he knows Aba very well. And he has companies operating here, operating in Abia. So, it is not as if he is a foreigner coming to run elections in Aba. He is somebody who has been consistent in promoting Aba’s welfare.

“We are looking for a way to get the country back, and it is very simple. We need people like Michael, who shall be a senator in the Federal Republic of Nigeria. We also need NDC House of Assembly and House of Representatives members, so that if the President wants to make a reform, there will be people from his party who will help him do it. That is why I advise Abia South: please, let us support Michael. He is an achiever, he is a young man, he is down to earth, and we need a paradigm change.

World.title: Vanguard summit: Mental health neglect threatens Nigeria’s stability – Sheikh
World.content:
File image

…Charges FG to enforce 2021 Act, expand services

By Sola Ogundipe

Nigeria’s neglect of mental health is threatening social stability, weakening public trust and deepening despair among young people struggling with insecurity, and diminishing their confidence in the future, Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, a leading psychiatrist, has warned.

Sheikh, a professor of psychiatry and psychopharmacology, at the Department of Psychiatry, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, called on the Federal Government to implement the National Mental Health Act 2021 and expand access to affordable care, particularly at the community level, warning that untreated psychological distress could weaken families, fracture communities and erode confidence in public institutions.

Speaking at the 4th Vanguard Mental Health Summit held at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, Sheikh said in a presentation titled “Mental Health as Social Capital: The Hidden Wealth of Nations” that mental wellbeing was fundamental to the trust, relationships and cooperation societies need to function.

He described mental health as one of the most neglected areas of healthcare, particularly in Africa and Nigeria, where inadequate investment has constrained access to services, especially community-based care.

“Nigeria faces a serious social capital crisis. We are a nation of about 230 million people, with a large youth population, yet our social indicators raise troubling questions about trust, cohesion and confidence in the future. Low trust in institutions and tensions between communities weaken the relationships that hold society together,” he said.

Sheikh identified insecurity, family breakdown, substance misuse and the growing desire among young Nigerians to leave the country as issues that must be understood beyond their immediate economic and social dimensions.

“When you live in survival mode, you cannot plan for tomorrow. The growing desire among young Nigerians to leave the country is not only an economic or migration issue. For some, it also reflects a loss of confidence in the future.

“Family breakdown and substance use, including the misuse of codeine and other psychoactive substances, must also be understood in context. They can reflect deeper psychological distress.”

He warned that prolonged exposure to violence and trauma could undermine the trust and social bonds needed to rebuild communities and sustain development.

“Consider a child who grows up in Kaduna witnessing killings and receiving no psychological support. That child may become an adult living with hypervigilance and deep mistrust. How will such an adult trust the state? How will that person nurture the next generation?” he asked.

According to Sheikh, the consequences of insecurity extend beyond deaths, displacement and property losses to include lasting psychological harm that can affect how survivors relate to others, engage with institutions and raise their families.

On the way forward, he said: “First, we must strengthen the mental health system and expand access to affordable, quality care, particularly at the community level. Second, we must implement the National Mental Health Act 2021 rather than allow its provisions to remain largely on paper. Third, we must ensure that attempted suicide is no longer treated as a criminal offence and that people in crisis receive appropriate care and support.”

Further, Sheikh stressed that mental health should be treated as a national and humanitarian priority, with services available close to where people live rather than concentrated in specialist facilities.

He also cautioned against viewing mental wellbeing solely through its economic benefits, noting that untreated mental health conditions could affect education, employment, productivity and quality of life, while access to care could produce benefits for individuals and society.

“The bridge between poverty and prosperity is not infrastructure alone, it requires mental health. The bridge between conflict and peace is not negotiation alone, it also requires trauma healing and reconciliation,” he said.

Explaining the relationship between mental health and social capital, Sheikh noted “Psychological wellbeing could help people build relationships, participate in community life and cooperate with others. In turn, supportive family ties, friendships and wider social networks could reduce loneliness, provide emotional support and help people cope with adversity.

“The relationship works both ways. Mental health can help generate social capital, while social capital can support mental wellbeing,” he said, adding that supportive relationships and access to opportunities were essential to ensuring that people could benefit from these connections.

“Without mental health, there is no sustainable social development. Without social capital, there is no development, and without development, there is no lasting prosperity,” he said.

World.title: La Liga: Isco’s Betis rise back above Real Madrid to third
World.content:
Real Betis’ Spanish midfielder #22 Isco (R) celebrates with Real Betis’ Colombian forward #09 Juan Hernandez scoring his team’s fourth goal during the Spanish league football match between Real Betis and CA Osasuna at Benito Villamarin Stadium in Seville on October 11, 2026. (Photo by JORGE GUERRERO / AFP)

Veteran playmaker Isco struck twice to help Real Betis climb back into third place in La Liga with a 5-2 win over Osasuna on Sunday.

The Andalucian side moved a point above Real Madrid, fourth, and level with second place Atletico Madrid, trailing leaders Barca by five points.

Manuel Pellegrini’s side claimed a sixth league win from eight matches with an exciting display of attacking football at La Cartuja stadium, where they are playing until their Benito Villamarin home is renovated, likely 2028.

Former Real Madrid midfielder Isco, 34, netted from the penalty spot after a foul on Rodrigo Riquelme, and Ez Abde doubled the hosts lead after half-an-hour with a cool finish.

Ante Budimir’s own goal gave Betis their third after half-time, before the Croatian striker netted at the correct and Raul Garcia added another to give Osasuna a fighting chance.

Isco capitalised on a loose ball in the box to grab his second and Jose Morante bagged a fifth in stoppage time to close out Betis’s big win.

“Football is never truly under control,” said Pellegrini after his side almost let their three-goal lead slip.

“As soon as the pace drops, the other team can pull level.”

The former Manchester City coach also praised Isco after his brace.

“He has spectacular quality and a maturity as a player that allows him to perform at whatever level he wants to,” added Pellegrini.

Elsewhere Valencia, 19th, earned a point in a 2-2 draw at Racing Santander under new coach Javier Aguirre.

Real Sociedad defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-2 in another entertaining battle.

The Basque side, sixth, eased into a three-goal lead Mario Soriano pulled one back for the visitors in San Sebastian to spark a Depor fight back.

They were given further encouragement when Real Sociedad’s Pablo Marin was sent off in the 66th minute for a foul on Nsongo Bil in the box and Yeremay Hernandez netted from the penalty spot.

Both teams finished with 10 men after Lorenzo Amatucci brought down Mikel Oyarzabal as the last man, and Depor could not find an equaliser.

On Saturday Liga leaders Barcelona beat Getafe 3-0 to prolong their perfect start to the season, with eight wins from eight league games.

Hansi Flick’s side are followed by second place Atletico Madrid, who snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves, while Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid scraped a 1-0 victory over Villarreal despite Vinicius Junior’s red card for hair-pulling.

World.title: Tinubu to flag off 376km Niger highway Tuesday
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – President Bola Tinubu will on Tuesday flag off the reconstruction and dualisation of the 376km Lambata–Bida–Mokwa–Makera–Kontagora Federal Highway in Niger State, a project expected to improve transport links and boost agricultural and commercial activities across North-Central Nigeria.

For farmers struggling to move produce to markets, traders transporting goods and commuters travelling between communities, the highway could ease movement and open up economic opportunities, provided the project is delivered to the required standard.

In a statement by Dr Abiodun Essiet, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement for the North-Central region, the project was described as a major infrastructure initiative under Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

The flag-off, scheduled for noon in Bida, is expected to attract the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago; and other federal and state government officials.

The statement said the highway would strengthen the movement of people, agricultural produce and commercial goods across the region.

“Beyond road construction, the project represents an investment in the economic connections that link farmers to markets, businesses to customers and communities to wider commercial opportunities,” it said.

Niger State’s agricultural economy stands to benefit from improved access to markets, while transport operators and businesses could gain from better road conditions, reduced journey delays and safer travel.

The project aligns with the Renewed Hope Agenda’s infrastructure priorities, which identify road development as a driver of economic growth and national development.

However, the statement did not disclose the contract sum, contractor, construction timetable or expected completion date.

It said the project’s success would ultimately depend on what is delivered to road users and host communities.

“The ultimate measure of the project’s success will be the delivery of a durable highway that improves transportation, strengthens economic connections and serves the needs of communities along the corridor,” the statement said.

World.title: Tinubu to Aspirants: Don’t make promises you cannot fund
World.content:
Tinubu

By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor

President Bola Tinubu has challenged those seeking to lead Nigeria to explain the cost of their campaign promises, how they intend to implement them and whether they can sustain them.

Tinubu said every government commitment must be backed by a credible plan and be financially sustainable to avoid passing the burden to Nigerians and future generations.

The President stated this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, stressing that leaders must balance the need to provide immediate relief with the responsibility to protect the future of the country’s children.

“As President, I have a duty to provide relief today without compromising our children’s future.

“Every commitment must be sustainable and backed by a credible plan. That responsibility guides our decisions, including the difficult ones,” he said.

Tinubu added that political promises were easy to make when their costs could be deferred, leaving citizens and future generations to bear the consequences.

“Anyone seeking to lead Nigeria should be prepared to explain what their promises will cost, how they will deliver them, and whether they can sustain them.

“Promises are easy to make when the costs can be postponed, leaving Nigerians and future generations to pay the bill,” he said.

The President also referred to the stories of some Nigerians, including Blessing, Ada, Abigail and Kabir, saying their experiences demonstrated the impact of government investments on people’s daily lives.

He also acknowledged a request from Emmanuel, saying it reminded him of the work still required to expand access to essential services.

“Emmanuel, your request reminds me of the work still ahead. I know many more Nigerians like you are waiting for these services,” Tinubu said.

He stressed the need to continue expanding access to affordable transportation across the country, noting that the Federal Government would work with state governments to achieve the objective.

“Our responsibility is to keep expanding access until affordable transportation becomes a reality for more communities across our country.

“That is the work we will continue in collaboration with the States,” he added.

World.title: Adelabu denies calling on Nigerians to reject APC
World.content:
Adelabu

Says viral video is an old 2022 interview taken out of context

The media office of former Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu, has dismissed a viral report claiming that he called on Nigerians to reject the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the allegation as false and misleading.

In a statement issued in October 2026, Adelabu’s media office said the video circulating on social media was an excerpt from an interview he granted in 2022, when he was the governorship candidate of the Accord Party in Oyo State.

It said Adelabu did not call on Nigerians to reject the APC, urging the public to disregard what it described as a deliberate attempt to misrepresent his position and create friction between him, President Bola Tinubu and the party’s leadership.

According to the statement, Adelabu had consistently maintained his loyalty to the APC and the President despite controversies surrounding the party’s governorship nomination process in Oyo State.

The former minister, who served under the APC-led Federal Government, reportedly left public office to pursue his governorship ambition in the state.

The statement alleged that the APC nomination process was marred by controversies, including the alleged imposition of a preferred aspirant and the failure to transparently release the primary election results.

It said Adelabu had nevertheless maintained that he had no intention of leaving the party and that his political ambition was not a do-or-die affair.

“His position has been consistent: loyalty does not preclude the demand for fairness, transparency and adherence to democratic principles,” the statement said.

It argued that Adelabu’s criticism of the party’s internal electoral process should not be interpreted as a call for Nigerians to reject the APC.

The media office explained that the 2022 interview reflected Adelabu’s view that political parties had disappointed Nigerians and that voters should focus on the credibility and character of individual candidates.

It added that the comments were made in the context of the political environment at the time and did not amount to opposition to the APC or Tinubu’s presidential ambition.

The statement also described Adelabu’s relationship with Tinubu as longstanding, saying it was based on mutual respect and trust.

It challenged those circulating the video to publish the full, unedited interview rather than selectively extracting portions of it.

The media office further claimed that Adelabu had not granted any media interview since the conclusion of the controversial APC governorship nomination process in Oyo State in which he made the alleged statement.

It urged APC members, the media and the public to verify information before sharing it, warning against the spread of unsubstantiated claims.

“Chief Adelabu remains committed to the APC, loyal to Mr President and supportive of the party’s broader political objectives,” the statement said.

The media office advised the public to rely on authentic statements from Adelabu or his authorised representatives.

World.title: Top 10 highest-paid content creators in 2026 – Forbes ranking
World.content:
MrBeast has emerged as the world’s highest-paid content creator, earning an estimated $300 million as social media influencers expand their businesses into entertainment, technology, consumer products and streaming.

According to Forbes’ 2026 Top Creators ranking, the 50 creators featured on the list collectively generated $1.02 billion, representing a 20 per cent increase from $853 million recorded in the previous year’s ranking.

The publication, edited by Steven Bertoni, with reporting by Zoya Hasan and Alexandra York, alongside Sofia Chierchio and Martina Di Licosa, highlighted how digital creators are transforming their online popularity into lucrative business empires.

From YouTube personalities and TikTok stars to podcasters and entrepreneurs, the creators are increasingly competing with traditional entertainment companies through original productions, brand partnerships, merchandise and investments.

Forbes noted that creators are also making significant inroads into Hollywood and streaming. Examples include films developed from online content that have generated hundreds of millions of dollars at the box office, as well as digital personalities securing deals with major streaming platforms.

Here are the 10 highest-paid creators featured in the Forbes 2026 ranking, based on their reported earnings.

1. MrBeast — $300 million

Total followers: 873 million | Average engagement: 3.00%

Jimmy Donaldson, popularly known as MrBeast, tops the ranking with estimated earnings of $300 million.
