World.title: Make way for Satt Baayu, an all-women Kutch collective weaving tradition and innovation
World.content:
Traditional handcrafted textiles and crafts with a bit of innovation is the highlight of Ek Pehel, a three-day exhibition by Satt Baayu starting October 15 at Saptaparni in Hyderabad.

Big step

Ek Pehel, meaning first step, marks a significant move for Satt Baayu, a collective of seven women artisans from Kutch in Gujarat. Formed seven months ago, Satt Baayu or seven women in Kutchi, has been developing a new collection based on their individual ideas and design approaches.

The collective brings together their different craft practices, including Mashru and Kutchi weaving styles, and Suf and Rabari embroideries reflecting their diversity. “We know that people in Hyderabad appreciate crafts, heritage, and handmade things. So it felt like a good place to begin for us,” says Krishna Velji Vankar, one of the artisans, about their first exhibition.

Speaking over the phone from Sarli village, around 30 km from Bhuj in Kutch, Krishna, an extra-weft weaving artisan designer, represents the collective’s other artisan designers and co-founders— Bhawna Puwar, Amruta Vankar, Renu Rabari, Pooja Vankar, Usha Jaypal and Karmi Ben Rabari from the neighbouring villages of Faradi, Bhujodi, Desalpar, Varamseda and Gadhpadar.

Family legacy

Although the craft has been passed down to them from their ancestors, this is the first time that these women are at an independently organised exhibition. “Many women in Kutch practice weaving and embroidery but due to family responsibilities they often work at home. They do not have the opportunities to build business or travel independently for exhibitions,” says Krishna. By coming together as a group, the women hope to support each other, grow stronger collectively, and create more opportunities for other women artisans.

Stories from the Kutch EK Pehel, a three-day exhibition by Satt Baayu, a collective of seven women artisan designers is at Saptaparni, Road No.8, Banjara Hills. The display from October 15 to 18 has a collection of saris, stoles, dupattas, jackets, kaftan, bags, carpets, tops, kurtas, skirts and beaded jewellery. The exhibition also features work of three artisan groups from Karnataka, Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh who have been part of Somaiya Kala Vidya’s outreach projects. Visitors can meet the artisan designers, explore the new collection and shop directly from the makers.

The artisans are graduates of the design course at Somaiya Kala Vidya (SKV) and are currently pursuing the institute’s Business Management for Artisans (BMA) programme. While each of them has specific organisational responsibilities, they also create and develop their own designs.

Preserving and innovating

The women artisans have worked with colours, motifs, materials and forms to integrate their ideas into the craft. Preserving the craft’s identity while innovating is their hallmark. Kutchi weaving is marked by setting up the loom, preparing the yarns, applying starch with a Kalori brush and creating extra-weft motifs. “This technique is being preserved while experimenting with motifs and colours,” says Krishna.

Each artisan-designer is inspired by different elements to create garments and accessories. Instead of the traditional stripes made in Mashru weaving, Amruta has experimented with checks in her new collection. Even materials like mulberry silk, which is not part of family tradition, has been explored. They have also worked with trying a colour palette with black and white designs, emerald blue, deep purples, pink and green combinations.

Some collections are inspired by Dravidian architecture, crafts from Karnataka, and the kolam tradition from Tamil Nadu. “Since Hyderabad has a mix of cultures and audiences, we thought it would be interesting to bring our collection here.”

The collective hopes visitors will see how Kutch crafts can evolve through innovation, technique, finishing, new designs, and the involvement of educated artisans, while retaining their distinct identity. “We want people to look at a piece and easily identify it but at the same time be surprised and think, ‘Is this really Kutch craft?’. We also want people to see how artisans are taking responsibility for design and also marketing, displaying, and pricing, while finding ways to build sustainable businesses of their own,” she adds.

Through Ek Pehel, the women artisans hope to inspire other women to take their craft forward and explore entrepreneurship while holding on to tradition.

World.title: North Korea fired projectile towards sea, South Korean military says
World.content:
South Korea's military on Monday (October 12, 2026) said North Korea fired at least one projectile toward its eastern waters, adding to a recent streak in weapons demonstrations.

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff did not immediately say whether the weapon was ballistic or how far it flew. The office of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the country also detected the launch and described the weapon as a suspected ballistic missile.

The launch came days after South Korea on Friday (October 9) flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon, designed to fly at least five times the speed of sound and evade missile defence systems, which President Lee Jae Myung described as an important step in strengthening the South's conventional defence capabilities.

While maintaining a hard line toward Seoul, North Korea has been ramping up weapons testing as it seeks to expand its arsenal of nuclear-capable systems, including an Oct. 3 test of what the North described as a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to evade missile defences in South Korea and Japan.

North Korea has also conducted other missile tests and live-fire drills and commissioned a new warship as leader Kim Jong Un continues to flaunt his nuclear weapons program while rejecting U.S. and South Korean offers to resume long-stalled diplomacy.

Tensions were further worsened after three South Korean soldiers were injured in land mine explosions last month near the heavily armed inter-Korean border. The South's military and the U.S.-led United Nations Command concluded the blasts were caused by devices planted by North Korea, which has denied responsibility and ridiculed the South's demands for an apology.

World.title: Anti-CEC protests continue; journalists detained despite SC order, Rahul Gandhi announces march to Supreme Court as Delhi braces for fresh curbs
World.content:
Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas and All India Students’ Association president Neha were among several protestors allegedly injured by security forces as they were being detained in the capital on Sunday (October 11, 2026), the second day of a protest called by youth organisations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Despite the Supreme Court’s directives on Saturday (October 10), around a dozen journalists were detained on Sunday (October 11) while covering the protest at different locations. There was no official announcement by Delhi Police on the total number of detentions on Sunday.

Keep track | Anti-CEC protest LIVE: CJI Surya Kant declines to meet INDIA Bloc leaders on October 12; Delhi Police detain women protesters after 6 p.m.

Leader of the Opposition (LoP) and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, announced a march to the Supreme Court on Monday (October 12), calling the “youth, all opposition parties, civil society groups, all those who believe in democracy and stand by the Constitution of India,” to join the procession.

Security set to be tightened on October 12

The unprecedented security arrangements in the New Delhi area — imposed on October 10, and considerably relaxed after the top court’s hearing earlier in the day — are likely to be back on Monday (October 12) in the wake of Mr. Gandhi’s call. While mobile Internet was restored on Sunday (October 11), residents continued a cautious approach. Despite the festive season, footfall and business remained low in Connaught Place and the central Delhi area that was still interspersed with police barricades.

Activists of different organisations alleged that they were beaten by security forces, which the Delhi Police denied. The police claimed that the protestors were being adamant and not cooperating at the time of detention.

Meanwhile, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders who were released on Sunday (October 11) after being detained a day earlier, asserted that the protests would continue till the CEC resigns. He called Prime Minister Narendra Modi the biggest “coward” and urged people to protest peacefully wherever they were. CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke left for Maharashtra to be with his family, following the demise of his grandmother.

New epicentre of protest

As security forces continued to block all entrances to Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in the capital, the agitation shifted to other parts of the city, with Connaught Place in the heart of the national capital becoming the new epicentre of the protest.

A series of protests broke out in the outer circle of Connaught Place, starting from a march carried out by various students groups, including All India Students’ Federation (AISF), the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) and the Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS), followed by a march led by AISA and then by the Revolutionary Workers’ Party of India (RWPI) and the Disha Students’ Organisation. All of them were detained by security personnel.

In the evening, women SFI activists doing a ‘Tiranga Yatra’ were detained from Connaught Place after 6 p.m. and taken away in a bus by security forces. The SFI termed the detention of women post 6 p.m. as illegal and alleged that the women activists were beaten by male officers.

By evening, security was stepped up in Connaught Place and security personnel detained many people, including some who were just talking to the media.

The CJP’s leaders, however, are seeking a return to Jantar Mantar. Mr. Ranka, Mr. Das, and Ms. Singh plan to visit the Parliament Street police station to seek a date for holding a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. “Delhi Police can give us a date for Jantar Mantar in 24 hours, or we will give another protest call ourselves,” Mr. Ranka said.

Tomorrow at 10AM, me, @SauravDassss, @whattalawyer and other CJP leaders will go to Parliamentary Street Police Station to get a date for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. @DelhiPolice can give us a date for Jantar Mantar in 24 hours, or we will give another protest call ourselves. @Cockroachisback — Ashutosh Ranka (@AshutoshRanka) October 11, 2026

Journalists detained again

At least seven journalists were detained on Sunday (October 11), from different parts of the city while covering the protest, despite many of them wearing their ID cards around their necks. Many of them were taking videos on their phones. The Delhi Police claimed that the reporters were working “too close” to the protestors while they were being detained and may have been detained because of “confusion”.

During the day, some student activists were detained in buses which had cage-like structures resembling police lockups, which is uncommon while detaining student protestors in Delhi.

On Saturday (October 10), 45 metro stations were shut down in the capital, while internet services were blocked around the Jantar Mantar area. Both the metro and internet services resumed on Sunday after a rap from the Supreme Court. However, residents continued to have a cautious approach, and footfall at businesses remained low in the central Delhi area which remained under heavy barricading.

World.title: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as president approves cabinet decision
World.content:
Key developments:

Emergency imposed under Article 232, governor’s rule under Article 234

Cabinet recommended move due to KP govt’s ‘deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’

Technocratic council formed; Fakhr Alam appointed as KP chief secretary

PTI’s Gohar condemns decision as undemocratic, says peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy

Governor Kundi calls for unity for ‘new chapter’ in KP’s development

ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet.

The measures have been approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, the President House said in a statement. The two provisions pertain to the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule.

Following the imposition, internet disruptions were being reported from parts of Peshawar, with Dawn unable to contact its correspondents there.

According to sources in the telecom sector, mobile network and data services have been slowed or shut down in selected areas of some cities. However, there is no province-wide shutdown of mobile data or internet.

Internet watchdog NetBlocks said network data showed a major disruption to internet connectivity in parts of KP as emergency was imposed.

The federal government also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP. On the ground, shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block several roads, with heavy police deployment.

The decision to impose the emergency provisions came during an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in KP.

A statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.

The members proposed, given the “gravity” of the situation, that the PM advise the president to exercise “his constitutional authority and impose an emergency in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution”.

The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation.

That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks .

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.

On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

It may be recalled that in July 2024, when Afridi’s predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur was the chief minister, the KP Assembly passed a resolution urging the federal government to consult with it and the provincial government before launching a new military operation.

The resolution, passed by a majority vote, cautioned that proceeding without provincial consent could hinder the offensive’s success and result in adverse consequences, for which the federal government would be responsible.

In December that year, the assembly voted unanimously against a potential military operation in parts of Khyber and Bannu districts.

About a year later, after Afridi became the KP CM, the provincial assembly convened a grand jirga with Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and other parties in attendance. The moot unanimously demanded that the Centre prioritise negotiations with Afghanistan and consult the KP government over Afghan policy.

Constitutional provisions

Emergency

Article 232 of the Constitution provides for the proclamation of emergency in a province.

It says, “If the president is satisfied that a grave emergency exists in which the security of Pakistan, or any part thereof, is threatened by war or external aggression, or by internal disturbance beyond the power of a provincial government to control, he may issue a Proclamation of Emergency.”

However, invoking this article “due to internal disturbances beyond the powers of a provincial government to control” requires a resolution from the provincial assembly of that province.

In case the president “acts on his own” — which is not currently the case — the Proclamation of Emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days.

According to this provision, parliament “shall have power to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during the time of the proclamation of an emergency.

Nothing in this Article shall restrict the power of a provincial assembly to make any law which the Constitution empowers it to make, but if any provision of a provincial law is repugnant to any provision of an Act by Parliament, the latter would prevail and the provincial law would be void as long as the parliamentary Act is in effect.

Governor’s rule

On the other hand, Article 234 deals with the imposition of the governor’s rule “in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a province”. For imposition of the governor’s rule, the president simply requires a request from the provincial governor, it says.

“A proclamation issued under this Article shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time,” the Constitution reads.

However, it adds that no such proclamation shall in any case remain in force for more than six months.

Article 233, which provides powers to the president to suspend certain fundamental rights during the emergency period, was not mentioned in the summary signed by President Zardari.

Where is Sohail Afridi?

A couple of hours after the imposition of emergency was announced, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan, who had been accompanying now dysfunctional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on the PTI’s long march, claimed that the he had been taken into custody.

Dawn contacted police for a confirmation soon after Jan’s claim, but there was no response.

Meanwhile, MNA Shahid Khattak also claimed Afridi’s “arrest”, as well as MNA Junaid Akbar and others from there party.

He also said he would be leading the march now.

Later, the PTI issued a statement, condemning the “arrest” of Afridi and other and describing it as an act of “political victimisation and an attempt to weaken the province’s elected leadership and democratic institutions”.

It quoted PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram as saying that Afridi’s “arrest” could not be viewed in isolation from the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule.

“The developments reflect a broader effort to bypass elected institutions and undermine the constitutional authority of the province.

“The arrest of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and Junaid Akbar has exposed the political nature of the federal government’s actions. These measures are not directed at addressing security challenges; they are intended to weaken PTI, undermine the elected government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and disregard the democratic will of its people,” he said.

Akram demanded the “immediate and unconditional release” Afridi, Akbar and “all other political detainees arrested in connection with the ongoing action against PTI”. He also demanded that the federal government publicly disclose the “legal grounds, specific charges and procedural basis for the arrests of the chief minister and the PTI provincial president”.

However, he sounded less certain while speaking on Geo News programme ‘Naya Pakistan’. He said they had received reports of Afridi and Akbar’s arrest, and adding that they were unable to confirm whether Jan and Khattak, too, had been taken into custody.

“We are unable to contact some people […] Because the internet has been suspended in several areas, we are unable to contact. You do not know the havoc they have created in KP. People are escaping and going into hiding,” he said.

In a clip shared on PTI’s official X account, Salman Akram Raja, the party’s secretary general, said, “We do not know where Sohail Afridi is, in what condition he has been kept. Junaid Akbar is also missing.”

When Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry was asked about reports of Afridi’s arrest during ‘Naya Pakistan’, he said some individuals had been detained in view of the law and order situation but did not confirm whether they included Afridi.

He said those who did not have a criminal record or were not wanted would be released.

Council, chief secretary appointed

Following the imposition of emergency, the federal government formed an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council to assist the governor with running the province.

Later, Governor Kundi also chaired the first meeting of the council, vowing to restore peace in the province.

Earlier in the day, the federal government appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as the chief secretary of KP, according to an official notification, a copy of which is available with Dawn.

The appointment will take effect immediately and remain in place until further orders, it said.

Dr Irfan, a Grade 22 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was previously serving as secretary of the Power Division in the federal Ministry of Energy. He hails from Mardan.

In a separate notification, the federal government also placed Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada at the disposal of the KP government with “immediate effect and until further orders”.

Akhunzada, a Grade 20 PAS officer, was serving as an additional secretary at PMO.

He hails from Charsadda and has also served as additional political agent for North and South Waziristan, secretary of health, information and education in KP, and commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan.

‘Peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy’

PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan strongly condemned the imposition of emergency in KP and “completely rejected” it.

“This is an extremely alarming and grave political mistake and an undemocratic measure — the people will never accept such actions against their rights,” Gohar wrote in a post on X.

He stated: “There is still time; this decision can be withdrawn in a few days. Let the federation set aside its ego, understand the ground realities, accept legitimate demands, respect the sentiments and emotions of the people, and save the country from further political and economic damage and from pushing back the democratic process.

“Revisiting political decisions is not a sign of weakness but of wisdom in the national interest — otherwise, great damage will be done.”

Stressing that the mandate of the people of KP was their constitutional and legal right, the PTI chairman said: “Peace cannot be established, nor stability brought, by ignoring this mandate, weakening provincial autonomy, and creating conflict between the federation and the province.”

He asserted that there was “no disagreement on eliminating terrorism, but the fight against terrorism cannot be used as a justification to suppress the people’s voice, achieve political objectives, or limit the province’s constitutional authority”.

“Terrorism can only be combated through national unity and a joint strategy,” Gohar maintained.

“The federation cannot be strengthened by weakening the provinces. The solution to problems lies not in force, confrontation, and extraordinary measures, but in political wisdom, supremacy of the Constitution, and meaningful negotiations and practical steps.”

The PTI chairman said his party will raise the matter on “every constitutional, legal, and democratic forum for the protection of the people’s mandate, provincial autonomy, and constitutional and democratic rights”.

Later in the day, Gohar said PTI would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums.

The PTI parliamentary committee held a meeting and categorically rejected the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP. In a statement issued afterwards, it termed the development “a direct assault on the public mandate and an unacceptable move”.

“In a three-hour-long meeting of the PTI parliamentary party, the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was strongly condemned and unanimously rejected. The meeting declared this step contrary to facts, unconstitutional, undemocratic, and a blatant insult to the public mandate of the province,” the statement said.

“The parliamentary party made it clear that measures to render the elected provincial government ineffective and usurp its constitutional powers could pose grave threats to the federal system and democratic traditions. Such decisions will increase political instability and public unrest in the province, while already existing tensions between the federation and the province will further intensify,” it added.

The statement added that the solution to political differences should be found through constitutional and democratic procedures and mutual consultation, rather than through force and coercion.

It also raised serious questions regarding the conduct of the federal government.

“The parliamentary party took the stance that if terrorism and the deteriorating law and order situation are the primary justification for the imposition of emergency, then why is the situation in Balochistan being ignored?” the statement asked.

The meeting also made it clear that Afridi was the elected chief minister and a member of the provincial assembly.

“Measures regarding his arrest, detention, or the usurping of his constitutional and democratic powers were strongly condemned. The meeting termed such actions an insult to the public mandate and a dangerous precedent for democratic traditions,” it said.

The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), of which PTI is a part, termed the move a violation of the Constitution.

In a statement, the opposition alliance particularly assailed President Zardari’s PPP, claiming that the “most undemocratic actions and the imposition of governor’s rule” had been the hallmark of the party in the country’s history.

“On the one hand, despite the extremely dire administrative and law and order situation in Balochistan, no such step has been taken, while on the other hand, this province — whose assembly and government stand on the true and real mandate of the people — has been targeted,” it contended.

TTAP said it would convene a meeting on the matter and announce a joint course of action.

Governor Kundi urges unity for ‘new chapter’

Meanwhile, Governor Kundi said the decision was made for “establishing peace in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the prosperity of its people, and the development of the province”.

“I am your governor, but beyond that, I want to play my role as a servant of this soil and a protector of your rights. Let us come together to bring peace to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and begin a new chapter of our province’s development,” he said in a statement.

Kundi assured the public that it was his responsibility to raise their issues on the relevant forums.

Recalling the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism, he said, “Now the time has come that we do not let these sacrifices go to waste and together establish lasting peace in our province.”

The PPP leader urged the public to set aside their political differences and unite for the province’s peace, the protection of its people, and the future of the coming generations.

“We must not let our differences become an obstacle in the path of our province’s common interests.”

Cannot allow PTI to destabilise the economy: PM tells cabinet

Addressing the cabinet meeting, the premier said the PTI-led KP government cannot be allowed to derail the stabilising economy amid tensions between the two sides.

“I will not allow them (PTI) to destabilise the economy,” he said during the meeting.

On terrorism in KP and Balochistan, the premier said, “The way common citizens are being martyred, the way police officials and security officials, children and mothers [..] there can be nothing more heart-wrenching.”

He recalled that Pakistan has repeatedly urged neighbouring Afghanistan to rein in the terrorist elements; however, “they still do not understand it”.

PM Shehbaz also reiterated his condemnation of the recent deadly Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, noting the long-standing fraternal ties between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

“Our only goal is that peace should be restored in the region,” he said.

“Pakistan expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia and stands with it. We will not tolerate any aggression against Saudi Arabia,” he said, adding that it was a “red line” for Pakistan.

During his address, PM Shehbaz also spoke of the recent staff-level agreement reached with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

“It is hoped that we will unlock the $1.2 billion tranche within this year,” he said, recalling a meeting with the IMF’s Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last month.

He commended the political and military leadership for “working together day and night” in bringing fiscal discipline to Pakistan.

The premier recalled his visit to London last month, where he had met with senior executives from leading global financial institutions.

He also spoke of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the international community, taking note of the appreciation Pakistan has received for mediation in the Middle East conflict.

“Pakistan continues to play its role with hard work and sincerity,” he said, particularly lauding the role of the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

Additional input by Ikram Junaidi, Kalbe Ali

World.title: Info minister alleges 'nexus' between PTI-led KP govt, terrorists
World.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Sunday alleged that the PTI-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, as the Centre explained that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

The press conference by government ministers — Tarar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry — came shortly after the Centre imposed emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s lack of efforts to combat terrorism.

The Centre and the PTI — which was in power in KP — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks .

Addressing the media in Islamabad, the information minister said all cabinet members who attended Sunday’s meeting were of the view that the “PTI government in KP is hand in glove with terrorists and has an unholy alliance with terrorists”.

“Terrorists have a clear say in how each district will be run,” he alleged, citing reports from the Intelligence Bureau and law enforcement agencies (LEAs).

He contended that while other political parties faced terrorist attacks in the region, the PTI got “secure access and passage” thanks to its alleged alliance with such groups.

“What is the reason that even police stations of some districts have been sublet to the Taliban?” Tarar asked, emphasising that the case was not merely of inaction and incompetence but of “empowering” the terrorists.

The minister went on to allege that a “power-sharing formula was gradually taking shape between terrorists and the PTI’s KP government, which was starting from southern districts and was ingressing further into the entire KP”.

He said the “unholy alliance and the nexus between them, as a result of which they had outsourced several districts to terrorists,” enabled the martyrdom of people and attacks on civilian infrastructure.

“I say this publicly that these [Taliban] are foreign-funded people who want to bring our country to destruction,” he said, asserting that a provincial government’s facilitation towards such elements was a “constitutional breakdown”.

Tarar referred to the recent bill regarding police assignments and alleged that the KP government wanted to “hire individuals from terrorist groups in the police”. “They were gradually dragging the entire province towards destruction, irrefutable proof and evidence of which is available.”

Meanwhile, the interior minister warned the groups gathered in parts of KP — an apparent reference to PTI supporters taking part in its long march — to disperse as they did not have any “provincial protection”.

“Whoever is caught, complete legal action will be taken and that person themselves will be responsible for it. We will deal with them strictly, so it is my request that please disperse.”

Responding to a query, Naqvi said, “We have to restore law and order in KP, and we will take whatever action is needed for that, and we will normalise the situation as soon as we can.”

Asked about the reported arrests of KP ministers, Naqvi said individuals would be held under preventative detention where required to maintain law and order, whereas those “wanted will be arrested”.

Responding to a query highlighting terrorism in Balochistan, the interior minister said counterterrorism operations in recent months there had resulted in a “difference” in the situation there.

On the KP emergency, the law minister explained that an Area Development Secretariat (ADS), overseen by the governor, has been formed by the federal government to directly manage 12 districts “that were nearly in a war situation”.

He noted that Parliament assumes the legislative powers of the provincial assembly as the latter stands non-functional.

KP Advisory Council formed

The minister then questioned the KP cabinet’s performance, hailed the province getting “riddance from this group” and provided details of a technocratic KP Advisory Council.

The 11-member council has been formed by the Centre as part of the emergency measures under Article 232 of the Constitution, according to an order seen by Dawn. It will assist the governor in exercising the functions of the KP government on behalf of the federal government.

Through the order, the Centre also appointed Advocate Sanaullah as the KP advocate general.

The province’s home affairs will be overseen by former prisons chief Kifayatullah Khan, described as “very competent” by Tarar.

Tariq Mahmood Pasha, a former FBR chief and an aide to then-finance minister Ishaq Dar, has been assigned as advisor for finance affairs.

MNA Samar Haroon Bilour has been appointed as information adviser, while retired Lt Gen Nigar Johar has been tasked with health affairs.

Former advocate general Amir Javed was assigned the portfolio for law; ex-senator Osman Saifullah Khan will advise the governor on energy and power; Asif Rafiq Afridi was given the portfolio for communication and works; while Maulana Tayyab Qureshi will oversee religious affairs.

Tarar noted that all chosen advisers had either doctorate degrees or extensive experience in public service.

These included Adviser for Industries and Commerce Dr Muhammad Irshad (a former FBR chief with a PhD in finance), Adviser for Mines and Minerals Dr Sarfraz Ali Shah (who had a PhD in economics) and Adviser for Education Dr Syed Amir Abdullah (with a PhD in international relations).

The Cabinet Division has issued an order by the federal government that said that after the proclamation of an emergency, the government of KP “cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution”.

Exercising its powers under Article 232, the government ordered that an Area Development Secretariat (ADS), under the superintendence of the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC), be immediately established to “restore law and order, safeguard the security of the citizens of Pakistan and ensure good governance and development” in Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan (Upper) and South Waziristan (Lower).

It said that the ARDC shall be a representative council comprising the notables from the designated districts and shall be headed by a chairman. The members, the chairman, the vice chairman and the spokesperson of the ARDC shall be appointed in such manner and for such duration, as may be determined.

The order further said that the ADS shall be headed by the additional chief secretary of the designated Districts, who shall be the administrator of these areas.

“Officials of the provincial government and of other bodies or authorities posted in the designated districts shall be placed under the operational and administrative control of ADS. Any further postings/transfers to the designated districts may be ordered by the prime minister on the recommendation of the administrator, from time to time,” it said.

It said that the administrator shall perform all the functions of and exercise all executive, administrative, and law enforcement powers vested in or exercisable by the provincial government in the designated districts.

It said that the administrator may: establish organisational setups for governance, security and development in selected districts with command over district administration, law enforcement and all line departments; issue binding orders to civil, police, and military authorities; issue orders for operational, organisational and administrative functions of ADS; issue orders for allocation and transfer of funds; coordinate with federal agencies, armed forces and provincial bodies for law enforcement and security of the areas; reorganise departments and take necessary actions for public safety, economic stability, relief operations and provision of essential services; and take such other measures as are necessary for the purposes of effective and good governance, maintenance of law and order and provision of services in the designated districts.

“All orders, notifications, directions, or actions taken by the administrator shall have the same legal effect as if issued by the provincial government,” it read.

The order further said that provisions of Chapter 3 (provincial governments) of the Constitution’s Part IV and Clause 3 of Article 175, which pertains to the separation of the judiciary from the executive, will not apply to the designated districts. KP Government Rules of Business 1985 will not apply either.

Naqvi details govt efforts to resolve issues

In his remarks, the interior minister said the Centre tried to take the KP government on board in the counterterrorism fight, but the efforts were in vain due to a lack of response from the latter.

At the outset of Sunday’s briefing, Naqvi said, “Today was not an easy day for us. For over one month, we continuously tried to take the KP government on board. I was personally in touch with them in the background; our only goal was to onboard them so that we could fight together against terrorism.”

The minister went on to reveal that he was in contact with PTI leaders until 11:45pm last night and had been communicating with them “all day about the draft’s para four”. “They did not respond all day.”

“I told them that we can still avoid the situation. Things have gone too far, but we can still do something to delay tomorrow morning’s situation,” he said, referring to the imposition of emergency that the Centre had been mulling.

Naqvi also highlighted efforts by veteran politician Maulana Fazlur Rehman to reduce tensions, but no solution could be found.

He even said the Centre communicated to the PTI repeatedly that it had “no issue” with the party’s long march. “Our issue was entirely terrorism-related, and we want to take you on board on it.”

While acknowledging that there were many issues related to KP’s governance, Naqvi said, “My and the entire interior ministry’s point of view was clear: the situation was not linked to politics even one per cent. We were purely seeing this on the basis of terrorism.”

Referring to the Oct 3 talks between the Centre and PTI, he contended that the situation would have been different if they had reached an agreement back then.” “Even if last night they had said yes, it (emergency) would not have happened.”

He added, “Ask them who their masterminds are. Who were sabotaging them?”

The interior minister then elaborated on the security challenges KP faces, stating that the situation was “really bad” in 12 districts. “In some districts, you cannot even leave your house in the evening.”

“We had multiple meetings with Sohail Afridi, and the only topic was terrorism; no political conversation happened,” he emphasised. The minister said a plan was proposed to strengthen KP Police in five districts initially and eventually hand over security to it in six months, then repeat the process in another five districts.

“They said they had a lack of funds, but it is on the record that we said that we will provide any more funds you need. This was a four-month-old conversation but still no work has happened on it.”

The minister further claimed that the PTI team had agreed on imposing emergency in 12 districts, but added that they were “scared of being seen meeting with us”. “We had clarity on one thing that we did not want to involve politics in this.”

He further alleged, “Their connections with the Taliban are no secret. I would not say anything further.”

The minister remarked that the security situation was extremely bad in certain districts, yet the PTI was able to hold rallies and “not even one person was harmed”.

“We only had two options: either we would see the martyrdoms daily, or we end them. So this difficult decision we have made has a background,” he maintained, adding that the federal government tried its best to avoid it.

During the briefing, Naqvi claimed that “demands” the PTI put forward were already being considered last month, before the opposition party announced its long march towards Islamabad. “Some of their own people could not understand why the long march was taking place.”

He recalled that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wanted to hold talks with the National Assembly opposition leader last month and proposed forming a committee, but the government did not get any confirmation.

“We were trying our best to hold the meeting before the prime minister left so that the situation could be diffused,” he said, noting that a committee for the Oct 3 talks was formed later.

According to the interior minister, the consultations took place for two days and credited PTI MNA Asad Qaiser for saying with “clarity that it is not possible that we take even a step back on terrorism”.

“We will not do it for you; we will do it for Pakistan, and we will fight united against terrorism,” Naqvi quoted Qaiser as saying, adding that he requested the ex-NA speaker to take the KP government on board.

The minister then reiterated that an agreement draft was revised four times, after which the government negotiation committee found out a new draft had been presented by the opposition team.

“Although the previous day the chief minister had authorised them to agree on their behalf, the next day it all changed,” Naqvi said.

World.title: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack
World.content:
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, a day after another attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations at the facility.

Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.

The group on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the last 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom’s transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group “carried out four qualitative operations in the past 24 hours using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones”.

Saree said they targeted the Riyadh airport multiple times, as well as the Dammam airport and two facilities belonging to the Saudi state oil company Aramco.

Hours later, the Saudi coalition fighting the group reported that a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, sparking a fire. Air defences also intercepted a missile nearby, it added.

The civil aviation authority said the attack caused an unspecified number of injuries, and that a damage assessment was underway.

AFP journalists and locals reported hearing the sound of multiple blasts in the Saudi capital on Sunday.

“The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the north of the city.

‘Full-fledged war crime’

The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport — where three people were also killed on Thursday — as well as on other key targets in the world’s top crude oil exporter.

And although Saudi Arabia has poured billions into its military, Houthi attacks continue to slip through.

“Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves against Houthi attacks,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University.

The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”.

Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate on Sunday.

Saturday’s attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders around the world, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose country does not have diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, also denounced the “horrific terrorist attack”.

Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, the civil aviation authority said, with 309 wounded.

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also said one of its citizens died on Sunday after being wounded the day before.

A Riyadh-based Western diplomat told AFP the official number of injured may not give a full picture, as it did not appear to include those with minor wounds.

Operations suspended

Authorities suspended operations at the airport into Sunday, a senior aviation source said, with air traffic monitor Flightradar24 saying the closure was extended until 21:00 GMT (2am PKT on Monday).

A second aviation source confirmed the halt in operations “until further notice”, adding radar and communications equipment was damaged and runways needed to be assessed.

Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath.

“People who were in Terminal 3 started running towards us,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP.

“Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood.”

The attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said.

The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport, while Australia urged its citizens on Sunday to stay indoors altogether and “shelter in place”.

The Houthis also claimed to have targeted the Dammam airport, whose official website on Sunday showed many flights — both departures and arrivals — were delayed.

‘Rewrite the rules’

Saturday’s airport strike, on the eve of Saudi Arabia’s high-profile convention and entertainment season, was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since a 2015 suicide bombing.

With the summer heat subsiding, October also usually marks the beginning of the high season for Umrah pilgrims, with millions of Muslims from across the world flocking to Makkah.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to rewrite the rules of the game”.

“They want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them,” he said.

“So if their airport in Sanaa has to be closed because of the Saudi air embargo, they want to do the same thing to Saudi Arabia.”

On the ground in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said on Saturday.

The Houthis claimed to have repelled them.

Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

World.title: Fazl accuses govt of reneging on its commitments after seeking his mediation with PTI
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman — who was being cast as the man who could defuse tensions between the Centre and the PTI until Sunday — has accused the government of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts for mediating between the two parties.

Both sides held separate meetings with Fazl ahead of their political tensions culminating into the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where the PTI was in power.

Addressing a press conference on Sunday, Fazl shared details of his engagement with both sides at a press conference held at his residence in Islamabad following an emergency meeting of the party’s Central Core Committee.

He said he returned from Umrah on Oct 7, after which opposition leaders approached him and asked him to play a role in resolving the political impasse.

The following day, he continued, federal ministers also visited him and sought his intervention.

Tensions between the two sides had risen since the PTI announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. An impasse had emerged after talks between the two sides failed to yield any positive outcomes last week, following which the PTI began its march but remained within KP.

Meanwhile, several federal ministers spoke about the possibility of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, linking it with the province’s security situation and the PTI’s alleged non-cooperation on counterterrorism.

At the press conference on Sunday, Fazl said the PTI’s march had avoided entering Islamabad at his request and the government’s plan to impose emergency was deferred after its delegation approached him.

“Subsequently, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif invited me to the Prime Minister House for a meeting. Although I felt the government had already made up its mind, my colleagues advised me to meet the prime minister,” he said.

He said the government had insisted that the long march be called off first while the PTI demanded that its leaders be allowed to meet Imran in jail and court order regarding his transfer to a private hospital be implemented.

Both sides were insisting that the other should take the first step, Fazl recalled.

“I asked both sides to authorise me to act as a mediator and make decisions to move the process forward,” he said, adding that he also wanted to take now dysfunctional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi into confidence.

He said he held a conference call with Afridi, PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and PTI leader Asad Qaiser, among others.

Fazl said that during the conversation, he asked the KP chief minister whether the PTI was willing to end its long march if its demands were accepted.

“Sohail Afridi said that if the demands were accepted, they would call off the long march.”

Fazl said he had also visited the Prime Minister House and informed him that the PTI was ready to end its march if its demands were met.

“I asked the prime minister to give an assurance that the PTI would be allowed to meet Imran Khan, and Imran Khan will receive the required medical treatment,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said also intended to travel to Peshawar to hold further discussions with Afridi and other stakeholders, and that he wanted to involve two representatives each from the PTI and the PML-N in the negotiations under his “supervision to advance the process”.

However, he said, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called him during the cabinet meeting on Sunday and informed him that the government wanted to impose an emergency in KP because of the security situation.

“I questioned the rationale behind the proposed measure, pointing out that the security situation in Balochistan was worse than in KP, yet the government had not imposed governor’s rule there.”

Fazl then accused the government of reneging on its commitments despite agreeing to a proposed course of action, saying he had questioned Dar about the purpose of seeking his mediation if the cabinet intended to make its own decision.

“I asked Dar why I was asked to mediate if the cabinet was going to make the decision on its own,” he said.

Asked whether politicians were responsible for the failure of negotiations, the JUI-F chief said the question should be put to the prime minister.

“Ask Shehbaz Sharif how much authority he had during the negotiations,” he said. He further alleged that the government had created obstacles in the way of negotiations.

‘Attack on democracy’

Fazl also rejected the government’s move to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, terming it an “attack on democracy and the rights of the people”.

“We reject the entire decision, word for word,” he said.

The JUI-F chief said his party would challenge the decision through all available democratic and constitutional forums, including Parliament and the courts.

“We will defend the Constitution, human rights and democratic rights in this country through constitutional and democratic platforms available to us,” he said. “We are not prepared to bow, even for a moment, before such unconstitutional measures.”

He also regretted the PPP’s role in matter, describing it as one that undermined the Constitution and democracy.

Reiterating that “we stand firmly with the Constitution of Pakistan”, he went on to refer to military operations over the year, beginning from the tenure of former military ruler retired General Pervez Musharraf to the present day. This strategy had repeatedly failed, he said.

Responding to a question about the provincial government’s performance in KP, Fazl said that if the KP government had failed, the situation in Balochistan was worse.

Asked if the opposition would resign from the assemblies, Fazl said the decision would be considered when the situation arose.

World.title: Authorities impose Section 144 in Karachi, ban gatherings of more than 5 people till Oct 20
World.content:
KARACHI: The Karachi commissioner on Sunday imposed Section 144 in the metropolis till Oct 20 to prevent protests and demonstrations from inconveniencing the public and causing a “deterioration of the law and order situation”.

Section 144 is a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) which empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons.

The notification, issued by Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi, said that it had been reported that protests, demonstrations, sit-ins and rallies were being held on major roads, junctions and roundabouts, causing severe traffic congestion and posing “serious security concerns”.

“Such road blockages are disrupting routine public life, impeding the movement of emergency services and restricting access to hospitals. Accordingly, it has been requested that a ban under Section 144 of the CrPC be imposed on protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies and assemblies of more than five persons within the territorial limits of Karachi Division,” it said.

The notification said that there was “reasonable apprehension” that the holding, organising or facilitating of such gatherings, rallies, protests, demonstrations, processions and assemblies may “obstruct public roads and thoroughfares, disrupt normal civic and commercial activities, cause inconvenience to the general public and traffic congestion, impede access to hospitals, and result in untoward incidents and the deterioration of the law and order situation”.

It said that it was considered “necessary and expedient” to impose preventive restrictions for a specified period to avert any possible untoward incident, maintain public peace and tranquillity, safeguard the lives and property of citizens, ensure public safety and security, and facilitate the uninterrupted movement of the general public and essential services.

Therefore, the Karachi commissioner prohibited holding, organising, convening, facilitating or participating in protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies, processions or other public gatherings involving more than five persons from Oct 11 (Sunday) to Oct 20.

World.title: Maaz Sadaqat, Imran Randhawa star as Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka in second T20I to seal series
World.content:
Maaz Sadaqat hit a blistering 96 before Imran Randhawa’s miserly spell helped Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka by 82 runs in the second Twenty20 International and seal the three-match series for the hosts here at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday.

Both Maaz and Imran were able to make a match-winning impact in what was only their second T20I outing after making their debuts in Friday’s opening match.

While Maaz — who had hit a crucial half-century on debut — went on to showcase the more belligerent side of his potential, Imran justified his selection with precision bowling that kept Sri Lanka from getting into the game at any point during the chase.

After Pakistan were restricted to 46 in the powerplay, Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz transformed the innings with a commanding 88-run partnership for the second wicket. Farhan, who survived a couple of reprieves, led the recovery with a fluent 73 off 44 balls, striking four fours and five sixes, while Maaz provided the acceleration that ultimately carried Pakistan to their highest T20I total on home soil.

Fakhar Zaman had contributed 22 off 17 balls before falling to Maheesh Theekshana in the seventh over, but Maaz initially took time to settle after his arrival. He survived a leading edge that fell short of cover and was dropped by Nuwan Thushara off his own bowling on 44, before making Sri Lanka pay dearly for their lapses.

The left-hander brought up his half-century off 29 balls with a towering six over long-off against Theekshana in the 15th over. What followed was a remarkable exhibition of power-hitting as Maaz plundered 22 runs from the spinner’s final over, striking three sixes to take Pakistan past 165.

He continued to dismantle the bowling attack, using his feet against the pacers and finding boundaries on both sides of the wicket. His audacious scoop, reverse paddle and clean strikes over the ropes left Sri Lanka struggling for answers as Pakistan surged towards 200.

Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat convene during their partnership during the second Twenty20 International against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 11, 2026.—AFP

Farhan, meanwhile, brought up his half-century off 32 balls and continued to attack before Dasun Shanaka finally dismissed him in the 15th over, caught at deep third for 73. Maaz then took charge alongside Hasan Nawaz, who struck an unbeaten 19 off nine deliveries, as Pakistan collected 49 runs across the final three overs before the last.

Maaz reached 96 off just 51 balls, with six fours and seven sixes, but his maiden T20I century remained agonisingly out of reach. Attempting to slice Eshan Malinga behind point off the final delivery, he found Shanaka at deep cover instead. Pakistan nevertheless finished on 215-3, setting Sri Lanka a daunting target of 216.

Sri Lanka’s reply unravelled almost immediately. Salman Mirza, returning to international cricket after injury, removed Lahiru Udara for five in the opening over, before Imran struck to dismiss Sineth Jayawardena for 22 at the end of the powerplay.

Imran then delivered the decisive blows in the eighth over, removing captain Kusal Mendis for nine and Sahan Arachchige for a duck off successive deliveries, with wicket-keeper Khawaja Nafay taking two sharp catches. His figures improved to 3-9 after three overs, leaving Sri Lanka reeling at 49-4.

The 29-year-old completed an outstanding spell of four overs for just 11 runs and three wickets, conceding only five runs in his first two overs. Dasun Shanaka fell to Saim Ayub for nine, while Shadab Khan dismissed Kamindu Mendis for 23 to leave the visitors at 74-6.

Chamindu Wickramasinghe and Maheesh Theekshana offered some resistance with a seventh-wicket stand of 50, but the required rate had climbed beyond reach. Chamindu made 29 before falling to Salman Mirza, who finished with two wickets, while Theekshana remained unbeaten on 32 off 26 balls.

Pakistan’s Imran Randhawa (L) and Fakhar Zaman (R) celebrate during the second Twenty20 International against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 11, 2026.—AFP

Sri Lanka closed on 133-7, handing Pakistan an emphatic 82-run victory and an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series ahead of Tuesday’s final match.

Farhan, celebrating his first series victory as Pakistan captain, praised his side’s improved six-hitting and attacking intent, while Sri Lanka skipper Mendis admitted his batters needed to take greater responsibility on a surface suited to stroke-making.

Maaz was named player of the match for his explosive innings, but Imran’s disciplined spell ensured that Pakistan’s outstanding batting display translated into a series-clinching victory.

World.title: 'Our fight is against terrorism': Kundi chairs first meeting of KP Advisory Council
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday chaired the first meeting of the KP Advisory Council, which was formed by the federal government following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

At the outset of the meeting, all members of the council introduced themselves and their portfolios.

Addressing the meeting, Kundi congratulated the members of the council, while noting that they would have to face many challenges. He said that they would get a briefing on the portfolios they had been assigned and would get a few days to familiarise themselves.

“We have to fast-track things. There will be zero tolerance on corruption. Things should be done in a timely manner,” he said, adding that they would have to demonstrate a clear difference from the work done by their predecessors.

He said that the first order of business was the law and order situation, adding that there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces.

He said that the current situation was an “opportunity” as he called for building the province’s soft image.

“If we have peace, we will get tourists and investors. My support is with you. I am available for you 24/7,” he said.

Kundi then went on to read out a message for the people of the province, in which he said that due to “extraordinary circumstances”, “necessary measures” were taken under the Constitution.

He said that he would refrain from levelling allegations and political rhetoric.

“I have one message: peace, protection and stability have to be brought back to KP,” he said. He added that the people of KP had paid a huge price for the terrorism that plagued the province.

“The time has now come to give the people of the province, who have rendered these sacrifices, the right to peace. Our fight is against terrorism. Our fight is against the ideology and network which facilitates terrorism and weakens the implementation of the law,” he said.

He also said that Pakhtuns were not a cause of terrorism, but were the “biggest victims”. Therefore, the state had resolved that terrorism would be eliminated from KP and the people would be allowed to live their lives without fear.

“My first priority will be protecting the peace and the people. Right now, our biggest priority is taking effective steps against terrorism. For this, the capacity of the police and the Counter Terrorism Department will be increased,” he said.

He went on to say that another objective would be to cater to the people.

“Mere statements are not the real test of a government, rather the service it provides to the people,” he said. Kundi said that the council would focus on healthcare, education and employment.

The last objective, he said, would be to eliminate the whole ecosystem giving rise to terrorism in the province.

“We cannot solve the issue by just targeting terrorists. Those facilitating and financing … must be eliminated,” he said, adding that those involved in terrorism would be dealt with according to the law.

He assured the people of KP that the “extraordinary steps” taken were not meant to target a particular party or group. Kundi said that the main purpose was to ensure peace and security as he asked for their cooperation.

Security situation reviewed

Separately, Kundi chaired a high-level meeting regarding the security situation in the province, during which he was briefed in detail on the overall situation, counter-terrorism efforts and the current circumstances.

According to a handout, it was decided during the meeting that all containers currently placed in Peshawar will be removed in phases “as soon as possible”.

“Internet services will be partially restored based on necessity,” the statement added.

It was also decided during the meeting to enhance the compensation package for martyred police personnel and to review police salaries, as well as to pay “special attention” to the education and training of the heirs of martyred personnel.

The governor commended the role of the administration and the police, remarking that it was a “positive development” that no untoward incident had occurred amid the prevailing circumstances, the handout said.

He added that eradicating terrorism was a “top priority” and that the operational capacity of the police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) would be further improved to achieve this goal.

“The meeting was attended by Advisor on Home Affairs Kifayatullah Khan, Chief Secretary Dr Muhammad Fakhr-e-Alam Irfan, Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed, Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Amjad Ali Khan, Additional IG Special Branch Muhammad Kashif Alam, Additional IG CTD, CCPO Dr Mian Saeed, Joint Director General IB Arshad Ali Khan, and other relevant officials,” the statement added.

World.title: TTAP condemns imposition of governor’s rule, emergency in KP, calls move 'unconstitutional'
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Sunday condemned the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terming the move unconstitutional and contrary to democratic principles.

It announced that it would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums. It also said the long march would go ahead as planned.

Addressing a press conference, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said governor’s rule and an emergency would not resolve the province’s problems, stressing that counterterrorism efforts required a unified strategy developed through political consensus.

He rejected allegations that the KP government had failed to cooperate with the federal government in tackling terrorism, saying the provincial administration remained committed to eliminating the menace.

“If the problem of terrorism exists in 12 districts, why has governor’s rule been imposed across the province?” he asked.

Gohar said the PTI had consistently condemned terrorism in all its forms and maintained that the country’s security and defence remained paramount. However, he argued that counterterrorism measures should not be used to justify action against his party.

He said the PTI would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums, adding that the party’s struggle for constitutional and democratic rights would continue.

The PTI chairman also called for the release of political prisoners and the restoration of the legal rights of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. He demanded that Imran be transferred to a hospital for treatment, that his family be allowed to meet him, and that details of his health and treatment be shared with them.

Gohar said the party had approached the Supreme Court and high courts 19 times seeking relief for its incarcerated founder. He said the announcement of a long march for Aug 5 had been made to secure Imran’s rights after the party failed to obtain relief through the courts.

He claimed that around 1,500 PTI workers were imprisoned in Punjab, while 10 members of the provincial assembly, including three ministers, and eight members of the National Assembly had also been arrested.

The PTI chairman rejected the government’s narrative about his party, arguing that political action against the PTI should not be linked to efforts to eliminate terrorism.

He further claimed that terrorism had not been discussed during 15 meetings with government representatives before Oct 2. He said the KP government had increased police capacity, provided security resources and participated in counterterrorism meetings.

Gohar said federal interference had weakened the provincial government’s authority, adding that sidelining an elected chief minister was inconsistent with democratic principles.

Consensus needed on counterterrorism

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the party had consistently called for a mutually agreed strategy to address terrorism, arguing that decisions on security operations should be taken in consultation with all political parties.

Referring to the Parachinar agreement, he said the party’s position had remained clear and that it was seeking the implementation of previously agreed decisions rather than the introduction of new conditions.

He said the party had cited the February 2026 meeting of the Apex Committee and a resolution adopted at a peace jirga as the basis for moving forward.

Raja said Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had taken a clear position and that the provincial government could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to undertake whatever measures it considered appropriate.

“We cannot give anyone written permission to do whatever they want and then endorse it,” he said.

He added that any decision concerning governor’s rule or an emergency must be made in accordance with constitutional principles and political consensus.

Raja said negotiations had involved consultations with Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, while Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other political leaders had been trying to ensure the process succeeded.

He claimed that the talks had been progressing satisfactorily and that the imposition of an emergency was a hasty decision. He also cited Senator Kamran Murtaza as saying that negotiations were moving in the right direction.

The TTAP leader described the arrest of a provincial assembly speaker as an extraordinary step, adding that the assembly remained in existence.

Despite what he described as a crackdown on the PTI, Raja said the party remained committed to its principles and was seeking peace and protection for innocent people.

He confirmed that there had been no change to the announcement of the long march by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying peaceful protest was a fundamental constitutional right.

“We will not throw stones. Through peaceful protest, we have to express our moral position,” he said, adding that a large-scale, peaceful demonstration by citizens across the country would convey a strong message.

He said people would decide how to express their displeasure over what he described as actions against democracy, while distinguishing between political protest and revolutionary action.

National Action Plan must be implemented

Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said Pakistan was a federation whose provinces were united under a single Constitution, and criticised the treatment meted out to the PTI.

He claimed that Imran had received the majority of public support in the elections and alleged that the ruling establishment feared the public mandate and had continuously targeted the PTI.

Abbas blamed the government for the prevailing insecurity, saying the conduct of those in power had caused greater damage than the country’s external enemies could inflict.

He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) and said the seven days since the start of negotiations could have been used to make progress towards a political settlement.

Abbas further said the party could not support military operations in which ordinary citizens became victims, stressing that counterterrorism measures must protect civilians and contribute to lasting peace.

The press conference was held at an imambargah in Islamabad’s Bhara Kahu as the KP House, where the alliance would typically hold press conferences had been sealed.

Speaking to Dawn, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai said that after deciding to hold a press conference, the alliance initially thought to go to KP House, but came to know that it had been sealed. He added that they then decided to hold it at the National Press Club (NPC), but were refused by the club despite being willing to pay the fee.

“Then we have decided to hold the presser at Bhara Kahu,” he said.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni
